metadata.title: Podcast: Stuart Russell: Long-Term Future of Artificial Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #9

body.input: And that actually resembles the real world

metadata.title: Podcast: Stuart Russell: Long-Term Future of Artificial Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #9

body.input: much more than chess does.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stuart Russell: Long-Term Future of Artificial Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #9

body.input: Because in the real world, we have work, we have home life,

metadata.title: Podcast: Stuart Russell: Long-Term Future of Artificial Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #9

body.input: we have sport, whatever, different kinds of activities,

metadata.title: Podcast: Stuart Russell: Long-Term Future of Artificial Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #9

body.input: shopping, these all are connected to each other,

metadata.title: Podcast: Stuart Russell: Long-Term Future of Artificial Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #9

body.input: but they're weakly connected.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stuart Russell: Long-Term Future of Artificial Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #9

body.input: So when I'm typing a paper,

metadata.title: Podcast: Stuart Russell: Long-Term Future of Artificial Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #9

body.input: I don't simultaneously have to decide which order

metadata.title: Podcast: Stuart Russell: Long-Term Future of Artificial Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #9

body.input: I'm gonna get the milk and the butter,

metadata.title: Podcast: Stuart Russell: Long-Term Future of Artificial Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #9

body.input: that doesn't affect the typing.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stuart Russell: Long-Term Future of Artificial Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #9

body.input: But I do need to realize, okay, I better finish this

metadata.title: Podcast: Stuart Russell: Long-Term Future of Artificial Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #9

body.input: before the shops close,

metadata.title: Podcast: Stuart Russell: Long-Term Future of Artificial Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #9

body.input: because I don't have any food at home.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stuart Russell: Long-Term Future of Artificial Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #9

body.input: So there's some weak connection,

metadata.title: Podcast: Stuart Russell: Long-Term Future of Artificial Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #9

body.input: but not in the way that chess works,

metadata.title: Podcast: Stuart Russell: Long-Term Future of Artificial Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #9

body.input: where everything is tied into a single stream of thought.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stuart Russell: Long-Term Future of Artificial Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #9

body.input: So the thought was that to solve Go,

metadata.title: Podcast: Stuart Russell: Long-Term Future of Artificial Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #9

body.input: we'd have to make progress on stuff

metadata.title: Podcast: Stuart Russell: Long-Term Future of Artificial Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #9

body.input: that would be useful for the real world.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stuart Russell: Long-Term Future of Artificial Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #9

body.input: And in a way, AlphaGo is a little bit disappointing,

metadata.title: Podcast: Stuart Russell: Long-Term Future of Artificial Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #9

body.input: because the program design for AlphaGo

metadata.title: Podcast: Stuart Russell: Long-Term Future of Artificial Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #9

body.input: was actually not that different from Deep Blue,

metadata.title: Podcast: Stuart Russell: Long-Term Future of Artificial Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #9

body.input: or even from Alfred Samuel's checker playing program

metadata.title: Podcast: Stuart Russell: Long-Term Future of Artificial Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #9

body.input: from the 1950s.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stuart Russell: Long-Term Future of Artificial Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #9

body.input: And in fact, the two things that make AlphaGo work,

metadata.title: Podcast: Stuart Russell: Long-Term Future of Artificial Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #9

body.input: one is this amazing ability to evaluate the positions,

metadata.title: Podcast: Stuart Russell: Long-Term Future of Artificial Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #9

body.input: and the other is the meta reasoning capability,

metadata.title: Podcast: Stuart Russell: Long-Term Future of Artificial Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #9

body.input: which allows it to explore some paths in the tree very deeply,

metadata.title: Podcast: Stuart Russell: Long-Term Future of Artificial Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #9

body.input: and to abandon other paths very quickly.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stuart Russell: Long-Term Future of Artificial Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #9

body.input: So this word meta reasoning, while technically correct,

metadata.title: Podcast: Stuart Russell: Long-Term Future of Artificial Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #9

body.input: inspires perhaps the wrong degree of power

metadata.title: Podcast: Stuart Russell: Long-Term Future of Artificial Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #9

body.input: that AlphaGo has, for example.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stuart Russell: Long-Term Future of Artificial Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #9

body.input: The word reasoning is a powerful word.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stuart Russell: Long-Term Future of Artificial Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #9

body.input: So let me ask you, sort of,

metadata.title: Podcast: Stuart Russell: Long-Term Future of Artificial Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #9

body.input: you were part of the symbolic AI world for a while,

metadata.title: Podcast: Stuart Russell: Long-Term Future of Artificial Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #9

body.input: like where AI was,

metadata.title: Podcast: Stuart Russell: Long-Term Future of Artificial Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #9

body.input: there's a lot of excellent, interesting ideas there.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stuart Russell: Long-Term Future of Artificial Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #9

body.input: That unfortunately met a winter.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stuart Russell: Long-Term Future of Artificial Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #9

body.input: And so do you think it re-emerges?

metadata.title: Podcast: Stuart Russell: Long-Term Future of Artificial Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #9

body.input: So I would say, yeah, it's not quite as simple as that.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stuart Russell: Long-Term Future of Artificial Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #9

body.input: So the AI winter, the first winter

metadata.title: Podcast: Stuart Russell: Long-Term Future of Artificial Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #9

body.input: that was actually named as such was the one in the late 80s.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stuart Russell: Long-Term Future of Artificial Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #9

body.input: And that came about because in the mid 80s,

metadata.title: Podcast: Stuart Russell: Long-Term Future of Artificial Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #9

body.input: there was really a concerted attempt to push AI

metadata.title: Podcast: Stuart Russell: Long-Term Future of Artificial Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #9

body.input: out into the real world,

metadata.title: Podcast: Stuart Russell: Long-Term Future of Artificial Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #9

body.input: using what was called expert system technology.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stuart Russell: Long-Term Future of Artificial Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #9

body.input: And for the most part,

metadata.title: Podcast: Stuart Russell: Long-Term Future of Artificial Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #9

body.input: that technology was just not ready for prime time.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stuart Russell: Long-Term Future of Artificial Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #9

body.input: They were trying in many cases

metadata.title: Podcast: Stuart Russell: Long-Term Future of Artificial Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #9

body.input: to do a form of uncertain reasoning,

metadata.title: Podcast: Stuart Russell: Long-Term Future of Artificial Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #9

body.input: judgment, combinations of evidence, diagnosis,

metadata.title: Podcast: Stuart Russell: Long-Term Future of Artificial Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #9

body.input: those kinds of things.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stuart Russell: Long-Term Future of Artificial Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #9

body.input: Which was simply invalid.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stuart Russell: Long-Term Future of Artificial Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #9

body.input: And when you try to apply invalid reasoning methods

metadata.title: Podcast: Stuart Russell: Long-Term Future of Artificial Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #9

body.input: to real problems,

metadata.title: Podcast: Stuart Russell: Long-Term Future of Artificial Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #9

body.input: you can fudge it for small versions of the problem,

metadata.title: Podcast: Stuart Russell: Long-Term Future of Artificial Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #9

body.input: but when it starts to get larger,

metadata.title: Podcast: Stuart Russell: Long-Term Future of Artificial Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #9

body.input: the thing just falls apart.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stuart Russell: Long-Term Future of Artificial Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #9

body.input: So many companies found that the stuff just didn't work

metadata.title: Podcast: Stuart Russell: Long-Term Future of Artificial Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #9

body.input: and they were spending tons of money on consultants

metadata.title: Podcast: Stuart Russell: Long-Term Future of Artificial Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #9

body.input: to try to make it work.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stuart Russell: Long-Term Future of Artificial Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #9

body.input: And there were other practical reasons,

metadata.title: Podcast: Stuart Russell: Long-Term Future of Artificial Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #9

body.input: like they were asking the companies

metadata.title: Podcast: Stuart Russell: Long-Term Future of Artificial Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #9

body.input: to buy incredibly expensive Lisp machine workstations,

metadata.title: Podcast: Stuart Russell: Long-Term Future of Artificial Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #9

body.input: which were literally between 50 and $100,000 in 1980s money,

metadata.title: Podcast: Stuart Russell: Long-Term Future of Artificial Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #9

body.input: which would be like between 150 and $300,000 per workstation

metadata.title: Podcast: Stuart Russell: Long-Term Future of Artificial Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #9

body.input: in current prices.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stuart Russell: Long-Term Future of Artificial Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #9

body.input: And then the bottom line, they weren't seeing a profit from it.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stuart Russell: Long-Term Future of Artificial Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #9

body.input: Yeah, in many cases.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stuart Russell: Long-Term Future of Artificial Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #9

body.input: I think there were some successes.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stuart Russell: Long-Term Future of Artificial Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #9

body.input: There's no doubt about that.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stuart Russell: Long-Term Future of Artificial Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #9

body.input: But people, I would say, over-invested.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stuart Russell: Long-Term Future of Artificial Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #9

body.input: Every major company was starting an AI department, just like now.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stuart Russell: Long-Term Future of Artificial Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #9

body.input: And I worry a bit that we might see similar disappointments.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stuart Russell: Long-Term Future of Artificial Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #9

body.input: Not because the current technology is invalid,

metadata.title: Podcast: Stuart Russell: Long-Term Future of Artificial Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #9

body.input: but it's limited in its scope.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stuart Russell: Long-Term Future of Artificial Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #9

body.input: And it's almost the dual of the scope problems

metadata.title: Podcast: Stuart Russell: Long-Term Future of Artificial Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #9

body.input: that expert systems had.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stuart Russell: Long-Term Future of Artificial Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #9

body.input: What have you learned from that hype cycle

metadata.title: Podcast: Stuart Russell: Long-Term Future of Artificial Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #9

body.input: and what can we do to prevent another winter, for example?

metadata.title: Podcast: Stuart Russell: Long-Term Future of Artificial Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #9

body.input: Yeah, so when I'm giving talks these days,

metadata.title: Podcast: Stuart Russell: Long-Term Future of Artificial Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #9

body.input: that's one of the warnings that I give.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stuart Russell: Long-Term Future of Artificial Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #9

body.input: So this is a two-part warning slide.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stuart Russell: Long-Term Future of Artificial Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #9

body.input: One is that rather than data being the new oil,

metadata.title: Podcast: Stuart Russell: Long-Term Future of Artificial Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #9

body.input: data is the new snake oil.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stuart Russell: Long-Term Future of Artificial Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #9

body.input: That's a good line.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stuart Russell: Long-Term Future of Artificial Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #9

body.input: And then the other is that we might see a very visible failure

metadata.title: Podcast: Stuart Russell: Long-Term Future of Artificial Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #9

body.input: in some of the major application areas.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stuart Russell: Long-Term Future of Artificial Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #9

body.input: And I think self-driving cars would be the flagship.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stuart Russell: Long-Term Future of Artificial Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #9

body.input: And I think when you look at the history,

metadata.title: Podcast: Stuart Russell: Long-Term Future of Artificial Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #9

body.input: so the first self-driving car was on the freeway,

metadata.title: Podcast: Stuart Russell: Long-Term Future of Artificial Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #9

body.input: driving itself, changing lanes, overtaking in 1987.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stuart Russell: Long-Term Future of Artificial Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #9

body.input: And so it's more than 30 years.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stuart Russell: Long-Term Future of Artificial Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #9

body.input: And that kind of looks like where we are today, right?

metadata.title: Podcast: Stuart Russell: Long-Term Future of Artificial Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #9

body.input: Prototypes on the freeway, changing lanes and overtaking.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stuart Russell: Long-Term Future of Artificial Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #9

body.input: Now, I think significant progress has been made,

metadata.title: Podcast: Stuart Russell: Long-Term Future of Artificial Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #9

body.input: particularly on the perception side.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stuart Russell: Long-Term Future of Artificial Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #9

body.input: So we worked a lot on autonomous vehicles

metadata.title: Podcast: Stuart Russell: Long-Term Future of Artificial Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #9

body.input: in the early mid-'90s at Berkeley.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stuart Russell: Long-Term Future of Artificial Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #9

body.input: And we had our own big demonstrations.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stuart Russell: Long-Term Future of Artificial Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #9

body.input: We put congressmen into self-driving cars

metadata.title: Podcast: Stuart Russell: Long-Term Future of Artificial Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #9

body.input: and had them zooming along the freeway.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stuart Russell: Long-Term Future of Artificial Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #9

body.input: And the problem was clearly perception.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stuart Russell: Long-Term Future of Artificial Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #9

body.input: At the time, the problem was perception.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stuart Russell: Long-Term Future of Artificial Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #9

body.input: Yeah, so in simulation with perfect perception,

metadata.title: Podcast: Stuart Russell: Long-Term Future of Artificial Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #9

body.input: you could actually show that you can drive safely for a long time,

metadata.title: Podcast: Stuart Russell: Long-Term Future of Artificial Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #9

body.input: even if the other car is misbehaving and so on.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stuart Russell: Long-Term Future of Artificial Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #9

body.input: But simultaneously, we worked on machine vision

metadata.title: Podcast: Stuart Russell: Long-Term Future of Artificial Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #9

body.input: for detecting cars and tracking pedestrians and so on.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stuart Russell: Long-Term Future of Artificial Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #9

body.input: And we couldn't get the reliability of detection and tracking

metadata.title: Podcast: Stuart Russell: Long-Term Future of Artificial Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #9

body.input: up to a high enough level,

metadata.title: Podcast: Stuart Russell: Long-Term Future of Artificial Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #9

body.input: particularly in bad weather conditions, nighttime rain, fog.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stuart Russell: Long-Term Future of Artificial Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #9

body.input: Good enough for demos, but perhaps not good enough to cover the general operation.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stuart Russell: Long-Term Future of Artificial Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #9

body.input: Yeah, so the thing about driving is, suppose you're a taxi driver

metadata.title: Podcast: Stuart Russell: Long-Term Future of Artificial Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #9

body.input: and you drive every day, eight hours a day for 10 years, right?

metadata.title: Podcast: Stuart Russell: Long-Term Future of Artificial Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #9

body.input: That's 100 million seconds of driving.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stuart Russell: Long-Term Future of Artificial Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #9

body.input: And any one of those seconds, you can make a fatal mistake.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stuart Russell: Long-Term Future of Artificial Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #9

body.input: So you're talking about eight nines of reliability, right?

metadata.title: Podcast: Stuart Russell: Long-Term Future of Artificial Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #9

body.input: Now, if your vision system only detects 98.3% of the vehicles,

metadata.title: Podcast: Stuart Russell: Long-Term Future of Artificial Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #9

body.input: then that's sort of one in a bit nines of reliability.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stuart Russell: Long-Term Future of Artificial Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #9

body.input: So you have another seven orders of magnitude to go.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stuart Russell: Long-Term Future of Artificial Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #9

body.input: And this is what people don't understand.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stuart Russell: Long-Term Future of Artificial Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #9

body.input: They think, oh, because I had a successful demo, I'm pretty much done.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stuart Russell: Long-Term Future of Artificial Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #9

body.input: But you're not even within seven orders of magnitude of being done.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stuart Russell: Long-Term Future of Artificial Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #9

body.input: And that's the difficulty.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stuart Russell: Long-Term Future of Artificial Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #9

body.input: And it's not the, can I follow a white line?

metadata.title: Podcast: Stuart Russell: Long-Term Future of Artificial Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #9

body.input: That's not the problem, right?

metadata.title: Podcast: Stuart Russell: Long-Term Future of Artificial Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #9

body.input: We follow a white line all the way across the country.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stuart Russell: Long-Term Future of Artificial Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #9

body.input: But it's the weird stuff that happens.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stuart Russell: Long-Term Future of Artificial Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #9

body.input: It's on the edge cases, yeah.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stuart Russell: Long-Term Future of Artificial Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #9

body.input: The edge case, other drivers doing weird things.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stuart Russell: Long-Term Future of Artificial Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #9

body.input: So if you talk to Google, right?

metadata.title: Podcast: Stuart Russell: Long-Term Future of Artificial Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #9

body.input: So they had actually a very classical architecture where you had machine vision,

metadata.title: Podcast: Stuart Russell: Long-Term Future of Artificial Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #9

body.input: which would detect all the other cars and pedestrians and the white lines and the road signs.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stuart Russell: Long-Term Future of Artificial Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #9

body.input: And then basically that was fed into a logical database.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stuart Russell: Long-Term Future of Artificial Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #9

body.input: And then you had a classical 1970s rule-based expert system telling you,

metadata.title: Podcast: Stuart Russell: Long-Term Future of Artificial Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #9

body.input: if you're in the middle lane and there's a bicyclist in the right lane who is signaling this,

metadata.title: Podcast: Stuart Russell: Long-Term Future of Artificial Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #9

body.input: then you need to do that, right?

metadata.title: Podcast: Stuart Russell: Long-Term Future of Artificial Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #9

body.input: And what they found was that every day they'd go out and there'd be another situation that the rules didn't cover.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stuart Russell: Long-Term Future of Artificial Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #9

body.input: So they'd come to a traffic circle and there's a little girl riding her bicycle the wrong way around the traffic circle.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stuart Russell: Long-Term Future of Artificial Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #9

body.input: What do you do? We don't have a rule. Oh my God. Okay, stop.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stuart Russell: Long-Term Future of Artificial Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #9

body.input: And then they'd come back and add more rules.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stuart Russell: Long-Term Future of Artificial Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #9

body.input: And they just found that this was not really converging.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stuart Russell: Long-Term Future of Artificial Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #9

body.input: And if you think about it, right, how do you deal with an unexpected situation,

metadata.title: Podcast: Stuart Russell: Long-Term Future of Artificial Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #9

body.input: meaning one that you've never previously encountered and the sort of the reasoning required to figure out the solution for that situation has never been done.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stuart Russell: Long-Term Future of Artificial Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #9

body.input: It doesn't match any previous situation in terms of the kind of reasoning you have to do.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stuart Russell: Long-Term Future of Artificial Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #9

body.input: Well, you know, in chess programs, this happens all the time.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stuart Russell: Long-Term Future of Artificial Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #9

body.input: You're constantly coming up with situations you haven't seen before and you have to reason about them.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stuart Russell: Long-Term Future of Artificial Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #9

body.input: And you have to think about, okay, here are the possible things I could do.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stuart Russell: Long-Term Future of Artificial Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #9

body.input: Here are the outcomes. Here's how desirable the outcomes are.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stuart Russell: Long-Term Future of Artificial Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #9

body.input: And then pick the right one.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stuart Russell: Long-Term Future of Artificial Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #9

body.input: You know, in the 90s, we were saying, okay, this is how you're going to have to do automated vehicles.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stuart Russell: Long-Term Future of Artificial Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #9

body.input: They're going to have to have a look ahead capability.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stuart Russell: Long-Term Future of Artificial Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #9

body.input: But the look ahead for driving is more difficult than it is for chess because the other right.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stuart Russell: Long-Term Future of Artificial Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #9

body.input: There's humans and they are less predictable than chess pieces.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stuart Russell: Long-Term Future of Artificial Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #9

body.input: Well, then you have an opponent in chess who's also somewhat unpredictable.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stuart Russell: Long-Term Future of Artificial Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #9

body.input: But for example, in chess, you always know the opponent's intention.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stuart Russell: Long-Term Future of Artificial Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #9

body.input: They're trying to beat you, right?

metadata.title: Podcast: Stuart Russell: Long-Term Future of Artificial Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #9

body.input: Whereas in driving, you don't know, is this guy trying to turn left or has he just forgotten to turn off his turn signal or is he drunk or is he changing the channel on his radio or whatever it might be.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stuart Russell: Long-Term Future of Artificial Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #9

body.input: You've got to try and figure out the mental state, the intent of the other drivers to forecast the possible evolutions of their trajectories.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stuart Russell: Long-Term Future of Artificial Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #9

body.input: And then you've got to figure out, okay, which is the trajectory for me that's going to be safest.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stuart Russell: Long-Term Future of Artificial Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #9

body.input: And those all interact with each other because the other driver is going to react to your trajectory and so on.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stuart Russell: Long-Term Future of Artificial Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #9

body.input: So, you know, you've got the classic merging onto the freeway problem where you're kind of racing a vehicle that's already on the freeway and you're going to pull ahead of them or you're going to let them go first and pull in behind.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stuart Russell: Long-Term Future of Artificial Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #9

body.input: And you get this sort of uncertainty about who's going first.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stuart Russell: Long-Term Future of Artificial Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #9

body.input: So all those kinds of things mean that you need decision-making architecture that's very different from either a rule-based system or it seems to me kind of an end-to-end neural network system.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stuart Russell: Long-Term Future of Artificial Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #9

body.input: You know, so just as AlphaGo is pretty good when it doesn't do any look ahead, but it's way, way, way, way better when it does.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stuart Russell: Long-Term Future of Artificial Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #9

body.input: I think the same is going to be true for driving. You can have a driving system that's pretty good when it doesn't do any look ahead, but that's not good enough.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stuart Russell: Long-Term Future of Artificial Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #9

body.input: You know, and we've already seen multiple deaths caused by poorly designed machine learning algorithms that don't really understand what they're doing.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stuart Russell: Long-Term Future of Artificial Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #9

body.input: Yeah, on several levels, I think on the perception side, there's mistakes being made by those algorithms where the perception is very shallow on the planning side, the look ahead, like you said.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stuart Russell: Long-Term Future of Artificial Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #9

body.input: And the thing that we come up against that's really interesting when you try to deploy systems in the real world is you can't think of an artificial intelligence system as a thing that responds to the world always.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stuart Russell: Long-Term Future of Artificial Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #9

body.input: You have to realize that it's an agent that others will respond to as well. So in order to drive successfully, you can't just try to do obstacle avoidance.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stuart Russell: Long-Term Future of Artificial Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #9

body.input: You can't pretend that you're invisible. You're the invisible car.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stuart Russell: Long-Term Future of Artificial Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #9

body.input: Right.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stuart Russell: Long-Term Future of Artificial Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #9

body.input: It doesn't work that way.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stuart Russell: Long-Term Future of Artificial Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #9

body.input: I mean, but you have to assert, yet others have to be scared of you. Just we're all, there's this tension. There's this game.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stuart Russell: Long-Term Future of Artificial Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #9

body.input: So we study a lot of work with pedestrians. If you approach pedestrians as purely an obstacle avoidance, so you're doing look ahead and modeling the intent, they're not going to take advantage of you.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stuart Russell: Long-Term Future of Artificial Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #9

body.input: They're not going to respect you at all. There has to be a tension, a fear, some amount of uncertainty.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stuart Russell: Long-Term Future of Artificial Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #9

body.input: That's how we have created.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stuart Russell: Long-Term Future of Artificial Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #9

body.input: Or at least just a kind of a resoluteness.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stuart Russell: Long-Term Future of Artificial Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #9

body.input: You have to display a certain amount of resoluteness. You can't be too tentative.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stuart Russell: Long-Term Future of Artificial Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #9

body.input: And yeah, so the solutions then become pretty complicated. You get into game theoretic analyses.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stuart Russell: Long-Term Future of Artificial Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #9

body.input: And so at Berkeley now, we're working a lot on this kind of interaction between machines and humans.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stuart Russell: Long-Term Future of Artificial Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #9

body.input: And that's exciting.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stuart Russell: Long-Term Future of Artificial Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #9

body.input: And so my colleague, Ankur Dragan, actually, you know, if you formulate the problem game theoretically, you just let the system figure out the solution.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stuart Russell: Long-Term Future of Artificial Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #9

body.input: You know, it does interesting unexpected things. Like sometimes at a stop sign, if no one is going first, right, the car will actually back up a little.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stuart Russell: Long-Term Future of Artificial Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #9

body.input: Right.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stuart Russell: Long-Term Future of Artificial Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #9

body.input: And just to indicate to the other cars that they should go. And that's something it invented entirely by itself.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stuart Russell: Long-Term Future of Artificial Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #9

body.input: That's interesting.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stuart Russell: Long-Term Future of Artificial Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #9

body.input: We didn't say this is the language of communication at stop signs. It figured it out.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stuart Russell: Long-Term Future of Artificial Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #9

body.input: That's really interesting. So let me one just step back for a second. Just this beautiful philosophical notion.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stuart Russell: Long-Term Future of Artificial Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #9

body.input: So Pamela McCordick in 1979 wrote, AI began with the ancient wish to forge the gods.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stuart Russell: Long-Term Future of Artificial Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #9

body.input: So when you think about the history of our civilization, do you think that there is an inherent desire to create, let's not say gods, but to create super intelligence?

metadata.title: Podcast: Stuart Russell: Long-Term Future of Artificial Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #9

body.input: Is it inherent to us? Is it in our genes that the natural arc of human civilization is to create things that are of greater and greater power and perhaps echoes of ourselves.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stuart Russell: Long-Term Future of Artificial Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #9

body.input: So to create the gods, as Pamela said.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stuart Russell: Long-Term Future of Artificial Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #9

body.input: Maybe. I mean, you know, we're all individuals, but certainly we see over and over again in history, individuals who thought about this possibility.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stuart Russell: Long-Term Future of Artificial Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #9

body.input: Hopefully when I'm not being too philosophical here, but if you look at the arc of this, you know, where this is going, and we'll talk about AI safety.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stuart Russell: Long-Term Future of Artificial Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #9

body.input: We'll talk about greater and greater intelligence. Do you see that there in when you created the ethyl program and you felt this excitement, what was that excitement?

metadata.title: Podcast: Stuart Russell: Long-Term Future of Artificial Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #9

body.input: Was it an excitement of a tinkerer who created something cool like a clock or was there a magic or was it more like a child being born?

metadata.title: Podcast: Stuart Russell: Long-Term Future of Artificial Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #9

body.input: Yeah. So, I mean, I certainly understand that viewpoint. And if you look at the Lighthill report, which was so in the seventies, there was a lot of controversy in the UK about AI and you know, whether it was for real and how much the money the government should invest.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stuart Russell: Long-Term Future of Artificial Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #9

body.input: So it's a long story, but the government commissioned a report by Lighthill, who was a physicist, and he wrote a very damning report about AI, which I think was the point.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stuart Russell: Long-Term Future of Artificial Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #9

body.input: And he said that these are, you know, frustrated men who unable to have children would like to create and, you know, create life, you know, as a kind of replacement, you know, which I think is really pretty unfair.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stuart Russell: Long-Term Future of Artificial Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #9

body.input: But there is, I mean, there is a kind of magic, I would say, when you build something, and what you're building in is really just you're building in some understanding of the principles of learning and decision making.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stuart Russell: Long-Term Future of Artificial Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #9

body.input: And to see those principles actually then turn into intelligent behavior in specific situations, it's an incredible thing.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stuart Russell: Long-Term Future of Artificial Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #9

body.input: And, you know, that is naturally going to make you think, okay, where does this end?

metadata.title: Podcast: Stuart Russell: Long-Term Future of Artificial Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #9

body.input: And so there's magical, optimistic views of where it ends, whatever your view of optimism is, whatever your view of utopia is, it's probably different for everybody.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stuart Russell: Long-Term Future of Artificial Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #9

body.input: But you've often talked about concerns you have of how things may go wrong. So I've talked to Max Tegmark, there's a lot of interesting ways to think about AI safety.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stuart Russell: Long-Term Future of Artificial Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #9

body.input: You're one of the seminal people thinking about this problem amongst sort of being in the weeds of actually solving specific AI problems. You also think about the big picture of where we're going.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stuart Russell: Long-Term Future of Artificial Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #9

body.input: So can you talk about several elements of it? Let's just talk about maybe the control problem. So this idea of losing ability to control the behavior in our AI system.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stuart Russell: Long-Term Future of Artificial Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #9

body.input: So how do you see that? How do you see that coming about? What do you think we can do to manage it?

metadata.title: Podcast: Stuart Russell: Long-Term Future of Artificial Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #9

body.input: Well, so it doesn't take a genius to realize that if you make something that's smarter than you, you might have a problem.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stuart Russell: Long-Term Future of Artificial Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #9

body.input: Alan Turing wrote about this and gave lectures about this in 1951. He did a lecture on the radio.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stuart Russell: Long-Term Future of Artificial Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #9

body.input: And he basically says, once the machine thinking method starts, very quickly they'll outstrip humanity.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stuart Russell: Long-Term Future of Artificial Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #9

body.input: And if we're lucky, we might be able to turn off the power at strategic moments, but even so our species would be humbled.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stuart Russell: Long-Term Future of Artificial Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #9

body.input: And actually, he was wrong about that, right? If it's a sufficiently intelligent machine, it's not going to let you switch it off. It's actually in competition with you.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stuart Russell: Long-Term Future of Artificial Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #9

body.input: So what do you think is meant just for a quick tangent, if we shut off this super intelligent machine, that our species would be humbled?

metadata.title: Podcast: Stuart Russell: Long-Term Future of Artificial Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #9

body.input: I think he means that we would realize that we are inferior, right? That we only survive by the skin of our teeth because we happen to get to the off switch.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stuart Russell: Long-Term Future of Artificial Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #9

body.input: That was a close call. Just in time. And if we hadn't, then we would have lost control over the earth.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stuart Russell: Long-Term Future of Artificial Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #9

body.input: Are you more worried when you think about this stuff about super intelligent AI or are you more worried about super powerful AI that's not aligned with our values? So the paperclip scenarios kind of...

metadata.title: Podcast: Stuart Russell: Long-Term Future of Artificial Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #9

body.input: I think, so the main problem I'm working on is the control problem, the problem of machines pursuing objectives that are, as you say, not aligned with human objectives.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stuart Russell: Long-Term Future of Artificial Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #9

body.input: And this has been the way we've thought about AI since the beginning.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stuart Russell: Long-Term Future of Artificial Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #9

body.input: You build a machine for optimizing and then you put in some objective and it optimizes.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stuart Russell: Long-Term Future of Artificial Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #9

body.input: And we can think of this as the King Midas problem.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stuart Russell: Long-Term Future of Artificial Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #9

body.input: Because if the King Midas put in this objective, everything I touch should turn to gold.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stuart Russell: Long-Term Future of Artificial Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #9

body.input: And the gods, that's like the machine, they said, okay, done. You now have this power. And of course, his food and his drink and his family all turned to gold and then he dies of misery and starvation.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stuart Russell: Long-Term Future of Artificial Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #9

body.input: And this is a warning, it's a failure mode that pretty much every culture in history has had some story along the same lines. There's the genie that gives you three wishes and third wish is always, please undo the first two wishes because I messed up.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stuart Russell: Long-Term Future of Artificial Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #9

body.input: And when Arthur Samuel wrote his checker playing program, which learned to play checkers considerably better than Arthur Samuel could play and actually reached a pretty decent standard,

metadata.title: Podcast: Stuart Russell: Long-Term Future of Artificial Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #9

body.input: Norbert Wiener, who was one of the major mathematicians of the 20th century, he's sort of the father of modern automation control systems.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stuart Russell: Long-Term Future of Artificial Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #9

body.input: He saw this and he basically extrapolated, as Turing did and said, okay, this is how we could lose control.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stuart Russell: Long-Term Future of Artificial Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #9

body.input: And specifically that we have to be certain that the purpose we put into the machine is the purpose which we really desire.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stuart Russell: Long-Term Future of Artificial Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #9

body.input: And the problem is we can't do that.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stuart Russell: Long-Term Future of Artificial Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #9

body.input: You mean it's very difficult to encode, to put our values on paper is really difficult or you're just saying it's impossible?

metadata.title: Podcast: Stuart Russell: Long-Term Future of Artificial Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #9

body.input: The line is gray between the two.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stuart Russell: Long-Term Future of Artificial Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #9

body.input: So theoretically it's possible, but in practice it's extremely unlikely that we could specify correctly in advance the full range of concerns of humanity.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stuart Russell: Long-Term Future of Artificial Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #9

body.input: You talked about cultural transmission of values, I think is how humans to human transmission of values happens, right?

metadata.title: Podcast: Stuart Russell: Long-Term Future of Artificial Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #9

body.input: Well, we learn. Yeah. I mean, as we grow up, we learn about the values that matter how things should go, what is reasonable to pursue and what isn't reasonable to pursue.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stuart Russell: Long-Term Future of Artificial Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #9

body.input: I think machines can learn in the same kind of way.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stuart Russell: Long-Term Future of Artificial Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #9

body.input: Yeah. So I think that what we need to do is to get away from this idea that you build an optimizing machine and then you put the objective into it.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stuart Russell: Long-Term Future of Artificial Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #9

body.input: Because if it's possible that you might put in a wrong objective, and we already know this is possible because it's happened lots of times, right?

metadata.title: Podcast: Stuart Russell: Long-Term Future of Artificial Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #9

body.input: That means that the machine should never take an objective that's given as gospel truth.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stuart Russell: Long-Term Future of Artificial Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #9

body.input: Because once it takes the objective as gospel truth, then it believes that whatever actions it's taking in pursuit of that objective are the correct things to do.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stuart Russell: Long-Term Future of Artificial Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #9

body.input: So you could be jumping up and down and saying, no, no, no, no, you're going to destroy the world.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stuart Russell: Long-Term Future of Artificial Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #9

body.input: But the machine knows what the true objective is and is pursuing it. And tough luck to you.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stuart Russell: Long-Term Future of Artificial Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #9

body.input: And this is not restricted to AI, right? This is, I think, many of the 20th century technologies, right?

metadata.title: Podcast: Stuart Russell: Long-Term Future of Artificial Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #9

body.input: So in statistics, you minimize a loss function. The loss function is exogenously specified.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stuart Russell: Long-Term Future of Artificial Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #9

body.input: In control theory, you minimize a cost function. In operations research, you maximize a reward function and so on.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stuart Russell: Long-Term Future of Artificial Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #9

body.input: So in all these disciplines, this is how we conceive of the problem. And it's the wrong problem because we cannot specify with certainty the correct objective, right?

metadata.title: Podcast: Stuart Russell: Long-Term Future of Artificial Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #9

body.input: We need uncertainty. We need the machine to be uncertain about what it is that it's supposed to be maximizing.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stuart Russell: Long-Term Future of Artificial Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #9

body.input: Favorite idea of yours. I've heard you say somewhere, well, I shouldn't pick favorites, but it just sounds beautiful. We need to teach machines humility.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stuart Russell: Long-Term Future of Artificial Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #9

body.input: Yeah, it's a beautiful way to put it. I love it.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stuart Russell: Long-Term Future of Artificial Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #9

body.input: That they humble in that they know that they don't know what it is they're supposed to be doing and that those objectives, I mean, they exist.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stuart Russell: Long-Term Future of Artificial Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #9

body.input: They're within us, but we may not be able to explicate them. We may not even know how we want our future to go.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stuart Russell: Long-Term Future of Artificial Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #9

body.input: Exactly.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stuart Russell: Long-Term Future of Artificial Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #9

body.input: And the machine, a machine that's uncertain is going to be deferential to us. So if we say don't do that, well, now the machines learn something a bit more about our true objectives,

metadata.title: Podcast: Stuart Russell: Long-Term Future of Artificial Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #9

body.input: because something that it thought was reasonable in pursuit of our objectives turns out not to be. So now it's learned something.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stuart Russell: Long-Term Future of Artificial Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #9

body.input: So it's going to defer because it wants to be doing what we really want. And that point, I think, is absolutely central to solving the control problem.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stuart Russell: Long-Term Future of Artificial Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #9

body.input: And it's a different kind of AI when you take away this idea that the objective is known, then in fact, a lot of the theoretical frameworks that we're so familiar with,

metadata.title: Podcast: Stuart Russell: Long-Term Future of Artificial Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #9

body.input: you know, Markov decision processes, goal-based planning, you know, standard games research, all of these techniques actually become inapplicable. And you get a more complicated problem because.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stuart Russell: Long-Term Future of Artificial Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #9

body.input: Because now.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stuart Russell: Long-Term Future of Artificial Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #9

body.input: The interaction with the human becomes part of the problem.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stuart Russell: Long-Term Future of Artificial Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #9

body.input: Because the human by making choices is giving you more information about the true objective and that information helps you achieve the objective better.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stuart Russell: Long-Term Future of Artificial Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #9

body.input: And so that really means that you're mostly dealing with game theoretic problems where you've got the machine and the human and they're coupled together rather than a machine going off by itself with a fixed objective.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stuart Russell: Long-Term Future of Artificial Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #9

body.input: Which is fascinating on the machine and the human level that we when you don't have an objective means you're together coming up with an objective.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stuart Russell: Long-Term Future of Artificial Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #9

body.input: I mean, there's a lot of philosophy that, you know, you could argue that life doesn't really have meaning. We together agree on what gives it meaning.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stuart Russell: Long-Term Future of Artificial Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #9

body.input: And we kind of culturally create things that give why the heck we are in this earth anyway. We together as a society create that meaning and you have to learn that objective.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stuart Russell: Long-Term Future of Artificial Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #9

body.input: And one of the biggest I thought that's where you were going to go for a second.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stuart Russell: Long-Term Future of Artificial Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #9

body.input: One of the biggest troubles we run into outside of statistics and machine learning and AI and just human civilization is when you look at I came from I was born in the Soviet Union.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stuart Russell: Long-Term Future of Artificial Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #9

body.input: And the history of the 20th century, we ran into the most trouble as humans when there was a certainty about the objective and you do whatever it takes to achieve that objective.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stuart Russell: Long-Term Future of Artificial Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #9

body.input: Whether you're talking about Germany or communist Russia.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stuart Russell: Long-Term Future of Artificial Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #9

body.input: I would say with corporations, in fact, some people argue that we don't have to look forward to a time when AI systems take over the world. They already have and they call corporations.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stuart Russell: Long-Term Future of Artificial Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #9

body.input: Right? That corporations happen to be using people as components right now, but they are effectively algorithmic machines and they're optimizing an objective, which is quarterly profit that isn't aligned with overall well-being of the human race.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stuart Russell: Long-Term Future of Artificial Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #9

body.input: And they are destroying the world. They are primarily responsible for our inability to tackle climate change.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stuart Russell: Long-Term Future of Artificial Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #9

body.input: So I think that's one way of thinking about what's going on with corporations.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stuart Russell: Long-Term Future of Artificial Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #9

body.input: But I think the point you're making is valid that there are many systems in the real world where we've sort of prematurely fixed on the objective and then decoupled the machine from those that's supposed to be serving.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stuart Russell: Long-Term Future of Artificial Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #9

body.input: And I think you see this with government. Right? Government is supposed to be a machine that serves people.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stuart Russell: Long-Term Future of Artificial Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #9

body.input: But instead, it tends to be taken over by people who have their own objective and use government to optimize that objective, regardless of what people want.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stuart Russell: Long-Term Future of Artificial Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #9

body.input: Do you find appealing the idea of almost arguing machines where you have multiple AI systems with a clear fixed objective?

metadata.title: Podcast: Stuart Russell: Long-Term Future of Artificial Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #9

body.input: We have in government the red team and the blue team that are very fixed on their objectives and they argue and they kind of disagree, but it kind of seems to make it work somewhat.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stuart Russell: Long-Term Future of Artificial Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #9

body.input: The duality of it. Let's go 100 years back when there was still was going on at the founding of this country. There was disagreements and that disagreement is where there's a balance between certainty and forced humility because the power was distributed.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stuart Russell: Long-Term Future of Artificial Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #9

body.input: Yeah, I think that the nature of debate and disagreement argument takes as a premise the idea that you could be wrong.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stuart Russell: Long-Term Future of Artificial Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #9

body.input: Which means that you're not necessarily absolutely convinced that your objective is the correct one.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stuart Russell: Long-Term Future of Artificial Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #9

body.input: If you were, absolutely, there would be no point in having any discussion or argument because you would never change your mind and there wouldn't be any sort of synthesis or anything like that.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stuart Russell: Long-Term Future of Artificial Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #9

body.input: So I think you can think of argumentation as an implementation of a form of uncertain reasoning.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stuart Russell: Long-Term Future of Artificial Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #9

body.input: I've been reading recently about utilitarianism and the history of efforts to define in a sort of clear mathematical way a formula for moral or political decision making.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stuart Russell: Long-Term Future of Artificial Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #9

body.input: And it's really interesting that the parallels between the philosophical discussions going back 200 years and what you see now in discussions about existential risk because it's almost exactly the same.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stuart Russell: Long-Term Future of Artificial Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #9

body.input: So someone would say, okay, well, here's a formula for how we should make decisions. So utilitarianism is roughly, each person has a utility function and then we make decisions to maximize the sum of everybody's utility.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stuart Russell: Long-Term Future of Artificial Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #9

body.input: And then people point out, well, in that case, the best policy is one that leads to the enormously vast population, all of whom are living a life that's barely worth living.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stuart Russell: Long-Term Future of Artificial Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #9

body.input: And this is called the repugnant conclusion. And another version is that we should maximize pleasure and that's what we mean by utility.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stuart Russell: Long-Term Future of Artificial Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #9

body.input: And then you'll get people effectively saying, well, in that case, we might as well just have everyone hooked up to a heroin drip.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stuart Russell: Long-Term Future of Artificial Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #9

body.input: And they didn't use those words, but that debate was happening in the 19th century as it is now about AI that if we get the formula wrong, we're going to have AI systems working towards an outcome that in retrospect would be exactly wrong.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stuart Russell: Long-Term Future of Artificial Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #9

body.input: Do you think there's, as beautifully put, the echoes are there, but do you think, I mean, if you look at Sam Harris, our imagination worries about the AI version of that because of the speed at which the things going wrong in the utilitarian context could happen.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stuart Russell: Long-Term Future of Artificial Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #9

body.input: Yeah.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stuart Russell: Long-Term Future of Artificial Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #9

body.input: Is that a worry for you?

metadata.title: Podcast: Stuart Russell: Long-Term Future of Artificial Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #9

body.input: I think that, you know, in most cases, not in all, but if we have a wrong political idea, you know, we see it starting to go wrong and we're, you know, we're not completely stupid.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stuart Russell: Long-Term Future of Artificial Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #9

body.input: And so we said, okay, that was maybe that was a mistake. Let's try something different.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stuart Russell: Long-Term Future of Artificial Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #9

body.input: And also we're very slow and inefficient about implementing these things and so on. So you have to worry when you have corporations or political systems that are extremely efficient.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stuart Russell: Long-Term Future of Artificial Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #9

body.input: But when we look at AI systems, or even just computers in general, right, they have this different characteristic from ordinary human activity in the past.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stuart Russell: Long-Term Future of Artificial Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #9

body.input: So let's say you were a surgeon. You had some idea about how to do some operation, right? Well, and let's say you were wrong, right? That that way of doing the operation would mostly kill the patient.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stuart Russell: Long-Term Future of Artificial Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #9

body.input: Well, you'd find out pretty quickly, like after three, maybe three or four tries, right?

metadata.title: Podcast: Stuart Russell: Long-Term Future of Artificial Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #9

body.input: But.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stuart Russell: Long-Term Future of Artificial Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #9

body.input: That isn't true for pharmaceutical companies.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stuart Russell: Long-Term Future of Artificial Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #9

body.input: Because they don't do three or four operations. They they manufacture three or four billion pills and they sell them and then they find out maybe six months or a year later that, oh, people are dying of heart attacks or getting cancer from this drug.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stuart Russell: Long-Term Future of Artificial Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #9

body.input: And so that's why we have the FDA, right? Because of the scalability of pharmaceutical production.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stuart Russell: Long-Term Future of Artificial Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #9

body.input: And you and there have been some unbelievably bad episodes.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stuart Russell: Long-Term Future of Artificial Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #9

body.input: In the history of pharmaceuticals and adulteration of of products and so on that that have killed tens of thousands or paralyzed hundreds of thousands of people.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stuart Russell: Long-Term Future of Artificial Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #9

body.input: Now with computers, we have that same scalability problem that you can sit there and type for I equals one to five billion do right now. All of a sudden you're having an impact on a global scale.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stuart Russell: Long-Term Future of Artificial Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #9

body.input: And yet we have no FDA, right? There's absolutely no controls at all.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stuart Russell: Long-Term Future of Artificial Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #9

body.input: Over what a bunch of undergraduates with too much caffeine can do to the world.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stuart Russell: Long-Term Future of Artificial Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #9

body.input: And, you know, we look at what happened with Facebook.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stuart Russell: Long-Term Future of Artificial Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #9

body.input: Well, social media in general and click through optimization.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stuart Russell: Long-Term Future of Artificial Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #9

body.input: So you have a simple feedback algorithm that's trying to just optimize click through.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stuart Russell: Long-Term Future of Artificial Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #9

body.input: That sounds reasonable, right? Because you don't want to be feeding people ads that they don't care about and not interested in.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stuart Russell: Long-Term Future of Artificial Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #9

body.input: And you might even think of that process as simply adjusting the the feeding of ads or news articles or whatever it might be to match people's preferences.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stuart Russell: Long-Term Future of Artificial Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #9

body.input: Right, which sounds like a good idea.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stuart Russell: Long-Term Future of Artificial Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #9

body.input: But in fact, that isn't how the algorithm works.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stuart Russell: Long-Term Future of Artificial Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #9

body.input: Right.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stuart Russell: Long-Term Future of Artificial Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #9

body.input: You make more money.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stuart Russell: Long-Term Future of Artificial Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #9

body.input: The algorithm makes more money if it can better predict what people are going to click on because then it can feed them exactly that.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stuart Russell: Long-Term Future of Artificial Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #9

body.input: Right. So the way to maximize click through is actually to modify the people to make them more predictable.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stuart Russell: Long-Term Future of Artificial Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #9

body.input: And one way to do that is to feed them information which will change their behavior and preferences towards extremes that make them predictable.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stuart Russell: Long-Term Future of Artificial Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #9

body.input: Whatever is the nearest extreme or the nearest predictable point, that's where you're going to end up.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stuart Russell: Long-Term Future of Artificial Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #9

body.input: And the machines will force you there.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stuart Russell: Long-Term Future of Artificial Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #9

body.input: Now, and I think there's a reasonable argument to say that this, among other things, is contributing to the destruction of democracy in the world.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stuart Russell: Long-Term Future of Artificial Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #9

body.input: And where was the oversight of this process?

metadata.title: Podcast: Stuart Russell: Long-Term Future of Artificial Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #9

body.input: Where were the people saying, okay, you would like to apply this algorithm to five billion people on the face of the Earth.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stuart Russell: Long-Term Future of Artificial Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #9

body.input: Can you show me that it's safe?

metadata.title: Podcast: Stuart Russell: Long-Term Future of Artificial Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #9

body.input: Can you show me that it won't have various kinds of negative effects?

metadata.title: Podcast: Stuart Russell: Long-Term Future of Artificial Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #9

body.input: No, there was no one asking that question.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stuart Russell: Long-Term Future of Artificial Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #9

body.input: There was no one placed between the undergrads with too much caffeine and the human race.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stuart Russell: Long-Term Future of Artificial Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #9

body.input: They just did it.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stuart Russell: Long-Term Future of Artificial Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #9

body.input: But some way outside the scope of my knowledge, so economists would argue that the invisible hand, so the capitalist system, it was the oversight.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stuart Russell: Long-Term Future of Artificial Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #9

body.input: So if you're going to corrupt society with whatever decision you make as a company, then that's going to be reflected in people not using your product.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stuart Russell: Long-Term Future of Artificial Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #9

body.input: Sort of one, that's one model of oversight.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stuart Russell: Long-Term Future of Artificial Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #9

body.input: We shall see.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stuart Russell: Long-Term Future of Artificial Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #9

body.input: But in the meantime, you know, but you might even have broken the political system that enables capitalism to function.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stuart Russell: Long-Term Future of Artificial Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #9

body.input: Well, you've changed it.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stuart Russell: Long-Term Future of Artificial Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #9

body.input: So we should see.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stuart Russell: Long-Term Future of Artificial Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #9

body.input: Change is often painful.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stuart Russell: Long-Term Future of Artificial Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #9

body.input: So my question is absolutely it's fascinating.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stuart Russell: Long-Term Future of Artificial Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #9

body.input: You're absolutely right that there is zero oversight on algorithms that can have a profound civilization changing effect.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stuart Russell: Long-Term Future of Artificial Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #9

body.input: So do you think it's possible?

metadata.title: Podcast: Stuart Russell: Long-Term Future of Artificial Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #9

body.input: I mean, I haven't.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stuart Russell: Long-Term Future of Artificial Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #9

body.input: Have you seen government?

metadata.title: Podcast: Stuart Russell: Long-Term Future of Artificial Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #9

body.input: So do you think it's possible to create regulatory bodies oversight over AI algorithms, which are inherently such cutting edge set of ideas and technologies?

metadata.title: Podcast: Stuart Russell: Long-Term Future of Artificial Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #9

body.input: Yeah, but I think it takes time to figure out what kind of oversight, what kinds of controls.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stuart Russell: Long-Term Future of Artificial Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #9

body.input: I mean, it took time to design the FDA regime.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stuart Russell: Long-Term Future of Artificial Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #9

body.input: You know, some people still don't like it and they want to fix it.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stuart Russell: Long-Term Future of Artificial Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #9

body.input: And I think there are clear ways that it could be improved.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stuart Russell: Long-Term Future of Artificial Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #9

body.input: But the whole notion that you have stage one, stage two, stage three, and here are the criteria for what you have to do to pass a stage one trial.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stuart Russell: Long-Term Future of Artificial Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #9

body.input: Right.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stuart Russell: Long-Term Future of Artificial Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #9

body.input: We haven't even thought about what those would be for algorithms.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stuart Russell: Long-Term Future of Artificial Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #9

body.input: So, I mean, I think there are.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stuart Russell: Long-Term Future of Artificial Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #9

body.input: There are things we could do right now.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stuart Russell: Long-Term Future of Artificial Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #9

body.input: With regard to bias, for example, we have a pretty good.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stuart Russell: Long-Term Future of Artificial Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #9
