metadata.title: Podcast: Stuart Russell: Long-Term Future of Artificial Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #9

body.input: So I think we could start having some standards on that.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stuart Russell: Long-Term Future of Artificial Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #9

body.input: I think there are there are things to do with.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stuart Russell: Long-Term Future of Artificial Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #9

body.input: Impersonation and falsification that we could we could work on, so I think.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stuart Russell: Long-Term Future of Artificial Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #9

body.input: Or a very simple point, so impersonation is a machine.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stuart Russell: Long-Term Future of Artificial Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #9

body.input: Acting as if it was a person.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stuart Russell: Long-Term Future of Artificial Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #9

body.input: I can't see a real justification.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stuart Russell: Long-Term Future of Artificial Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #9

body.input: For why we shouldn't insist that machine self identify as machines.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stuart Russell: Long-Term Future of Artificial Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #9

body.input: You know, where is the social benefit in in fooling people into thinking that this is really a person when it isn't.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stuart Russell: Long-Term Future of Artificial Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #9

body.input: You know, I don't mind if it uses a human like voice.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stuart Russell: Long-Term Future of Artificial Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #9

body.input: That's easy to understand.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stuart Russell: Long-Term Future of Artificial Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #9

body.input: That's fine, but it should just say, I'm a machine in some some form.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stuart Russell: Long-Term Future of Artificial Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #9

body.input: And now many people are speaking to that.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stuart Russell: Long-Term Future of Artificial Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #9

body.input: I would think relatively obvious facts.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stuart Russell: Long-Term Future of Artificial Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #9

body.input: So I think most people.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stuart Russell: Long-Term Future of Artificial Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #9

body.input: Yeah, I mean, there is actually a law in California.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stuart Russell: Long-Term Future of Artificial Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #9

body.input: That bans impersonation, but only in certain restricted circumstances.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stuart Russell: Long-Term Future of Artificial Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #9

body.input: So for the purpose of engaging in a fraudulent transaction and for the purpose of modifying someone's voting behavior.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stuart Russell: Long-Term Future of Artificial Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #9

body.input: So those are those are the circumstances where machines have to self identify.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stuart Russell: Long-Term Future of Artificial Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #9

body.input: But I think this, you know, arguably it should be in all circumstances.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stuart Russell: Long-Term Future of Artificial Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #9

body.input: And then when you when you talk about deep fakes, you know, we're just at the beginning.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stuart Russell: Long-Term Future of Artificial Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #9

body.input: But already it's possible to make a movie of anybody saying anything in ways that are pretty hard to detect, including yourself, because you're on camera now and your voice is coming through with high resolution.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stuart Russell: Long-Term Future of Artificial Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #9

body.input: So you could take what I'm saying and replace it with a pretty much anything else you wanted me to be saying.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stuart Russell: Long-Term Future of Artificial Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #9

body.input: And even it would change my lips and express your expressions to fit.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stuart Russell: Long-Term Future of Artificial Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #9

body.input: And there's actually not much in the way of real legal protection against that.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stuart Russell: Long-Term Future of Artificial Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #9

body.input: I think in the commercial area, you could say, yeah, that's you're using my brand and so on.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stuart Russell: Long-Term Future of Artificial Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #9

body.input: There are rules about that.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stuart Russell: Long-Term Future of Artificial Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #9

body.input: But in the political sphere, I think it's at the moment, it's you know, anything goes.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stuart Russell: Long-Term Future of Artificial Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #9

body.input: So that could be really, really damaging.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stuart Russell: Long-Term Future of Artificial Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #9

body.input: And let me just try to make not an argument, but try to look back at history and say something dark.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stuart Russell: Long-Term Future of Artificial Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #9

body.input: In essence is while regulation seems to be oversight seems to be exactly the right thing to do here.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stuart Russell: Long-Term Future of Artificial Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #9

body.input: It seems that human beings, what they naturally do is they wait for something to go wrong.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stuart Russell: Long-Term Future of Artificial Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #9

body.input: If you're talking about nuclear weapons, you can't talk about nuclear weapons being dangerous until somebody actually like the United States drops the bomb or Chernobyl melting.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stuart Russell: Long-Term Future of Artificial Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #9

body.input: Do you think we will have to wait for things going wrong in a way that's obviously damaging to society, not an existential risk, but obviously damaging?

metadata.title: Podcast: Stuart Russell: Long-Term Future of Artificial Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #9

body.input: Or do you have faith that I hope not?

metadata.title: Podcast: Stuart Russell: Long-Term Future of Artificial Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #9

body.input: But I mean, I think we do have to look at history.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stuart Russell: Long-Term Future of Artificial Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #9

body.input: And so the two examples you gave, nuclear weapons and nuclear power are very, very interesting because nuclear weapons, we knew in the early years of the 20th century that atoms contained a huge amount of energy.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stuart Russell: Long-Term Future of Artificial Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #9

body.input: We had E equals MC squared, we knew the mass differences between the different atoms and their components, and we knew that you might be able to make an incredibly powerful explosive.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stuart Russell: Long-Term Future of Artificial Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #9

body.input: So H.G. Wells wrote science fiction book, I think in 1912.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stuart Russell: Long-Term Future of Artificial Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #9

body.input: Frederick Soddy, who was the guy who discovered isotopes, is a Nobel Prize winner. He gave a speech in 1915 saying that one pound of this new explosive would be the equivalent of 150 tons of dynamite, which turns out to be about right.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stuart Russell: Long-Term Future of Artificial Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #9

body.input: And this was in World War I, right? So he was imagining how much worse the world war would be if we were using that kind of explosive.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stuart Russell: Long-Term Future of Artificial Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #9

body.input: But the physics establishment simply refused to believe that these things could be made.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stuart Russell: Long-Term Future of Artificial Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #9

body.input: Including the people who are making it.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stuart Russell: Long-Term Future of Artificial Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #9

body.input: Well, so they were doing the nuclear physics.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stuart Russell: Long-Term Future of Artificial Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #9

body.input: I mean, eventually were the ones who made it. You talk about Fermi or whoever.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stuart Russell: Long-Term Future of Artificial Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #9

body.input: Well, so up to the development was mostly theoretical.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stuart Russell: Long-Term Future of Artificial Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #9

body.input: So it was people using sort of primitive kinds of particle acceleration and doing experiments at the level of single particles or collections of particles.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stuart Russell: Long-Term Future of Artificial Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #9

body.input: They weren't yet thinking about how to actually make a bomb or anything like that.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stuart Russell: Long-Term Future of Artificial Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #9

body.input: But they knew the energy was there and they figured if they understood it better, it might be possible.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stuart Russell: Long-Term Future of Artificial Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #9

body.input: But the physics establishment, their view, and I think because they did not want it to be true, their view was that it could not be true.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stuart Russell: Long-Term Future of Artificial Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #9

body.input: That this could not provide a way to make a super weapon.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stuart Russell: Long-Term Future of Artificial Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #9

body.input: And there was this famous speech given by Rutherford, who was the sort of leader of nuclear physics.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stuart Russell: Long-Term Future of Artificial Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #9

body.input: It was on September 11th, 1933.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stuart Russell: Long-Term Future of Artificial Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #9

body.input: And he said, anyone who talks about the possibility of obtaining energy from transformation of atoms is talking complete moonshine.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stuart Russell: Long-Term Future of Artificial Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #9

body.input: And the next morning, Leo Szilard read about that speech and then invented the nuclear chain reaction.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stuart Russell: Long-Term Future of Artificial Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #9

body.input: And so as soon as he had that idea that you could make a chain reaction with neutrons, because neutrons were not repelled by the nucleus, so they could enter the nucleus and then continue the reaction.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stuart Russell: Long-Term Future of Artificial Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #9

body.input: As soon as he has that idea, he instantly realized that the world was in deep doo-doo.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stuart Russell: Long-Term Future of Artificial Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #9

body.input: Because this is 1933, right?

metadata.title: Podcast: Stuart Russell: Long-Term Future of Artificial Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #9

body.input: Hitler had recently come to power in Germany.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stuart Russell: Long-Term Future of Artificial Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #9

body.input: Szilard was in London and eventually became a refugee and came to the US.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stuart Russell: Long-Term Future of Artificial Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #9

body.input: And in the process of having the idea about the chain reaction, he figured out basically how to make a bomb and also how to make a reactor.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stuart Russell: Long-Term Future of Artificial Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #9

body.input: And he patented the reactor in 1934.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stuart Russell: Long-Term Future of Artificial Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #9

body.input: But because of the situation, the great power conflict situation that he could see happening, he kept that a secret.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stuart Russell: Long-Term Future of Artificial Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #9

body.input: And so between then and the beginning of World War II, people were working, including the Germans, on how to actually create neutron sources, right?

metadata.title: Podcast: Stuart Russell: Long-Term Future of Artificial Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #9

body.input: What specific fission reactions would produce neutrons of the right energy to continue the reaction?

metadata.title: Podcast: Stuart Russell: Long-Term Future of Artificial Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #9

body.input: And that was demonstrated in Germany, I think, in 1938, if I remember correctly.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stuart Russell: Long-Term Future of Artificial Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #9

body.input: The first nuclear weapon patent was 1939 by the French.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stuart Russell: Long-Term Future of Artificial Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #9

body.input: So this was actually going on well before World War II really got going.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stuart Russell: Long-Term Future of Artificial Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #9

body.input: And then the British probably had the most advanced capability in this area, but for safety reasons, among others, and plus just sort of just resources, they moved the program from Britain to the US.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stuart Russell: Long-Term Future of Artificial Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #9

body.input: And then that became Manhattan Project.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stuart Russell: Long-Term Future of Artificial Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #9

body.input: So the reason why we couldn't have any kind of oversight of nuclear weapons and nuclear technology was because we were basically already in an arms race and a war.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stuart Russell: Long-Term Future of Artificial Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #9

body.input: But you mentioned that in the 20s and 30s.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stuart Russell: Long-Term Future of Artificial Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #9

body.input: So what are the echoes?

metadata.title: Podcast: Stuart Russell: Long-Term Future of Artificial Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #9

body.input: The way you've described the story, I mean, there's clearly echoes. Why do you think most AI researchers, folks who are really close to the metal, they really are not concerned about it?

metadata.title: Podcast: Stuart Russell: Long-Term Future of Artificial Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #9

body.input: They don't think about it, whether it's they don't want to think about it.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stuart Russell: Long-Term Future of Artificial Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #9

body.input: But what are the, yeah, why do you think that is?

metadata.title: Podcast: Stuart Russell: Long-Term Future of Artificial Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #9

body.input: What are the echoes of the nuclear situation to the current AI situation?

metadata.title: Podcast: Stuart Russell: Long-Term Future of Artificial Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #9

body.input: And what can we do about it?

metadata.title: Podcast: Stuart Russell: Long-Term Future of Artificial Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #9

body.input: I think there is a kind of motivated cognition, which is a term in psychology means that you believe what you would like to be true rather than what is true.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stuart Russell: Long-Term Future of Artificial Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #9

body.input: And, you know, it's unsettling to think that what you're working on might be the end of the human race, obviously.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stuart Russell: Long-Term Future of Artificial Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #9

body.input: So you would rather instantly deny it and come up with some reason why it couldn't be true.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stuart Russell: Long-Term Future of Artificial Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #9

body.input: And, you know, I have I collected a long list of reasons that extremely intelligent, competent AI scientists have come up with for why we shouldn't worry about this.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stuart Russell: Long-Term Future of Artificial Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #9

body.input: For example, calculators are superhuman at arithmetic and they haven't taken over the world, so there's nothing to worry about.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stuart Russell: Long-Term Future of Artificial Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #9

body.input: Well, OK, my five year old, you know, could have figured out why that was an unreasonable and really quite weak argument.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stuart Russell: Long-Term Future of Artificial Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #9

body.input: You know, another one was, you know, while it's theoretically possible that you could have superhuman AI destroy the world, you know, it's also theoretically possible that a black hole could materialize right next to the Earth and destroy humanity.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stuart Russell: Long-Term Future of Artificial Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #9

body.input: I mean, yes, it's theoretically possible quantum theoretically, extremely unlikely that it would just materialize right there.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stuart Russell: Long-Term Future of Artificial Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #9

body.input: But that's a completely bogus analogy, because, you know, if the whole physics community on Earth was working to materialize a black hole in near Earth orbit.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stuart Russell: Long-Term Future of Artificial Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #9

body.input: Right. Wouldn't you ask them, is that a good idea? Is that going to be safe? You know, what if you succeed? Right. Right. And that's the thing.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stuart Russell: Long-Term Future of Artificial Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #9

body.input: Right. The AI community is sort of refused to ask itself, what if you succeed?

metadata.title: Podcast: Stuart Russell: Long-Term Future of Artificial Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #9

body.input: And initially, I think that was because it was too hard. But, you know, Alan Turing asked himself that.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stuart Russell: Long-Term Future of Artificial Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #9

body.input: And he said, we'd be toast. Right. If we were lucky, we might be able to switch off the power, but probably we'd be toast.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stuart Russell: Long-Term Future of Artificial Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #9

body.input: But there's also an aspect that because we're not exactly sure what the future holds, it's not clear exactly so technically what to worry about, sort of how things go wrong.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stuart Russell: Long-Term Future of Artificial Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #9

body.input: And so there is something it feels like maybe you can correct me if I'm wrong.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stuart Russell: Long-Term Future of Artificial Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #9

body.input: But there's something paralyzing about worrying about something that logically is inevitable, but you don't really know what that will look like.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stuart Russell: Long-Term Future of Artificial Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #9

body.input: Yeah, I think that's a reasonable point. And, you know, it's certainly in terms of existential risks, it's different from, you know, the asteroid collides with the Earth. Right.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stuart Russell: Long-Term Future of Artificial Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #9

body.input: Which, again, is quite possible. You know, it's happened in the past. It'll probably happen again. We don't know right now.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stuart Russell: Long-Term Future of Artificial Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #9

body.input: But if we did detect an asteroid that was going to hit the Earth in 75 years time, we'd certainly be doing something about it.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stuart Russell: Long-Term Future of Artificial Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #9

body.input: Well, it's clear there's a big rock. We'll probably have a meeting and see what do we do about the big rock.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stuart Russell: Long-Term Future of Artificial Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #9

body.input: With AI. Right, with AI. I mean, there are very few people who think it's not going to happen within the next 75 years.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stuart Russell: Long-Term Future of Artificial Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #9

body.input: I know Rod Brooks doesn't think it's going to happen. Maybe Andrew Ng doesn't think it's happened.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stuart Russell: Long-Term Future of Artificial Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #9

body.input: But, you know, a lot of the people who work day to day, you know, as you say, at the rock face, they think it's going to happen.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stuart Russell: Long-Term Future of Artificial Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #9

body.input: The median estimate from AI researchers is somewhere in 40 to 50 years from now or maybe even a little, you know, I think in Asia, they think it's going to be even faster than that.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stuart Russell: Long-Term Future of Artificial Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #9

body.input: I am a little bit more conservative. I think it would probably take longer than that.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stuart Russell: Long-Term Future of Artificial Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #9

body.input: But I think, you know, as happened with nuclear weapons, it can happen overnight that you have these breakthroughs.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stuart Russell: Long-Term Future of Artificial Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #9

body.input: It's more than one breakthrough, but, you know, it's on the order of half a dozen.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stuart Russell: Long-Term Future of Artificial Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #9

body.input: I mean, this is a very rough scale, but sort of half a dozen breakthroughs of that nature would have to happen for us to reach superhuman AI.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stuart Russell: Long-Term Future of Artificial Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #9

body.input: But the, you know, the AI research community is vast now.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stuart Russell: Long-Term Future of Artificial Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #9

body.input: Massive investments from governments, from corporations, tons of really, really smart people. You know, you just have to look at the rate of progress in different areas of AI to see that things are moving pretty fast.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stuart Russell: Long-Term Future of Artificial Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #9

body.input: So to say, oh, it's just going to be thousands of years. I don't see any basis for that.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stuart Russell: Long-Term Future of Artificial Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #9

body.input: You know, I see, you know, for example, the Stanford 100-year AI project, right, which is supposed to be sort of, you know, the serious establishment view.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stuart Russell: Long-Term Future of Artificial Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #9

body.input: Their most recent report actually said it's probably not even possible.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stuart Russell: Long-Term Future of Artificial Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #9

body.input: Oh, wow.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stuart Russell: Long-Term Future of Artificial Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #9

body.input: Right. Which if you want a perfect example of people in denial, that's it. Because, you know, for the whole history of AI, we've been saying to philosophers who said it wasn't possible.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stuart Russell: Long-Term Future of Artificial Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #9

body.input: Well, you have no idea what you're talking about. Of course it's possible.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stuart Russell: Long-Term Future of Artificial Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #9

body.input: Right. Give me an argument for why it couldn't happen. And there isn't one.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stuart Russell: Long-Term Future of Artificial Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #9

body.input: Right. And now because people are worried that maybe AI might get a bad name or I just don't want to think about this.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stuart Russell: Long-Term Future of Artificial Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #9

body.input: They're saying, okay, well, of course, it's not really possible.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stuart Russell: Long-Term Future of Artificial Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #9

body.input: You know, imagine, right, imagine if, you know, the, the leaders of the cancer biology community got up and said, well, you know, of course, curing cancer, it's not really possible.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stuart Russell: Long-Term Future of Artificial Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #9

body.input: There'd be a complete outrage and dismay.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stuart Russell: Long-Term Future of Artificial Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #9

body.input: And, you know, I find this really a strange phenomenon.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stuart Russell: Long-Term Future of Artificial Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #9

body.input: So, okay, so if you accept that it's possible, and if you accept that it's probably going to happen, the point that you're making that, you know, how does it go wrong?

metadata.title: Podcast: Stuart Russell: Long-Term Future of Artificial Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #9

body.input: A valid question without that, without an answer to that question, then you're stuck with what I call the guerrilla problem, which is, you know, the problem that the guerrillas face.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stuart Russell: Long-Term Future of Artificial Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #9

body.input: Right. They made something more intelligent than them, namely us a few million years ago.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stuart Russell: Long-Term Future of Artificial Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #9

body.input: And now, now they're in deep doo doo.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stuart Russell: Long-Term Future of Artificial Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #9

body.input: So there's really nothing they can do. They've lost the control.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stuart Russell: Long-Term Future of Artificial Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #9

body.input: They failed to solve the control problem of controlling humans.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stuart Russell: Long-Term Future of Artificial Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #9

body.input: And so they lost. So we don't want to be in that situation.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stuart Russell: Long-Term Future of Artificial Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #9

body.input: And if the guerrilla problem is the only formulation you have, there's not a lot you can do.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stuart Russell: Long-Term Future of Artificial Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #9

body.input: Right. Other than to say, okay, we should try to stop.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stuart Russell: Long-Term Future of Artificial Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #9

body.input: We should just not make the humans or in this case, not make the AI.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stuart Russell: Long-Term Future of Artificial Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #9

body.input: And I think that's really hard to do.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stuart Russell: Long-Term Future of Artificial Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #9

body.input: I'm not actually proposing that that's a feasible course of action.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stuart Russell: Long-Term Future of Artificial Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #9

body.input: I also think that, you know, if properly controlled AI could be incredibly beneficial.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stuart Russell: Long-Term Future of Artificial Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #9

body.input: So the but it seems to me that there's a there's a consensus that one of the major failure modes is this loss of control that we create AI systems that are pursuing incorrect objectives.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stuart Russell: Long-Term Future of Artificial Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #9

body.input: And because the AI system believes it knows what the objective is, it has no incentive to listen to us anymore, so to speak.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stuart Russell: Long-Term Future of Artificial Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #9

body.input: Right. It's just carrying out the strategy that it has computed as being the optimal solution.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stuart Russell: Long-Term Future of Artificial Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #9

body.input: And it may be that in the process, it needs to acquire more resources to increase the possibility of success or prevent various failure modes by defending itself against interference.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stuart Russell: Long-Term Future of Artificial Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #9

body.input: And so that collection of problems, I think, is something we can address.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stuart Russell: Long-Term Future of Artificial Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #9

body.input: Yes.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stuart Russell: Long-Term Future of Artificial Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #9

body.input: The other problems are, roughly speaking, misuse.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stuart Russell: Long-Term Future of Artificial Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #9

body.input: Right. So even if we solve the control problem, we make perfectly safe, controllable AI systems.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stuart Russell: Long-Term Future of Artificial Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #9

body.input: Well, why? Why does Dr. Evil going to use those?

metadata.title: Podcast: Stuart Russell: Long-Term Future of Artificial Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #9

body.input: Right. He wants to just take over the world and he'll make unsafe AI systems that then get out of control.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stuart Russell: Long-Term Future of Artificial Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #9

body.input: So that's one problem, which is sort of a, you know, partly a policing problem, partly a sort of cultural problem for the profession of how we teach people what kinds of AI systems are safe.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stuart Russell: Long-Term Future of Artificial Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #9

body.input: You talk about autonomous weapon system and how pretty much everybody agrees that there's too many ways that that can go horribly wrong.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stuart Russell: Long-Term Future of Artificial Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #9

body.input: And you have this great slaughter bots movie that kind of illustrates that beautifully.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stuart Russell: Long-Term Future of Artificial Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #9

body.input: Well, I want to talk about that. That's another.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stuart Russell: Long-Term Future of Artificial Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #9

body.input: There's another topic I'm happy to talk about.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stuart Russell: Long-Term Future of Artificial Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #9

body.input: I just want to mention that what I see is the third major failure mode, which is overuse, not so much misuse, but overuse of AI.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stuart Russell: Long-Term Future of Artificial Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #9

body.input: That we become overly dependent. So I call this the WALL-E problem.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stuart Russell: Long-Term Future of Artificial Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #9

body.input: If you've seen WALL-E, the movie, all right, all the humans are on the spaceship and the machines look after everything for them and they just watch TV and drink big gulps.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stuart Russell: Long-Term Future of Artificial Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #9

body.input: And they're all sort of obese and stupid and they sort of totally lost any notion of human autonomy.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stuart Russell: Long-Term Future of Artificial Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #9

body.input: And so in effect, this would happen like the slow boiling frog. We would gradually turn over more and more of the management of our civilization to machines as we are already doing.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stuart Russell: Long-Term Future of Artificial Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #9

body.input: And if this process continues, we sort of gradually switch from sort of being the masters of technology to just being the guests.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stuart Russell: Long-Term Future of Artificial Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #9

body.input: So we become guests on a cruise ship, which is fine for a week, but not further the rest of eternity.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stuart Russell: Long-Term Future of Artificial Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #9

body.input: And it's almost irreversible.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stuart Russell: Long-Term Future of Artificial Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #9

body.input: Once you lose the incentive to, for example, learn to be an engineer or a doctor or a sanitation operative or any other of the infinitely many ways that we maintain and propagate our civilization.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stuart Russell: Long-Term Future of Artificial Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #9

body.input: If you don't have the incentive to do any of that, you won't. And then it's really hard to recover.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stuart Russell: Long-Term Future of Artificial Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #9

body.input: And of course, AI is just one of the technologies that could that third failure mode result in that.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stuart Russell: Long-Term Future of Artificial Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #9

body.input: There's probably other technology in general detaches us from.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stuart Russell: Long-Term Future of Artificial Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #9

body.input: It does a bit, but the difference is that in terms of the knowledge to run our civilization, up to now we've had no alternative, but to put it into people's heads.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stuart Russell: Long-Term Future of Artificial Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #9

body.input: Right. And if you software with Google, I mean, so software in general, so computers in general, but the, you know, the knowledge of how, you know, how a sanitation system works, you know, that's an AI has to understand that it's no good putting it into Google.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stuart Russell: Long-Term Future of Artificial Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #9

body.input: So, I mean, we, we've always put knowledge in on paper, but paper doesn't run our civilization and only runs when it goes from the paper into people's heads again.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stuart Russell: Long-Term Future of Artificial Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #9

body.input: Right. So we've always propagated civilization through human minds and we've spent about a trillion person years doing that.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stuart Russell: Long-Term Future of Artificial Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #9

body.input: I literally, right. You, you can work it out. It's about right. There's about just over a hundred billion people who've ever lived.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stuart Russell: Long-Term Future of Artificial Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #9

body.input: And each of them has spent about 10 years learning stuff to keep their civilization going.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stuart Russell: Long-Term Future of Artificial Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #9

body.input: And so that's a trillion person years we put into this effort.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stuart Russell: Long-Term Future of Artificial Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #9

body.input: Beautiful way to describe all of civilization.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stuart Russell: Long-Term Future of Artificial Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #9

body.input: And now we're, you know, we're in danger of throwing that away. So this is a problem that AI console is not a technical problem.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stuart Russell: Long-Term Future of Artificial Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #9

body.input: It's a, you know, and if we do our job, right.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stuart Russell: Long-Term Future of Artificial Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #9

body.input: The AI systems will say, you know, the human race doesn't in the long run want to be passengers in a cruise ship.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stuart Russell: Long-Term Future of Artificial Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #9

body.input: The human race wants autonomy. This is part of human preferences.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stuart Russell: Long-Term Future of Artificial Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #9

body.input: So we, the AI systems are not going to do this stuff for you. You've got to do it for yourself.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stuart Russell: Long-Term Future of Artificial Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #9

body.input: Right. I'm not going to carry you to the top of Everest in an autonomous helicopter.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stuart Russell: Long-Term Future of Artificial Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #9

body.input: You have to climb it if you want to get the benefit and so on.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stuart Russell: Long-Term Future of Artificial Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #9

body.input: So, but I'm afraid that because we are short sighted and lazy, we're going to override the AI systems.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stuart Russell: Long-Term Future of Artificial Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #9

body.input: And, and there's an amazing short story that I recommend to everyone that I talk to about this called the machine stops.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stuart Russell: Long-Term Future of Artificial Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #9

body.input: Written in 1909 by Ian Forster, who, you know, wrote novels about the British Empire and sort of things that became costume dramas on the BBC.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stuart Russell: Long-Term Future of Artificial Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #9

body.input: But he wrote this one science fiction story, which is an amazing.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stuart Russell: Long-Term Future of Artificial Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #9

body.input: Vision of the future. It has, it has basically iPads.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stuart Russell: Long-Term Future of Artificial Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #9

body.input: It has video conferencing. It has MOOCs.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stuart Russell: Long-Term Future of Artificial Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #9

body.input: It has computer and computer induced obesity. I mean, literally the whole thing is what people spend their time doing is giving online courses or listening to online courses and talking about ideas, but they never get out there in the real world.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stuart Russell: Long-Term Future of Artificial Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #9

body.input: They don't really have a lot of face to face contact. Everything is done online.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stuart Russell: Long-Term Future of Artificial Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #9

body.input: You know, so all the things we're worrying about now were described in the story and, and then the human race becomes more and more dependent on the machine loses knowledge of how things really run and then becomes vulnerable to collapse.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stuart Russell: Long-Term Future of Artificial Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #9

body.input: And so it's a, it's a pretty unbelievably amazing story for someone writing in 1909 to imagine all this.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stuart Russell: Long-Term Future of Artificial Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #9

body.input: Yeah. So there's very few people that represent artificial intelligence more than you, so Russell.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stuart Russell: Long-Term Future of Artificial Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #9

body.input: If you say, okay, that's very kind.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stuart Russell: Long-Term Future of Artificial Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #9

body.input: So it's all my fault.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stuart Russell: Long-Term Future of Artificial Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #9

body.input: Right.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stuart Russell: Long-Term Future of Artificial Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #9

body.input: You're often brought up as the person. Well, Stuart Russell, like the AI person is worried about this. That's why you should be worried about it.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stuart Russell: Long-Term Future of Artificial Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #9

body.input: Do you feel the burden of that? I don't know if you feel that at all. But when I talk to people like from you talk about people outside of computer science, when they think about this still Russell is worried about AI safety, you should be worried too.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stuart Russell: Long-Term Future of Artificial Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #9

body.input: Do you feel the burden of that?

metadata.title: Podcast: Stuart Russell: Long-Term Future of Artificial Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #9

body.input: I mean, in a practical sense, yeah, because I get, you know, a dozen, sometimes 25 invitations a day to talk about it, to give interviews, to write press articles and so on.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stuart Russell: Long-Term Future of Artificial Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #9

body.input: So in that very practical sense, I'm seeing that people are concerned and really interested about this.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stuart Russell: Long-Term Future of Artificial Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #9

body.input: Are you worried that you could be wrong as all good scientists are?

metadata.title: Podcast: Stuart Russell: Long-Term Future of Artificial Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #9

body.input: Of course, I worry about that all the time.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stuart Russell: Long-Term Future of Artificial Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #9

body.input: I mean, that's always been the way that I've worked, you know, is like I have an argument in my head with myself, right?

metadata.title: Podcast: Stuart Russell: Long-Term Future of Artificial Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #9

body.input: So I have some idea and then I think, okay, how could that be wrong? Or did someone else already have that idea?

metadata.title: Podcast: Stuart Russell: Long-Term Future of Artificial Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #9

body.input: So I'll go and search in as much literature as I can to see whether someone else already thought of that or even refuted it.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stuart Russell: Long-Term Future of Artificial Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #9

body.input: So, you know, I right now I'm reading a lot of philosophy because.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stuart Russell: Long-Term Future of Artificial Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #9

body.input: You know, in the form of the debates over over utilitarianism and other kinds of moral, moral formulas, shall we say.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stuart Russell: Long-Term Future of Artificial Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #9

body.input: People have already thought through.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stuart Russell: Long-Term Future of Artificial Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #9

body.input: Some of these issues, but you know what? One of the things I'm I'm not seeing in a lot of these debates is this specific idea about the importance of uncertainty in the objective.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stuart Russell: Long-Term Future of Artificial Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #9

body.input: That this is the way we should think about machines that are beneficial to humans.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stuart Russell: Long-Term Future of Artificial Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #9

body.input: So this idea of provably beneficial machines based on explicit uncertainty in the objective.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stuart Russell: Long-Term Future of Artificial Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #9

body.input: You know, it seems to be.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stuart Russell: Long-Term Future of Artificial Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #9

body.input: You know, my gut feeling is this is the core of it. It's going to have to be elaborated in a lot of different directions.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stuart Russell: Long-Term Future of Artificial Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #9

body.input: And there are a lot of.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stuart Russell: Long-Term Future of Artificial Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #9

body.input: Provably beneficial.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stuart Russell: Long-Term Future of Artificial Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #9

body.input: Yeah, but there are I mean, it has to be right. We can't afford, you know, hand wavy beneficial.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stuart Russell: Long-Term Future of Artificial Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #9

body.input: Because there are, you know, whenever we do hand wavy stuff, there are loopholes.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stuart Russell: Long-Term Future of Artificial Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #9

body.input: And the thing about super intelligent machines is they find the loopholes.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stuart Russell: Long-Term Future of Artificial Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #9

body.input: You know, just like.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stuart Russell: Long-Term Future of Artificial Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #9

body.input: You know, tax evaders. If you don't write your tax law properly, that people will find the loopholes and end up paying no tax.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stuart Russell: Long-Term Future of Artificial Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #9

body.input: And so you should think of it this way.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stuart Russell: Long-Term Future of Artificial Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #9

body.input: And in getting those definitions right.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stuart Russell: Long-Term Future of Artificial Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #9

body.input: You know, it is really a long process.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stuart Russell: Long-Term Future of Artificial Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #9

body.input: You know, so you can you can define mathematical frameworks and within that framework, you can prove mathematical theorems that yes, this will you know, this this theoretical entity will be provably beneficial to that theoretical entity.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stuart Russell: Long-Term Future of Artificial Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #9

body.input: But that framework may not match the real world in some crucial way.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stuart Russell: Long-Term Future of Artificial Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #9

body.input: So long process thinking through it, iterating and so on.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stuart Russell: Long-Term Future of Artificial Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #9
