metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: Some people asked me to say a few words on the war in Ukraine.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: I think my words are worth little, but perhaps let me try.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: I considered doing a long solo episode on this war.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: I tried several times, but it is too personal for now.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: To give you context, I've been talking to refugees, friends, loved ones in Ukraine,

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: in Russia, in Poland, Slovakia, Moldova, Romania, even UK, Germany, Canada, India, China, and

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: of course the United States.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: Some of them crying or angry or confused or scared.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: I'm helping as best as I can privately, and I'm hoping to help in the future by traveling

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: to Ukraine and Russia and celebrating the humanity and the beauty of the people in this

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: region.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: This was all set up both for Ukraine and Russia trips before 2022, including conversations

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: with scientists, artists, athletes, leaders, and just, quote, regular folks who are equally

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: if not more fascinating to me.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: For now, it has become much more difficult, but I'll keep trying to find a way.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: I was born in the Soviet Union.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: My roots are both Ukrainian and Russian.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: And today, and until the day I die, I'm an American.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: I'm proud of all of this.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: I hope to keep celebrating the culture and the incredible human beings that make up these

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: nations and humanity as a whole.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: We're all one people.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: We're in this together.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: That's how I feel about the people of these nations.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: Now let me speak about those in the seats of power.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: I condemn all actions of leaders who play geopolitical games on the world stage disregarding

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: the costs paid in human suffering on the scale of millions.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: For this reason, I condemn Vladimir Putin's invasion of Ukraine.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: And I condemn many of the military interventions by the superpowers of the world, including

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: by my country, the country I love, the United States.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: But after World War II has intervened in over 40 nations, with many studies finding that

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: the United States is culpable for an unfathomable number of civilian deaths.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: I condemn all heads of state who needlessly wage wars, watching young men and women burn

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: in the fires they started.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: I don't understand how humans can be so cruel to each other.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: Or rather, I understand, but I believe in a future world where this is no longer true.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: Let me also say a few words of what I hope to do with this podcast.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: I want to explore the full complexity and beauty of human nature.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: I believe each of us are capable of good and evil.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: And I want to understand how the mind and the circumstance lead one to choose the former

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: path or the latter.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: And I believe conversation is one of the best ways to work toward this understanding.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: For that, I think I have to not only talk to the most inspiring humans in the world,

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: but also to the most controversial.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: I will speak with many people who I disagree with.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: Politicians, activists, CEOs, heads of state with very different opinions on the world.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: I will try hard to challenge their ideas without closing my mind to the depth and complexity

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: of their perspective and their humanity.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: My presence in the same room with wildly different people will make it easy for the media and

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: the internet to pick and choose clips and snapshots attacking me for being a shill for

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: one side or the other.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: I can't defend this point, except to say that I'm a shill for no one.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: And that I hope you see the strength of my integrity that I won't be influenced by any

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: of them no matter how rich, powerful, or charismatic they are.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: Like the poem If by Roger Kipling says,

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: This is a really, really important thing to me that I try to live by.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: That all human beings count with me the same.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: People have criticized me for wanting to have some of these conversations, like with Vladimir

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: Putin and Vladimir Zelensky, and for times in the past speaking about them without the

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: seriousness the topic deserves.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: For this, I would sincerely like to apologize.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: I'm disappointed, even ashamed, of my frequent ineliquence on these topics.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: I will work hard to do better.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: When I'm joking, it should be clear that it's a joke, and hopefully actually funny.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: When I'm being serious, I should speak with care and rigor.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: I've now done many hundreds of hours of podcast conversation.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: Despite my frequent failures and speaking, I hope you know where my heart is.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: Unfortunately, I think people will take clips of me and use them to attack me.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: This will happen more and more.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: I guess there's nothing I can do but send them my love.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: In the meantime, try to be a better person and a better interviewer.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: Let me also say that I like humor, especially dark humor.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: I like being silly and not taking myself seriously.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: I will keep taking risks with that, all with the goal of having fun and celebrating humanity

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: at its most absurd and most beautiful.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: I will occasionally dress up in strange and weird outfits to celebrate the absurdity of

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: life.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: I will hang out, break bread, and joke with all kinds of people.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: I don't have to agree with them to laugh with them in order to escape for brief moments

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: the tension, the conflict, the hatred in the world.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: Humor just might save this little chaotic little civilization of ours.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: I love the Ukrainian people.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: I love the Russian people.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: Of course, I love my fellow Americans, Californians and Midwesterners, New Yorkers and Texans.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: I love humans.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: I love life.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: And I want to share that love with others, with you.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: If I mess it up, I'm really, really sorry.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: I'm trying my best.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: I have no agenda and no one telling me what to do.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: I feel like the luckiest guy in the world to have all these opportunities.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: And I'm deeply grateful to be alive and to share that joy with other amazing people around

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: me.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: Thank you for your support.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: For all the love you've sent my way, I will work my ass off to not disappoint you.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: I love you all.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: This is the Lex Friedman podcast.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: To support it, please check out our sponsors in the description.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: And now here's my conversation with David Walthby.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: Let's start with a big question.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: According to Judaism, who is God?

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: It's difficult because Judaism, like any tradition that is thousands of years old and encompasses

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: so many different lands and languages and thinkers, it doesn't give a single answer

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: to even simple questions.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: And to large questions, it certainly doesn't give a single answer.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: Although Judaism was responsible for introducing the monotheistic idea to the world, it doesn't

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: mean that it's one idea.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: So if you take Maimonides, the greatest sage in the Jewish tradition, medieval philosopher,

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: he would say that God is an omnipotent, benevolent, intangible, unimaginable God.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: In fact, he said you can't say what God is, only what God is not, because you have to

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: emphasize, could talk more about that, but basically you have to emphasize the unknowability

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: of God.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: You have a modern philosopher like Heschel who says that God is a God of pathos, a God

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: of deep feeling, which probably would make Maimonides shiver if he heard such a description.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: And if you look in the Bible, God is always regretting or having human emotions.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: So there are so many different kinds of depictions and ideas.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: And there is this tremendous tension between transcendence and imminence.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: That is, in the Jewish tradition, God is exquisitely close, God is imminent.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: In the Talmud's words, God is as close as your mouth is to your ear.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: In other words, whatever you say, God hears it.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: And yet at the same time, God is unfathomably distant.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: Sometimes when I speak to high schoolers, I will say in the Jewish tradition, think

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: of it this way.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: When you were two years old, you had no idea what it was to be a 15 year old.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: Not only did you not know, but you didn't know what you didn't know.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: We conceive of God as being more, the distance between God and human beings is far greater

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: than the distance between a two year old and a 15 year old.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: So when we speak about God, we have to acknowledge how limited we really are.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: So okay, you laid out a lot of fascinating things on the table.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: So one, the knowability of God, then this idea of deep feeling, which again, can God

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: be operating in the space of feelings too.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: So not just the mouth and the ear of the senses.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: Can God be known?

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: Can God be felt by this three year old in the analogy versus the teenager?

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: So I will take refuge in a beautiful phrase by from Martin Buber, another Jewish theologian.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: He said, God cannot be expressed.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: God can only be addressed.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: In other words, you can speak to God, you can feel a sense of God, but can you begin

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: to comprehend or know God?

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: No.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: I'm not going to give Kospi, I'm pulling in a couple of early Jewish philosophers.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: He said, to know God, I would have to be God.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: But can we get close?

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: Is it useful or is it a distraction to visualize things, to embody, to create, to attach to

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: the stories some kind of visualizations in our mind?

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: For example, gender, he versus she, things like this, or old man in the sky kind of feeling.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: So it's almost inevitable, but I think ultimately you try to transcend it.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: This was the great, we just read this actually in synagogue, the story of the golden calf.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: And the story is that human beings found it impossible to not have a visualization because

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: they had just come from Egypt and in the world of pagan worship, everything is, it's not

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: that pagans thought that idol was actually God, but it represented visually what God

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: was.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: And along comes this idea that God is actually not capable of being visualized, which is

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: very difficult and it stretches the bounds of human comprehension, maybe even breaks

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: them.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: So would you say the proper way to operate as a human in relation to God is humility

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: and that you're screwed, you're not able to basically know anything, almost anything?

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: Well the reason that you're the salvation of this is that you can't, that you can't,

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: I was going to say the reason you're not screwed, but then I thought somebody might be upset

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: at a rabbi saying that.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: So I didn't say it and have not said it.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: But the reason you're not is that you don't have to have a comprehension of God.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: You have to have a relationship to God and those are not the same.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: I mean to draw an analogy that is not far from perfect as most analogies are, but this

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: one especially, you have relationships with people who are mysteries to you.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: You're a mystery to yourself.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: You can live and love somebody for 50 years and they can say something that surprises

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: you because ultimately we are trapped in here.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: And when a child first says I, we call that individuation, but what that really means

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: is I now know that I am cut off from the minds of all other children and all other people.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: And so you have with God a more intimate relationship because you can believe that God is, you are

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: known by God and you have a relationship to God despite the fact that you can't know God

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: just as you can't know others.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: And someone would say to have a good relationship, you want to be constantly surprised.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: Right.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: You don't want to know the thing.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: Well, the world that God created is constantly surprising.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: And by the way, the caveat to this, I had all these debates with Christopher Hitchens

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: and he would always say that God is a greater tyrant than North Korea because it continues

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: after your death.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: And the idea of being known by God is after all frightening if you think God knows what

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: I think and so on, if your image of God is unloving.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: Can we jump to this?

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: You had friendships and conversations with a lot of the fascinating figures of the past

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: 20, 30 years of the great intellectuals, one of which perhaps one of the greats is Christopher

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: Hitchens.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: What have you learned from your conversation, your friendship?

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: So there are a lot of views he held that I really did not agree with, but he was a remarkable

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: person.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: That was a good line about North Korea.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: He was full of incredibly good lines.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: Well, one of the things I learned was you can't win a debate with Christopher Hitchens.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: One of the reasons you can't win is because he has this British baritone and this ready

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: wit that you can't triumph over laughter.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: It doesn't matter if your argument is better.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: If your quip is better, you win.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: And so I remember once we were arguing about free will and he said, well, I choose to believe

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: in it.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: And I laughed and that was despite the fact that that's not really an argument.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: Or like, I have free will because I don't have a choice.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: Right, exactly.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: And people should watch your conversation with him.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: It's great.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: I mean, it's a kind of David versus Goliath situation and you're quite masterful at using

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: charisma and sweet talking Christopher Hitchens.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: I also genuinely liked him.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: I mean, I spent a three hour limousine ride with him from one debate to another from LA

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: to San Diego and the entire time he said, we just can't talk about religion.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: So we talked about literature and he gave me a long lecture about scotch.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: He was inexhaustible.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: I mean, not only did he...

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: I began, I wrote a couple of obituaries about him and one I began with the historian Keith

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: Thomas said there are two ways of achieving immortality by doing things worth remembering

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: or saying things worth remembering.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: And by that standard, he did both.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: I mean, he went all around the world to all sorts of danger zones.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: He knew like the best bars everywhere from Kuala Lumpur to Beirut to LA and he could

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: drink all night and write a 2000 word essay on the poetry of Yeats and go to sleep.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: I remember before one of our debates in Boston, he was at the bar and he said, come have a

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: drink.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: And I said, I'm going to have a drink before I go to debate with you.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: What are you crazy?

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: And he said, just have a beer, it's water.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: So he really was a constant inexhaustible fountain of intrigue and interest.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: What kind of things, if you can remember, if you can mention, if you can admit to have

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: him enlightening you or helping you change your mind about something in this world.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: So I think, unrelated to Scotch.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: Oh yeah, unrelated to Scotch.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: He convinced me that the idea, I mean, I had my doubts about it and have my doubts about

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: it, but he convinced me through many debates and not only he, that the idea that religion

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: makes people better is not, it's not ipso facto wrong, but it's a much, much more complicated

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: argument than I wished it to be.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: So he is, however you conceive of the term beauty, he's one of those, one of the more

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: beautiful humans.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: Yes.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: This weird little earth produced.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: So how do you explain the atheism combined with such a beautiful mind?

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: So from your perspective of a man of faith, how do you think about that?

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: So of the atheists that I have debated, I think about all of them somewhat differently.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: So I think that in some deep way, for example, Sam Harris is a religious personality.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: I don't even think that he would, he wouldn't like the word religious, but I don't even

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: think that he would take issue with that.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: I think that he would say his is a purely material based spirituality, but I mean his

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: orientation towards meditation and appreciation of Buddhism, there's something deeply seeking

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: spiritual about him.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: With Hitchens, I honestly, and I know that some of his fans will really not like this.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: It's not that he was any kind of closet believer, certainly not at all, but I almost feel as

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: though he was less a passionate arguer against religion than he was, first of all, extremely

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: upset by the forms that religion took in this world.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: And then once he trained his intellectual howitzers on a target, he had so much fun

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: inventing new arguments and attacking it that I really believe he gets carried away sometimes

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: by his own eloquence and intellectual range.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: So for example, the idea that you would call a book that religion poisons everything.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: I think he did that deliberately provocatively so that he could defend a proposition that

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: obviously is indefensible, that it poisons everything.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: So I don't know.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: I think he had tremendous joie de vivre.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: That's what sums him up.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: This guy loved life in all of its manifestations and arguing against something that someone

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: else believed was one of his greatest joys.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: Yeah.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: And of course, the practical aspect of that, he just saw the powerful and he challenged

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: them with humor.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: Absolutely.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: And you could argue perhaps that humor is the highest form of what humanity can achieve.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: Sometimes maybe us little humans take things a little too seriously.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: Then sometimes we need to just laugh at it all, laugh at ourselves.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: And that's probably the purest form of wisdom.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: You know, Auden, the poet said, among the people that I like or admire, I can find no

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: common quality.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: But among those I love, I can.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: All of them make me laugh.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: There you have it.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: Speaking of people that make you laugh, Sam Harris.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: Where's your fundamental disagreements and agreements with Sam?

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: Sam believes that religion is intellectually indefensible.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: He really believes it, like deep in his soul.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: And he gets angry at the idea that a proposition should be unchallenged if it offends his sense

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: of logic.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: Yeah.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: So he cannot move on until this is dealt with.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: In fact, I mean, I did a podcast with Eric Weinstein and then Sam did one.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: And Sam said, when I heard your podcast with David Wolpe, I learned stuff about what he

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: those unfounded assertions without challenging them and you just let them go.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: And I think that there was something too that was like, he finds it hard to have a conversation

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: about religion that doesn't arouse his real ire about the harm that he thinks religion

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: does in the world.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: Faith.

body.input: Yeah, faith.

body.input: I mean, they're both capable of separating their contempt for religion from the people

body.input: that they have sitting in front of them.

body.input: You mean Christopher Hitchens and Sam Harris?

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: Yes, both of them.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: Okay.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: So let me, you mentioned Eric Weinstein.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: People should listen to your conversation with Eric as a fascinating one is great.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: It's non-standard.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: It just goes all over the place and this humor and wit is great.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: So one interesting aspect that I also learned, perhaps not about you, but about Eric, about

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: both, but Eric has a similar thing with Jordan Peterson, which is if you ask them, do they

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: believe in God?

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: I think they answer, they're not comfortable answering that question or they might say

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: no, but they're usually just not comfortable answering that question.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: But there's a kind of sense that they would like to live life, a religious life as if

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: God exists.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: I think that's exactly right.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: I think first of all, Eric has a really deep appreciation of the Jewish tradition.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: I don't know Peterson.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: I've read his stuff and I've reviewed his stuff and so on.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: But I think that Jungians are in their very approach.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: They believe that myth is the way the world works.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: And so it's not that big a leap to God, but there's still a distance there.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: Is it possible to have your cake and eat it too?

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: Is it possible to have the depth of a religious life without believing in God?

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: How do you make sense of Eric Weinstein's devout life within the tradition?

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: I honestly think he believes in God, but doesn't believe in God and it's oscillating like it's

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: a quantum mechanical system of some sort.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: Schrodinger's God.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: And I think Eric's not indifferent to God.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: And it's different than Christianity.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: I've had this conversation many times because you can be very Jewish and have deep doubts

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: about theological questions because Judaism isn't a religion.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: It's a religious family.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: And so you're born Jewish.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: Like if I said to you tomorrow, if I was Christian and I said, oh, I believe in Jesus today and

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: then tomorrow I didn't, I'm not Christian anymore.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: But if tomorrow I said, oh, I don't believe all this stuff, I'm still Jewish.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: So it's a more complicated system.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: Having said that though, I think it's very hard to sustain over generations without some

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: belief that the source of it is beyond ourselves.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: And in that sense, as in many others, Eric is unique.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: through the generations.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: So without that, the traditions crumble.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: It's a very interesting idea and very interesting argument for devout faith, which is it's a

body.input: Otherwise, like traditions fall apart.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: On the other hand, you do see tradition.

body.input: Thanksgiving, one of my favorite.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: So I would say traditions that are demanding fall apart, traditions that require turkey

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: might not fall apart, but traditions that make demands of you that are countercultural

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: or are hard, they fall apart.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: I think I need to introduce you to some Thanksgiving dinners that are quite demanding.

body.input: Getting the family together.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: First of all, I'm a vegetarian, so I'm tough to have at Thanksgiving dinner.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: But there's a comedian named Kathy Landsman who one year, I heard this on the radio and

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: For some reason that hit hard.

body.input: I've seen pictures in concentration camps of people I don't know or whose words I haven't

body.input: really felt and gone through.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: But for some reason, here's just a normal person, like a normal body laying there.

body.input: That was him.

body.input: And you see, you can see his face, but at the same time you see that this is an amazing...

body.input: And I think what's so disturbing about it is exactly what you were saying is I've seen

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: I mean, it's projection, but it seemed like this perhaps is also just combining with Man's

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: by human beings to each other?

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: Is it religion?

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: Is it the thirst for power?

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: Is it the madness of crowds somehow carrying us forward?

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: I mean, for me, it's multi-causal.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: I don't think there's one reason.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: One of the things especially there has to do with the special nature of antisemitism,

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: which is let's put that to one side for the moment.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: The second is I think human beings are fundamentally split.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: They are mostly good except when put under certain pressures.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: My first explanation for hatred is as follows.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: Go to a playground.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: What happens when a new kid comes on the playground?

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: Do the other kids say, oh, let's go share our toys with the new kid?

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: No.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: They say, oh, who's that stranger and let's go get them because otherness is built into

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: our genetic.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: I mean, we're tribal by nature and we see people form tribes all the time of different

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: kinds.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: I asked you before if you were a chess player and when I was a kid and playing in tournaments

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: and I didn't do it for that long and I didn't do it that well, but when I was, it was like

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: the whole world was divided into people who could play chess and people who couldn't play

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: chess, which is ridiculous if you think about it as though that's the way you divide the

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: world, but we tend to do that.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: The Jews were always the identifiable other.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: There were Frenchmen and Jews.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: There were Russians and Jews.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: There were Germans and Jews.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: The great blessing of America is that there's no identifiable other quite that way is that

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: there's all these minorities and no, there's not an American and a something, but once

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: you have that identifiable other and you have a long history of blaming that identifiable

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: other for all the ills that befall you.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: Of course, people still do try to form, you said America, they still try to form other,

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: I mean, immigrant versus been here for a generation.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: There's so many ways to slice it.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: We still try to find ways.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: It's just more difficult in America because there's so many sub-tribes, hierarchies of

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: tribes and upon tribes.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: You're absolutely right.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: And I was moving fast because I didn't want to get bogged down in all the very difficult.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: It's true.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: I tried.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: You're hoping I wouldn't mention that tribalism happens in America.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: I was skating some.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: When you're on thin ice, your safety is in your speed.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: So I was trying to move fast.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: But for most of history in Eastern Western Europe, not obviously in Asia, but in Eastern

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: Western Europe, Jews were the ones who like, they're not like us.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: They're clearly not like us.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: And in addition, there's a peculiar quality and I don't know, I wonder what you'll think

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: of this explanation.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: There's a peculiar quality to anti-Semitism that is unlike any other hatred that I know

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: of, which is Jews are both superhuman and subhuman.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: They're vermin.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: The Nazis thought of them as vermin and yet they control the world.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: And there was an English scholar named Hyman McApee who said the reason that that's so

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: is the myth that Jews killed God.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: They killed Jesus.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: And to kill a God, you have to be superhumanly evil.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: You can't just be bad.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: Otherwise you can't kill a God.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: So there is some like supercharged evil sense that people got from that about Jews that

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: still in here.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: Yeah, that's true.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: A lot of the way we formulate the other in terms of tribes is often they're subhuman

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: and they're here to steal our resources like on the playground.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: But to be both is a fascinating construction.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: Do you agree with Solzhenitsyn that all of us have the capacity for evil?

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: 100% runs through every human heart.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: I have no doubt about it.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: And I know as you probably do, but I probably know more both because of what I do and because

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: I have lived a lot longer than you.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: I know a lot of religious leaders who people thought or think are above the human and they

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: are emphatically not.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: They're not.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: Some of them have done horrible things and they've used their position to do horrible

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: things.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: And it's because there is no perfect saint.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: There's no, you know, I mean, all through history, you discover all these saintly characters

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: that we worship, the people who actually knew them around them, some liked them and some

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: didn't.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: People are complicated, all of us.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: And the tough thing is, the thing that's the toughest for me is it's not very always clear

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: what is good and what is evil.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: Because certainly if you just look at history and it's not always propaganda, I really believe

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: that some part of Stalin thought he was doing good legitimately.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: And it makes you ask a question of yourself.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: For those of us who want to do good in the world, am I actually doing good?

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: And that's a really difficult question.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: So like in the technology sphere, for example, in this dream of creating technology that

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: will do some good, am I actually doing good?

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: So I have a question about that myself, not about Stalin.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: I'm sure that Stalin thought so.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: Stalin does not strike me from what I know of him as somebody given to a lot of self-doubt.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: But the question with AI to me is actually it goes back to the God question, which is

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: if we have an appreciation of the limitations of our own intelligence, that we know that

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: just like we can only hear certain things and see certain colors, how much of the world

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: is inaccessible to us because of the way our brains are constructed?

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: How can we possibly have any confidence that we can create things that in certain ways

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: are far more intelligent than we are and control them the way we think is best?

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: Seems to me a hubris that might end up being destructive.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: Definitely.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: Well, any sentence with the word hubris in it is going to end badly when implemented

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: at scale.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: But there is also beauty.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: So if you approach it with humility, there is a sense, I don't want to over romanticize

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: it, but there is a legged robot right behind you, which is hilarious.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: So there is a magic, I don't have kids, I would love to have kids, but there is a magic

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: to bringing robots to life that it feels like you are a mini God because you just breathe

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: life into an entity that operates in this world, especially when they have legs and

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: they move in this way.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: That's in the case of the four legged robot is like a dog that I think I don't think I'm

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: over romanticizing it.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: The feeling is like you would with a child.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: You just gave birth like, holy crap, this is a living thing.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: I wonder what he or she are thinking about.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: By the way, I'm not at all insensible to how remarkable it must feel to create that.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: I'm actually worried in part about how remarkable it feels to create that because to maintain

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: humility and perspective when it's such a fantastic thing is what's difficult.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: I think also because creativity is both part of what it is to be human and it's very much

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: part of the legacy of Western civilization and the legacy of having a creator God.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: If you have a tradition where God is known primarily through what God creates, so the

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: first debate I ever had since we talked about humor and God and creating, let me give you

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: my one God creating joke because the first debate I ever had on religion and science

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: was with Stephen Jay Gould.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: It was wonderful because he had a deep interest in religion and his interest was actually

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: not to say religion is terrible.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: I started with this joke and I think it made the debate go a little bit easier.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: The time has come when human beings can do everything that God can do and a scientist

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: looks up at heaven and says, God, look, you are great in your day and we thank you for

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: everything you did, but now we don't need you.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: God says, really, you don't need me?

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: He says, no, we can do everything you did.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: God says, everything?

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: Human being says, yeah, we can do everything.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: God says, okay, can you create a human being?

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: The scientist goes, yeah.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: God says, from dirt?

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: The scientist goes, yeah.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: He says, okay, let me see.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: The scientist reaches down, scoops up some dirt and God says, get your own dirt.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: The idea is that a creator God impels us to create too.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: Let me bring up Nietzsche who proclaimed that God is dead.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: His belief in God slowly disappearing from our world, do you think?

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: What kind of impact does that have on society?

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: You wrote that religion is not our enemy before the Western faiths captured the heart of our

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: world that was cruelty, carnage and destruction.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: In the 20th century when religion ceased to be a force of international politics, the

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: scale of human slaughter was far beyond anything human beings have ever known.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: What is the world like when we take religion out of it?

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: I think Nietzsche was largely right.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: It wasn't a statement about God.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: It was a statement about God's presence in the world.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: I think that that's largely true that God is not a force in a lot of Western society.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: I believe that if the force of nihilism has no clear counter without an idea that we're

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: all here for a purpose and that our lives are inherently meaningful and that there's

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: a God who wishes us to be better.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: I worry a lot about it.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: I think that the optimism that things are just going to get better and better is what

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: one philosopher called cut flower ethics.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: That is, we're still living off the morals that religion gave us, but now that they're

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: separate from the soil that gave birth to them, I see them wilting.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: So it's kind of optimism for the future of human civilization you think is in part grounded

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: in a religious society.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: I really do believe that.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: It was religion that the Greeks looked back at the golden age of the past.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: It was the Jews who said, no, the golden age is in the future.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: It's the Messiah.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: I think that that idea that we're moving towards something better, which I really believe humanity

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: can do and absent destroying ourselves will do.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: I mean, I'm very excited about the technology that I won't live to see.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: I think it's fantastic.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: That excitement is a kind of religious excitement because there's a reason to preserve this

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: whole thing.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: Absolutely.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: Because I really think, I know this sounds absurdly anthropomorphic, but I really think

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: God is cheering us on.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: I feel like this is why we're here.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: We're here to grow in soul and to grow each other in soul.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: Yeah.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: So what do you think the world, so if we just think of this force of nihilism that's contending

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: with the force of faith-based optimism, what do you make of the atrocities in the 20th

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: century?

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: Do you think at its core, it's part of human nature and has nothing to do with religion

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: or not religion?

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: Or do you think you can assign this kind of nihilistic view of the world?

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: I think it has to do with a religion that doesn't make ethical demands.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: That is, for Stalin and for Hitler, they both had religions, in a sense, but they were religions

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: that didn't make ethical demands for the other.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: I mean, 36 times the Torah talks about the stranger.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: The point is, it's trying to educate people away from their natural inclination towards

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: distrusting and disliking the other.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: It's a lot of work.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: That's really difficult to do.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: But if you have a tribal passion and not a universal ethic, then you're in trouble.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: Well, the Jewish tribe is a very strong tribe.
