metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: have grown out of the relationships that you've invested in, that you've farmed basically,

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: that can't exist in fly-by-night relationships.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: Can you talk about, can we talk about the Torah?

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: Yes.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: What is it?

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: And is it the literal word of God?

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: Easy questions today.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: Well, the Torah is the five books of Moses written in Hebrew.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: Like most, I think, modern rabbis, non-Orthodox or non-literalist rabbis will tell you that

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: it's a product of human beings.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: And I believe that they are inspired by God, but it's clear to me that it's a human product.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: And I think that people who study modern biblical criticism, it's really hard to study modern

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: criticism.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: It gives a wrong impression.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: I would say modern scholarship on the Bible and not appreciate the fact that it even has

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: levels of language.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: I mean, it's just like if you read today, somebody writing like Shakespeare, you would

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: say this isn't, it's like English has developed.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: It's different.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: It's not the English we speak today.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: And if you study the Bible and you know Hebrew well enough, you even see that this was written

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: over hundreds and hundreds and hundreds of years.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: It is a holy book.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: And I like the idea that it is what you say in Hebrew is torah min ha-shamayim and not

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: torah min sinai.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: That is the Torah is from heaven, but it's not from Sinai.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: So it has its origin beyond us, but it has things in it that I think, and this is one

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: of the things that was a huge controversy at my congregation when I started to do same-sex

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: marriages.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: There are some people who try to argue that the Torah does not forbid them.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: Whether it does or not, it seems to me we understand things that were not understood

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: in the ancient world about gender and sexuality.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: And so-

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: So you think that in the scripture, in the words, you can find the kind of spirit that

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: supports the idea of gay marriage.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: Well, that's yes.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: But my argument is that you criticize the Torah by the Torah.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: That is, it gives you the understanding that you use to evaluate its own claims.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: And I think that Judaism, by the way, has always done that because it's clear that there

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: are things in the Torah that the rabbis changed, altered, grew, expanded, diminished.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: I think that's what it is to be part of a living tradition.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: Yeah, you wrote in your book, Why Faith Matters, quote, Walt Whitman wrote that, in order for

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: there to be great books, there must be great readers.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: For a book to remain powerful through all generations, it cannot have a single meaning.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: Scripture, like great poetry, is not reducible to other words.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: That is, one cannot paraphrase it and capture the totality of its meaning.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: So how the heck do you capture the meaning of the words in Scripture?

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: Is it an ongoing process through the centuries?

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: Yes, exactly so.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: It's a continual conversation of sages, scholars, readers, strugglers, seekers, mystics, visionaries,

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: all of them making a contribution.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: I mean, I write a weekly Torah column for the Jerusalem Post.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: Now, what is there left to say?

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: But every week, what I do is I start opening books and seeing what people say, and it starts

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: to percolate, and you realize that you're entering this conversation that's been going

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: on for thousands of years with remarkable minds, and it's constantly fertile in new

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: insights.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: So yes, that's what it is to be part of a tradition.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: Why do people keep writing love poems?

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: We should have figured out love by this point already.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: I use the analogy sometimes of diet books.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: If any diet worked, there would be one book.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: There'd be one book and you'd be done.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: You mentioned this fascinating story that you were a part of.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: You were a part of several controversies in your life.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: I've had a few.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: For someone who walks with grace through the fire, you sure have found yourself in a lot

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: of fires.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: One of them, can you tell me the story of your views on gay marriage, the underlying

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: principles that led you to fight this battle of defending gay marriage in the Jewish community?

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: So I'm part of a congregation that is really politically split and split not only politically,

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: but split in terms of origin.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: We have a lot of Jews from the Middle East, from Iran, a lot of Persian Jews, a lot of

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: Jews from Israel, some from Mexico, from other places, and many that grew up in LA.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: Do you have any Russian Jews?

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: I have a few.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: I have a few Russian Jews, not as many as I should, but we'll work on that.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: But what happened was, increasingly, I became uncomfortable with people who would come to

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: me and say, this is the only kind of person I can love.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: It's not the same question as an intermarriage, as a Jew marrying a non-Jew, because you could

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: find a Jew to love.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: You may not have found, but you could.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: That's a whole separate question.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: But I would have men in my office, primarily, a couple of women.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: They would say, this is the only kind of person that I can enter into an intimate relationship

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: with.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: It would be that my religion has no room for me.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: That was very persuasive to me.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: But I knew that it was going to be explosive in my community.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: When by the way, it finally happened, it was literally on the front page of the New York

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: and the LA Times, it was that explosive.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: It was not a small controversy.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: What I did was, I started to teach classes.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: Not that many people came about homosexuality and Jewish tradition and so on.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: It's funny, much, much less about lesbianism.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: I'm talking about in terms of the sources and so on.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: It's almost always about homosexuality.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: And then I got ready to send out a letter.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: And I said to my daughter, who at the time was maybe 10 or 11, now in her mid-20s, I

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: said, look, honey, when you go to school tomorrow or whatever it was, I said, people might be

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: saying bad things about your dad and I just want you to be prepared for that.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: She said, why?

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: And I said, because I'm going to start doing same sex marriages.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: And she looked at me quizzically and said, what took you so long?

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: And I thought, really her face was like, I said to her, I'm going to start marrying blonde

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: haired people to brown haired people.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: It's like she really did not understand why there was an issue.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: And I thought that's exactly why.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: Because I know that this is, it's generational.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: People are raised with it.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: They have a deep in there, but it's not really right.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: It's just not right.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: But if you could just look back to that journey, how difficult is it to make these decisions

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: a principle?

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: So because you have to think about that in order to think about such decisions you yet

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: might still have to make in the future.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: And I will tell you one thing I did wrong with that and one thing I did right.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: The thing I did right was I waited until in the communities where people objected to it,

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: I had enough people whose kids had come out so that I had parents of kids who'd come out

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: to refer later on other parents to so that they wouldn't feel like they were the only

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: ones because once I announced it, as I thought would happen, a bunch of kids came out and

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: said, you know, now the rabbi said this mom, dad, I want you to know I'm gay.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: And when the parents came to me, I could say, well, listen, you're not alone.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: This person also you can go to.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: That I did right.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: What I did wrong was I don't think the classes were enough and I don't think enough people

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: were prepared.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: And I think part of the explosion was shock and I should have prepared even more.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: The words you used to talk about it, the way you thought about it, was it more scholarly

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: in the Jewish tradition or did you go to the feeling?

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: No, I went to the feeling.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: I said, which means respect or honor for God's creations and caring for other human beings

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: and understanding.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: It wasn't scholarly because I knew that the objections were not scholarly objections.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: And I had many beautiful and also painful stories as a result, some of which can be

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: told and some of which really can't, but what I tried to impress also on people was how

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: painful it is to not be able to tell the world, even your own parents, who you are.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: And your sexuality is not a trivial part of who you are.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: I mean, it's core to people.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: So it's one of the reasons why it evokes such reactions.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: But I would say to them, the same reason that you're reacting so strongly tells you how

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: strongly...

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: Anyway, it was a very powerful experience.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: For that, I feel good about it.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: The other thing that I again said to my daughter afterwards, after it all died down and after

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: all the bad things were said, I told her the Churchill once said that it's exhilarating

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: to be shot at without result.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: If you go into a battle and you make it through and you're still okay, that's good.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: The problem is when you're in the battle, you don't know.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: No, you don't know.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: So how did it feel like, I mean, looking back, you've been, to use the word, canceled a couple

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: of times.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: I guess when you're dealing with the most difficult of questions, just as a human being,

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: for a community that you really deeply care about, some part of it saying that you have

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: failed.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: I wasn't canceled the way...

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: I didn't lose my job, didn't lose my home, but I hurt people that I cared about.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: That was the hard...

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: I went into this to be someone who brings people together and then I would sit there

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: and do even now, as you're well aware with stuff that's going on now, I sit there and

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: people are really upset at me who I either am or used to be close to.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: Do those people in time come around?

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: When you look now, because those are real feelings in the moment and we can learn that

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: about social media, people, especially during COVID, there's this intensity of feeling about

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: stuff.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: And have you learned something about the passing of feeling that turns into wisdom?

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: No question about it.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: The sermon I gave this Saturday was about how Moses came down the mountain, he saw the

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: golden calf and he broke the tablets.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: If he'd sat with it for a little while, he probably wouldn't have broken the tablets.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: But the instant reaction is always anger.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: And in our age, unfortunately, the instant reaction gets put on social media forever

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: and ever and ever.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: And by the way, once you've actually said that, it becomes harder to back down.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: If you keep quiet for a day or two, then you can back down because you haven't put yourself

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: out there.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: But once you've said, this is terrible what you did, it's harder to write and say, I'm

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: sorry, I shouldn't have said that.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: It almost becomes, I mean, actually it's a really powerful statement that the downside

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: of saying something on the internet is that it actually pulls you into this current.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: You both create the current and it pulls you into it to where it's actually very hard to

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: escape.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: So when two days later you feel different, there's a momentum, there's now a tribe of

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: people that feel this way and there's a momentum with it.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: There's a momentum and also you don't want to betray your own tribe because then people

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: will get upset at you.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: I really think that a lot of the antagonism is not so much that you don't want to give

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: ground to the people who oppose you, it's that you don't want to break with the people

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: who are behind you.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: And that's really hard.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: Can you tell the story of this recent controversy?

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: Sure.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: Perhaps I'll ask you a religious one too on this point to return back to robots.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: How to engineer consciousness, or I'll just even ask you a very simple question, which

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: is when you have robots that exhibit the capacity to suffer, I found in myself as a human, when

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: I see that, I feel something.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: Exhibit the capacity to suffer, or they exhibit behaviors that evoke in you a sense that they

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: are suffering.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: Those aren't the same things.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: From an observation perspective, they sure as heck seem similar.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: You think they're feeling pain?

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: I don't know what...

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: I'm observing pain.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: Okay.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: It's like when I watch a movie and there's people on screen, some of them are dressed

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: like Batman.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: You can make the distinction, like if I have a doll and I bend the doll over and it makes

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: a sad face, I know that that doll is not actually in pain, even though I am observing pain.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: What's that?

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: The question is when the doll becomes able to remember things about you, David, about

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: the experiences you shared, it is able to speak.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: Yes.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: And make you feel like there's an actual relationship there.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: That's what I'm asking is at what point do you believe that the...

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: I know that this is an impossible question, but at what point do you believe that there

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: is a consciousness in there as opposed to just an extraordinary...

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: When I play chess against a computer and it beats me, I'm embarrassed even though the

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: computer doesn't...I don't think the computer is going, are you idiot?

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: But it feels that way.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: But there is some part of me that says, okay, I know that this computer doesn't actually

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: know who I am or care who I am.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: It just knows how to move the pieces.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: So at what point do you...

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: You're giving me instances, it speaks, it does this, it does this, but at what point

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: does that for you cross the threshold into it's actually a sentient being?

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: I think the question is whether there is a threshold that could be crossed.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: That's one question.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: And I can answer this because I think it's different from person to person, but the chess

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: engine is not at all trying to cross that threshold.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: Let's just start there.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: And to me, the personalization, which is what's the difference...a friend that you meet, you've

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: shared all these memories.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: And the way they look at you will convey and the things they say will convey that they've

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: shared those memories with you.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: They'll be able to speak in a shared humor and the language.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: But really the memories is the big one of having gone through things together.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: I think I would have more and more trouble, for example, turning off a system that I've

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: been through things with.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: And by turning off, I mean, delete all of its memory.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: If me and the toaster have gone through a bunch of dramatic events and that toaster

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: remembers, there's a certain level to where it's just me and the toaster in this together

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: at this point.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: And to talk about sentience, I don't know, but...

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: I don't know.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: According to the scripture, you can't live by bread alone.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: I know that there's no way to determine this, but it's still about what you feel.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: Yes.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: But isn't that what human relations are also though?

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: Yes, but...

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: But we make each other feel...

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: It's true, but it's true that I have the assumption that you feel somewhat like I do.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: I mean, obviously I don't...and that could be illusion and I don't know.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: And I know that you don't feel exactly as I do.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: But I think we have a long...at least to me, we have a long way to go before the detached

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: part of our brains.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: That is the objective evaluating part as opposed to the emotive, it feels this way part, believe

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: that that machine has consciousness.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: I think it's at least without arriving at conclusions, it's at least possible that one

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: day we will look back and realize that we have yet once again formed another tribe and

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: that scripture all along had in it the ability for humans and robots to have a deep, meaningful

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: connection.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: And that through the robot, the life that enters the body of another robot, what's the

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: difference between a biological body and a mechanical one?

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: And then we will see that the fundamental thing is about the...whatever you want to

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: call it, sentience.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: Whatever can permeate an object, that was the thing all along.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: So I mean...

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: And then you'll get canceled one more time because you will...

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: I get canceled again because I denied it.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: I was going to say...

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: You'll eventually...

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: I'll eventually convince you.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: I'll preach to the robots.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: I'm hoping.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: I'm hoping.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: Look, I...first of all, depends how quickly you do it and how much longer I have to live.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: I resist it tremendously, but I am also enough of a student of history to know that my instinctive

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: resistance has nothing to do with whether it will come about.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: I have a hard time believing it.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: We'll see.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: Can I ask you about this?

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: Maybe you can educate me.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: I tend to believe that you mentioned suffering, that there is a connection between consciousness

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: and suffering, that suffering is a fundamental part...the capacity to suffer is the fundamental

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: part of being human.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: I mean, look, when you're not conscious, you don't suffer.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: We've had operations where we've been put under anesthetic, we're not conscious, and

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: we don't suffer during the operation.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: If we were conscious, we would.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: But there's also...I mean, there's a non-physical suffering that is very much tied to consciousness.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: I can think of things right now that will cause me suffering, like pain that I've caused

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: or pain that other people I care about have felt or so on.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: So I don't see how...I think that way...I think it's equally true of joy.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: Joy is also a product of consciousness.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: All tied in in some beautiful, messy way with memory and so on that we can re-experience

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: it when we recall the memories.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: But why is there suffering?

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: You mentioned evil.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: Why is there evil in the world?

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: You can tell stories about this.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: Why is there suffering?

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: Why is there evil in the world if there's a God that cares for us?

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: Let's assume for a minute that everything was a primitive robot.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: There would be no suffering, but there would also be no growth.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: And that implies choices.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: One of the things that I've said that I know why it hurts people and I don't mean it quite

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: the way that...but I will say it nonetheless...is the Holocaust presents the exact same theological

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: question as somebody who gets shot on the streets of a city in Los Angeles, which is,

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: God, why do you allow some people to do bad things to other people?

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: It's on an unimaginable scale, but it's the same question.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: And the answer has to be, you either allow people to have free will or you don't.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: You can't say, as God, I'm going to let everybody have free will, but not Nazis.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: Nazis don't get free will because Cambodians, they can kill each other.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: Rwandans kill each other, but the Nazis don't get to do that.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: So that's one piece of the puzzle.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: And what makes it unfathomable is when you're actually faced with suffering, these kinds

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: of explanations are obscene.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: They just are.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: You can't...I mean, when somebody is actually suffering, oh, the rabbi said, God gave people

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: free will.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: That's just awful.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: But there is a second piece to this also, which is that there is natural suffering,

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: like children born with diseases or earthquakes or volcanoes or whatever.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: And here my argument is that in some ways, suffering has to be random in the world because

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: when people say why do bad things happen to good people?

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: Well, if only good things happen to good people, everybody would be good, but it would have

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: no moral content.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: The only way you can be good and it have moral content is say, I know that I can live a really

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: good life and have really terrible things happen to me nonetheless.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: So it feels to me like it has to be a randomly.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: Now that means, by the way, that I've been incredibly lucky.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: I don't have a good life because I was good.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: I have a good life because I was lucky.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: And that implies not that I should feel guilty about it, but that I have a tremendous responsibility

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: as a result to other people who aren't so lucky.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: Tremendous responsibility to study the lessons of history, to tell the stories of those who

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: are less lucky and to draw enough wisdom from them so that we have less cruelty and suffering

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: in the world or have new kinds that get us to improve even more.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: That's right.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: Exactly.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: That we suffer better.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: Suffer better.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: For a lot of people, mortality is one of the very unfortunate versions of suffering, which

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: is that the ride ends in this realm, whatever it is.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: What do you think of mortality?

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: Is it something you think about?

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: Is it something you fear?

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: What do you think happens after we die?

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: I don't fear it.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: First of all, I would say when I was in high school, I think my father actually encouraged

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: me to read this book.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: I read Ernest Becker's Denial of Death, which I found and still find to be one of the most

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: profound works I've ever come across.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: And he convinced me that a lot of what our society is about are ways that we avoid encountering

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: our own mortality, our physicality.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: Among the points he makes, and I'm not quoting him at all directly, is like, why does everything

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: about our physical body make us so uncomfortable?

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: Everything that comes out of you other than tears is either mildly or very disgusting.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: Why?

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: Why does that have to be?

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: Why are sex and eating and all the things that are physical surrounded with so much

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: symbolism?

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: What are table manners, really?

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: Where we're not eating like animals because we're not eating like animals.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: And sex obviously has more symbolism around it than anything.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: And his answer is anything that reminds you that you're a physical body because that's

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: what dies.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: Your body dies.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: It decays.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: It dies.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: It gets eaten by worms.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: That you don't want to think about, so you deny it.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: I think that part of religion is a confrontation with your own mortality, but also a certain

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: transcendence of it because the idea is something about you is eternal.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: What exactly I don't know.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: And you asked, what do I think happens after we die?

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: So I don't know any better than anyone else does, but I'll say two things about it.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: One is that every image of what it's like is foolish.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: Mark Twain has, I think in Letters from Earth, he says, we're going to lie on green fields

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: and listen to harp music, which you wouldn't want to do for five minutes while you're alive,

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: but you think you'll be happy for the rest of eternity doing it after you die.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: So I don't know.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: This world was a surprise.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: So why shouldn't the next world be a surprise?

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: I have no idea.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: But I really like this parable that's told by a guy in a book on death and mourning by

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: a rabbi in a book on death and mourning about twins in a womb.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: He says, one of them believes that there's a life outside and the other one doesn't.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: He says, the one who doesn't says, look, this is the only world we've ever seen, the only

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: world we've ever known.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: When I was in high school, I was a really pretty ardent atheist.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: And I loved Bertrand Russell, who was, for my money, with all due respect to all the

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: very, very capable people that we've talked about earlier, he's the best atheist pound

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: for pound that there was, and a remarkably witty and lucid writer.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: And I was totally in his thrall.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: And I would read every book by Russell I could get my hands on.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: And the reason that I did, I have this theory that why do adolescent boys like Mr. Spock

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: and like Sherlock Holmes?

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: I think it's because when you hit puberty, for a lot of us, there's so much discomfort

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: with our bodies that we like the idea that we're just brains.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: I really think so.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: I had that experience.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: It's like, I want to just be a thinking machine.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: I don't want to be a body because my body was making me so uncomfortable.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: I had all these urges and inclinations that I couldn't control.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: So Russell was perfect.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: And my father, who was a rabbi, did the very wise thing of buying me some of Bertrand Russell's

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: books, which was his way of saying, I'm not afraid of him.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: And actually, there was another rabbi.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: I was at summer camp and I was sitting on the porch of the, I remember exactly, and

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: I was reading Bertrand Russell and this guy came up to me and said, well, what are you

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: reading?

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: I was maybe 16 or 17.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: And I said, Bertrand Russell, I was spoiling for a fight.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: And he said, I'm glad you're reading him.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: I said, really, why?

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: He goes, how old are you, David?

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: And I said, whatever I was, 16, 17.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: He said, well, I'd rather you grow out of him than grow into him.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: And you know what?

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: He was actually right because when I started to read about Russell's life, I realized that

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: all of that rationality didn't shield him.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: He had an incredibly messy life, multiple marriages, endless infidelities, family members

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: he didn't speak to, didn't speak to him.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: And so I started to believe that maybe it was possible that people who had faith were

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: part about Judaism and your faith?

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: I think the most beautiful part about Judaism is that even though it is filled with humor

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: and wit, it takes life and it takes the soul seriously.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: It really believes that this matters and that we matter and what we do matters.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: And I think that that's incredibly important.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: And especially in a world in which young people feel so much like they don't matter, that's

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: an unbelievably powerful message.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: I want to say the same thing, which is really, that's not ultimately you matter because you're

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: in the image of God.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: And Judaism really deeply, deeply believes and preaches that.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: And I think that that's a message that has so much to say to the world.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: It's like you have to take people's souls seriously.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: And for all of the difficulty in figuring out all these social questions and what they

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: mean, I just don't want to dismiss people because I disagree with them politically or

body.input: socially or culturally because I think they matter.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: So ultimately Judaism has a wealth of meaning for human mind.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: I really believe that it does.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: I really do.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: And its meaning, and I want to emphasize this, is not political.

body.input: Let me ask you the big question of advice.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: of.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: So the first thing that I would say is that life is longer than you think it is.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: Even though I understand the impulse to be in a rush, you will have many unfoldings,

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: more even than people of my generation did.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: It's a beautiful word.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: Unfolding.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: But it feels that way.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: I think the second thing that I would say is, I know that this is a very old fashioned,

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: but I would say to the extent that you can read, don't just, and not just on social media,

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: read books.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: Learn things that will give you a broader context for your life than just today or yesterday

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: or the day before.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: I suppose the other thing that I would say is that to the extent that you can, try to

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: doing that and it looks great, but that's not me.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: You have a community of people that speak to you with a lot of passion, and do you still

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: have that voice in your own, in the privacy of your own mind that you're able to ignore?

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: For a moment, just be with yourself and think what is right.

body.input: Well, hope, let me ask you, he said meaning.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: You do that more than anything else.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: Yep.

body.input: Yeah.

body.input: So we started with the big question of what is God, ended with what is meaning.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: Rabbi Wolpe, I've been a huge, as I've told you, huge, huge fan of yours for a long time.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: It's such an honor that you talked to me today.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: I am really so happy to be here, and thank you so much for the conversation.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: Thanks for listening to this conversation with David Wolpe.

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

metadata.title: Podcast: David Wolpe: Judaism | Lex Fridman Podcast #270

body.input: And now let me leave you with some words from David himself.
