metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Malice: New Year's Special | Lex Fridman Podcast #253

body.input: Hello, comrade!

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Malice: New Year's Special | Lex Fridman Podcast #253

body.input: Happy New Year!

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Malice: New Year's Special | Lex Fridman Podcast #253

body.input: Dostoevsky wrote in The Idiot, my favorite of his books, through the main character Prince Michigan, that beauty will save the world.

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Malice: New Year's Special | Lex Fridman Podcast #253

body.input: Красота спасет мир. These words seem really naive and ultimately, at least to me, profound. What do they mean to you? Beauty will save the world.

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Malice: New Year's Special | Lex Fridman Podcast #253

body.input: Naive? Really? I don't think they seem naive at all.

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Malice: New Year's Special | Lex Fridman Podcast #253

body.input: Well, Solzhenitsyn actually, for his 1970 Nobel Prize speech, talked about this line a lot. And he thought for most of his life that was a silly line.

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Malice: New Year's Special | Lex Fridman Podcast #253

body.input: It was just words thrown out there. Because with all the suffering that's in the world, what has beauty actually ever done?

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Malice: New Year's Special | Lex Fridman Podcast #253

body.input: Oh my God, I hate this so much.

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Malice: New Year's Special | Lex Fridman Podcast #253

body.input: You're talking trash about Solzhenitsyn.

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Malice: New Year's Special | Lex Fridman Podcast #253

body.input: Yeah, I am.

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Malice: New Year's Special | Lex Fridman Podcast #253

body.input: Okay.

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Malice: New Year's Special | Lex Fridman Podcast #253

body.input: And this perfectly sets up this theme. You know, I said let's do this episode, start the new year on a positive note, give people hope, give people joy.

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Malice: New Year's Special | Lex Fridman Podcast #253

body.input: You and I both have friends who are models, right? And it's a silly profession to some extent, of course.

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Malice: New Year's Special | Lex Fridman Podcast #253

body.input: But you are actually a model. You are my friend.

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Malice: New Year's Special | Lex Fridman Podcast #253

body.input: Yeah, that's right. That's true. I am a model. I was trying to be subtle. But for those people who actually deserve to be models, when you look at someone who is a model and in some of their photos,

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Malice: New Year's Special | Lex Fridman Podcast #253

body.input: and these people look perfect. Now in real life, they're not perfect. They have flaws. They'll be the first to admit it, so on and so forth.

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Malice: New Year's Special | Lex Fridman Podcast #253

body.input: But when you look at beauty, it is almost impossible to maintain a sense of cynicism and hopelessness.

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Malice: New Year's Special | Lex Fridman Podcast #253

body.input: Because if there's even one moment when some element of perfection has been actualized, if there's one moment where beauty has been realized and captured, you can't say, well, it's never gonna happen again.

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Malice: New Year's Special | Lex Fridman Podcast #253

body.input: So I think beauty means hope. I think I hate that cynical idea of like...

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Malice: New Year's Special | Lex Fridman Podcast #253

body.input: I appreciate Solzhenitsyn's broader point that a lot of times people, there's something called a deepity, where people throw words together to sound profound.

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Malice: New Year's Special | Lex Fridman Podcast #253

body.input: And if you take it apart, like this is just complete gibberish. I don't think this is an example of that.

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Malice: New Year's Special | Lex Fridman Podcast #253

body.input: I think beauty inspires and more importantly, it proves to you this is something that can actually happen on this earth.

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Malice: New Year's Special | Lex Fridman Podcast #253

body.input: Plato, right? The Platonic theory of forms, like this world is imperfect, but these perfect forms exist in another dimension and that's where our concepts come from.

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Malice: New Year's Special | Lex Fridman Podcast #253

body.input: He was an early person trying to figure out where our concepts come from, and epistemology, and so on and so forth.

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Malice: New Year's Special | Lex Fridman Podcast #253

body.input: But that is something that is real in here. So I completely disagree with his analysis of that.

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Malice: New Year's Special | Lex Fridman Podcast #253

body.input: And I don't know if it'll save the world, but it's certainly a prerequisite.

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Malice: New Year's Special | Lex Fridman Podcast #253

body.input: And what's the point of fighting for your values if you don't want to make the world a more beautiful place?

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Malice: New Year's Special | Lex Fridman Podcast #253

body.input: Well, it's also how you define beauty, because beauty could be just aesthetic. Beauty could be art.

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Malice: New Year's Special | Lex Fridman Podcast #253

body.input: Of course, art could encompass a lot more than just literature and paintings. It can encompass the full life, the full dance of life.

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Malice: New Year's Special | Lex Fridman Podcast #253

body.input: But then beauty could be something just deeper, like whatever that awe you feel when you pause and hear the music.

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Malice: New Year's Special | Lex Fridman Podcast #253

body.input: Just hear and look up at the stars. For some reason, when I see rockets go up, for me it's like science.

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Malice: New Year's Special | Lex Fridman Podcast #253

body.input: What is that? The awe that we're able to accomplish that as humans.

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Malice: New Year's Special | Lex Fridman Podcast #253

body.input: You know, that's funny because there's lots of different schools of thought, like these people versus these people, and maybe vegans versus steakhouse people.

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Malice: New Year's Special | Lex Fridman Podcast #253

body.input: I think in terms of the sciences, and I guess you and I would be on opposite sides here, you have the astronomy people versus the zoology people.

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Malice: New Year's Special | Lex Fridman Podcast #253

body.input: The big question is, would you rather spend 10 minutes on the Moon or would you rather spend 10 minutes in the deep sea?

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Malice: New Year's Special | Lex Fridman Podcast #253

body.input: And for me, it's clearly the deep sea. The zoology that's down there, there's something I would encourage people to look up called deep staria, which is a jellyfish.

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Malice: New Year's Special | Lex Fridman Podcast #253

body.input: What's amazing when you watch these deep sea dives on YouTube is that the scientists, they're nature dorks like everybody else.

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Malice: New Year's Special | Lex Fridman Podcast #253

body.input: They went into this field and there's none of this maybe Solzhenitsyn-style cynicism of when they see an amazing animal in its natural environment, you know, exhibiting these crazy behaviors.

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Malice: New Year's Special | Lex Fridman Podcast #253

body.input: They lose it. They're on the mics like, oh my God! It's so exciting to watch.

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Malice: New Year's Special | Lex Fridman Podcast #253

body.input: So I'm not a rocket person, but I'm definitely a zoology person.

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Malice: New Year's Special | Lex Fridman Podcast #253

body.input: So animals and plants and the sea.

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Malice: New Year's Special | Lex Fridman Podcast #253

body.input: And also it's so mathematical. There's so many forms. There's this plant called areospermum, tighten up, soides.

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Malice: New Year's Special | Lex Fridman Podcast #253

body.input: I don't know how to pronounce it because they're always in Latin. You never hear them pronounced.

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Malice: New Year's Special | Lex Fridman Podcast #253

body.input: You said sperm.

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Malice: New Year's Special | Lex Fridman Podcast #253

body.input: Areospermum, yeah, because it's a woolly seed is the genus.

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Malice: New Year's Special | Lex Fridman Podcast #253

body.input: The leaf, it just always puts out one leaf, but the leaf is covered in little magnifying glasses, lenses to make it maximize the sunlight.

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Malice: New Year's Special | Lex Fridman Podcast #253

body.input: So it looks like this little crystal seashell. It's tiny. It's like two centimeters.

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Malice: New Year's Special | Lex Fridman Podcast #253

body.input: But it's just this amazing thing that grows out of the sands in South Africa.

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Malice: New Year's Special | Lex Fridman Podcast #253

body.input: Just to defend Solzhenitsyn for a second. So if I may read a couple of his lines from the speech.

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Malice: New Year's Special | Lex Fridman Podcast #253

body.input: Sure.

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Malice: New Year's Special | Lex Fridman Podcast #253

body.input: And one day, this is how he introduces it. One day, Dostoevsky threw out the enigmatic remark, beauty will save the world.

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Malice: New Year's Special | Lex Fridman Podcast #253

body.input: What sort of a statement is that? For a long time, I considered it mere words.

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Malice: New Year's Special | Lex Fridman Podcast #253

body.input: How could that be possible when in bloodthirsty history, did beauty ever save anyone from anything?

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Malice: New Year's Special | Lex Fridman Podcast #253

body.input: And then later he goes on to argue with himself in the speech as an older, wiser man now.

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Malice: New Year's Special | Lex Fridman Podcast #253

body.input: Perhaps that ancient trinity of truth, goodness, and beauty is not simply an empty, faded formula as we thought in the days of our self-confident materialistic youth.

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Malice: New Year's Special | Lex Fridman Podcast #253

body.input: If the tops of these three trees converge, as the scholars maintained,

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Malice: New Year's Special | Lex Fridman Podcast #253

body.input: but the two blatant, two direct stems of truth and goodness are crushed, cut down, not allowed through,

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Malice: New Year's Special | Lex Fridman Podcast #253

body.input: perhaps the fantastic, unpredictable, unexpected stems of beauty will push through and soar to that very same place.

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Malice: New Year's Special | Lex Fridman Podcast #253

body.input: And in so doing, will fulfill the work of all three.

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Malice: New Year's Special | Lex Fridman Podcast #253

body.input: In that case, Dostoevsky's remark, beauty will save the world, was not a careless phrase, but a prophecy.

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Malice: New Year's Special | Lex Fridman Podcast #253

body.input: Which of these three things are your favorites? Truth, goodness, or beauty?

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Malice: New Year's Special | Lex Fridman Podcast #253

body.input: What did he call truth and goodness? The blatant, two direct stems of truth and goodness versus the fantastic, unpredictable, unexpected stems of beauty, which is how I see your Twitter account.

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Malice: New Year's Special | Lex Fridman Podcast #253

body.input: I don't think that, I think there's a certain dearth of beauty if you had my Twitter account, that's for sure.

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Malice: New Year's Special | Lex Fridman Podcast #253

body.input: It's certainly no goodness.

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Malice: New Year's Special | Lex Fridman Podcast #253

body.input: Or truth.

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Malice: New Year's Special | Lex Fridman Podcast #253

body.input: Yeah, yeah. It's Twitter. There's no truth to be found.

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Malice: New Year's Special | Lex Fridman Podcast #253

body.input: I will answer the question. I will of course point out that having this kind of distinction between the three things is, I think, kind of synthetic.

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Malice: New Year's Special | Lex Fridman Podcast #253

body.input: I think they very heavily overlap. If not, I can probably make the argument they're synonymous.

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Malice: New Year's Special | Lex Fridman Podcast #253

body.input: In fact, I do believe that they're largely synonymous.

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Malice: New Year's Special | Lex Fridman Podcast #253

body.input: Goodness. That's such an interesting word, goodness.

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Malice: New Year's Special | Lex Fridman Podcast #253

body.input: Which of those three is my favorite?

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Malice: New Year's Special | Lex Fridman Podcast #253

body.input: I think truth is overrated in the sense that if something is a good story, the story doesn't have to be true or real in order to motivate you and move you.

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Malice: New Year's Special | Lex Fridman Podcast #253

body.input: A lot of times we can delude ourselves about somebody, and that might actually serve a purpose to some extent.

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Malice: New Year's Special | Lex Fridman Podcast #253

body.input: If you have someone who's maybe a family member and you kind of ignore bad things that they do, there might be reason for that.

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Malice: New Year's Special | Lex Fridman Podcast #253

body.input: Of the three which is most important, I think I would say probably goodness.

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Malice: New Year's Special | Lex Fridman Podcast #253

body.input: I would say of the three, the most important is goodness because if you don't appreciate goodness, then beauty is just empty.

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Malice: New Year's Special | Lex Fridman Podcast #253

body.input: It's just a picture or it's nice.

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Malice: New Year's Special | Lex Fridman Podcast #253

body.input: Bad people appreciate beauty. Bad people are often seductive or have a beauty about them.

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Malice: New Year's Special | Lex Fridman Podcast #253

body.input: In terms of action, I think it takes a lot of skill and work to create beauty or to create truth or to express truth or to express beauty.

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Malice: New Year's Special | Lex Fridman Podcast #253

body.input: But I think goodness is the easiest default state of being, just being good to others.

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Malice: New Year's Special | Lex Fridman Podcast #253

body.input: There'll be things where these videos where one dog is drowning and another dog jumps in and saves it from the pool.

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Malice: New Year's Special | Lex Fridman Podcast #253

body.input: That to me is just really amazing stuff and is very moving.

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Malice: New Year's Special | Lex Fridman Podcast #253

body.input: To me, goodness means integrity and it means kindness.

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Malice: New Year's Special | Lex Fridman Podcast #253

body.input: I think of the three, that would be the one I pick.

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Malice: New Year's Special | Lex Fridman Podcast #253

body.input: I think people also have this idea which is inculcated to them, especially by corporate America, that as you get older, it's okay to do the wrong things sometimes.

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Malice: New Year's Special | Lex Fridman Podcast #253

body.input: I don't buy that. I think goodness gets rarer and rarer.

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Malice: New Year's Special | Lex Fridman Podcast #253

body.input: I think people know better and they tell themselves lies.

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Malice: New Year's Special | Lex Fridman Podcast #253

body.input: But once you allow yourself the chance to just be good, I think it makes for a better life.

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Malice: New Year's Special | Lex Fridman Podcast #253

body.input: It's not that much work. It's not like going to the gym or working out. That's a lot of work and it's great afterwards.

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Malice: New Year's Special | Lex Fridman Podcast #253

body.input: But goodness is easy once you get into the habit of it. I suppose working out is the same way.

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Malice: New Year's Special | Lex Fridman Podcast #253

body.input: There's a lot of stuff. If you make it a habit, you're going to get the rewards of it and it's going to be easy.

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Malice: New Year's Special | Lex Fridman Podcast #253

body.input: The rewards of goodness, I think, are more immediate than the rewards of working out.

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Malice: New Year's Special | Lex Fridman Podcast #253

body.input: As opposed to the hard drugs.

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Malice: New Year's Special | Lex Fridman Podcast #253

body.input: Yeah.

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Malice: New Year's Special | Lex Fridman Podcast #253

body.input: You mentioned this quote on one of your live streams, I think. If you save one life, you save the world.

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Malice: New Year's Special | Lex Fridman Podcast #253

body.input: Yeah.

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Malice: New Year's Special | Lex Fridman Podcast #253

body.input: That's such a cool line. I remember reading about Paul Farmer. I think his name is. He's a doctor that really...

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Malice: New Year's Special | Lex Fridman Podcast #253

body.input: Doctors in general, they don't care about what they're doing as a broad policy across hundreds of thousands of millions of people.

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Malice: New Year's Special | Lex Fridman Podcast #253

body.input: They just care about the human in front of them, which is so interesting.

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Malice: New Year's Special | Lex Fridman Podcast #253

body.input: They don't care it's going to cost. In his case, to save one child, it will cost him hundreds of thousands of dollars.

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Malice: New Year's Special | Lex Fridman Podcast #253

body.input: They don't care about that. They can't.

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Malice: New Year's Special | Lex Fridman Podcast #253

body.input: They know very well that what their actions cannot be scaled, but they can't help but help the child in front of them.

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Malice: New Year's Special | Lex Fridman Podcast #253

body.input: And it's so interesting. That's such an interesting way to live.

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Malice: New Year's Special | Lex Fridman Podcast #253

body.input: And that's the way I kind of think when I try to do something positive is, will this help one person?

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Malice: New Year's Special | Lex Fridman Podcast #253

body.input: And I just kind of imagine a specific person, depending on the thing, that that would help with, like when I'm trying to create something, whether it's a piece of hardware or a video or anything like that, or educational material, lecture, that kind of stuff.

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Malice: New Year's Special | Lex Fridman Podcast #253

body.input: I don't know. What do you think about this quote? Is it profound or is it just poetic?

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Malice: New Year's Special | Lex Fridman Podcast #253

body.input: I think it's more profound than it sounds at first. The example I think of is Michelle Bachmann. She was a former congresswoman from Minnesota.

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Malice: New Year's Special | Lex Fridman Podcast #253

body.input: She clearly had crazy eyes, something weird was going on with her husband, but she adopted like 20 kids.

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Malice: New Year's Special | Lex Fridman Podcast #253

body.input: Terry Shappard is another friend of mine. He's like either a Navy SEAL or Marines. Whatever it is, Terry, I apologize. I'm not trying to be funny.

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Malice: New Year's Special | Lex Fridman Podcast #253

body.input: And he adopts like elder dogs. So going back to Bachmann, it's like, yeah, you can say she's crazy.

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Malice: New Year's Special | Lex Fridman Podcast #253

body.input: You can make fun of her politics all you want, and all that stuff is legitimate.

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Malice: New Year's Special | Lex Fridman Podcast #253

body.input: But if you save a kid, give them a home, and you save them from the foster system, and you put a roof over their heads and make them feel loved and appreciated,

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Malice: New Year's Special | Lex Fridman Podcast #253

body.input: it's really hard for me to sit here and call you like a totally bad person. I think that kind of thing is Nick Cersei is another one.

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Malice: New Year's Special | Lex Fridman Podcast #253

body.input: He adopted a kid. And I said, I think you're a hero. Like if you, there's some, you know, one of the things that's very hard for me, I'm writing, as you know, I talk about this endlessly, this book,

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Malice: New Year's Special | Lex Fridman Podcast #253

body.input: The White Pill, but writing about when people do hurtful things to children, it really is hard to watch.

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Malice: New Year's Special | Lex Fridman Podcast #253

body.input: And it's hard to, because when you're an author, you have to kind of empathize with the character. You have to, where's this character coming from, explain their point of view.

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Malice: New Year's Special | Lex Fridman Podcast #253

body.input: And that's the one that's the hardest for me to wrap my head around, like cruelty to children. Yeah.

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Malice: New Year's Special | Lex Fridman Podcast #253

body.input: Or, and yeah, sadism to children. It's just like, this is something even animals know not to do, do you know what I mean? Like dogs, when you see them around kids, they're very protective.

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Malice: New Year's Special | Lex Fridman Podcast #253

body.input: Like if the kid pokes their eyes out, the dog doesn't do anything. So it's like, if you can't even get to that level, what kind of person are you?

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Malice: New Year's Special | Lex Fridman Podcast #253

body.input: So I think that quote is a profound one and it's an important one. It also means we're not all called upon to be Superman, right?

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Malice: New Year's Special | Lex Fridman Podcast #253

body.input: You only have a very finite ability to move the needle. But at the same time, if you have actually, you know, saved a life, you can go to meet your maker.

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Malice: New Year's Special | Lex Fridman Podcast #253

body.input: You did your part. You know, you left the world a little bit better than you found it. And that's all you could ask anybody.

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Malice: New Year's Special | Lex Fridman Podcast #253

body.input: Also, I think from a policy perspective, it seems we just do better when we focus on doing a small thing, helping a helping one person.

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Malice: New Year's Special | Lex Fridman Podcast #253

body.input: Because it feels like when you start talking about communism and all those kinds of things, when you start to believe you could do good by a lot of people, that's where your mind somehow.

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Malice: New Year's Special | Lex Fridman Podcast #253

body.input: Stops being able to do good by a lot of people. That's when you start to think about utopias and somehow utopias goes to feeds power into the brain to where it deludes you completely.

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Malice: New Year's Special | Lex Fridman Podcast #253

body.input: And then you start. It's OK to crack a few eggs to make an omelet kind of reasoning. And you run to trouble.

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Malice: New Year's Special | Lex Fridman Podcast #253

body.input: It seems like it's much better even when you have the power and the money and so on to achieve scale, to focus on one and then locally.

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Malice: New Year's Special | Lex Fridman Podcast #253

body.input: Because then you have the feedback. So if you have some kind of program in Austin or Brooklyn or something like that, and you can watch, oh, this is working, this isn't working, then you could port it out to other places.

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Malice: New Year's Special | Lex Fridman Podcast #253

body.input: But top down, helping is, at the very least, is going to be inefficient.

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Malice: New Year's Special | Lex Fridman Podcast #253

body.input: And also, I think it's a lot more useful when you're helping people when it's a one on one relationship because then it's less embarrassing, but certainly less something to receive help.

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Malice: New Year's Special | Lex Fridman Podcast #253

body.input: And you also feel it's one thing if you get a check from the government, you know, food stamps.

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Malice: New Year's Special | Lex Fridman Podcast #253

body.input: It's not a thing if someone's like, hey, I'm going to buy your groceries until you get back on your feet.

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Malice: New Year's Special | Lex Fridman Podcast #253

body.input: You have this kind of motivation, I think, for most people to be like, you know what? This person believed in me.

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Malice: New Year's Special | Lex Fridman Podcast #253

body.input: I'm going to make it worth their while that they believed in me.

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Malice: New Year's Special | Lex Fridman Podcast #253

body.input: Yes, I didn't believe in me. Yeah.

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Malice: New Year's Special | Lex Fridman Podcast #253

body.input: When I was giving lectures at MIT, there was one was scared shitless.

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Malice: New Year's Special | Lex Fridman Podcast #253

body.input: And everybody, you know, how students are and all that kind of stuff, they're kind of bored and they don't they don't understand that you're human, too.

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Malice: New Year's Special | Lex Fridman Podcast #253

body.input: And now here's my conversation with Daphne Koller.

metadata.title: Podcast: Daphne Koller: Biomedicine and Machine Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #93

body.input: So you co-founded Coursera,

metadata.title: Podcast: Daphne Koller: Biomedicine and Machine Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #93

body.input: and made a huge impact in the global education of AI.

metadata.title: Podcast: Daphne Koller: Biomedicine and Machine Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #93

body.input: And after five years, in August 2016,

metadata.title: Podcast: Daphne Koller: Biomedicine and Machine Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #93

body.input: wrote a blog post saying that you're stepping away

metadata.title: Podcast: Daphne Koller: Biomedicine and Machine Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #93

body.input: and wrote, quote,

metadata.title: Podcast: Daphne Koller: Biomedicine and Machine Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #93

body.input: "'It is time for me to turn to another critical challenge,

metadata.title: Podcast: Daphne Koller: Biomedicine and Machine Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #93

body.input: the development of machine learning

metadata.title: Podcast: Daphne Koller: Biomedicine and Machine Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #93

body.input: and its applications to improving human health.'"

metadata.title: Podcast: Daphne Koller: Biomedicine and Machine Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #93

body.input: So let me ask two far out philosophical questions.

metadata.title: Podcast: Daphne Koller: Biomedicine and Machine Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #93

body.input: One, do you think we'll one day find cures

metadata.title: Podcast: Daphne Koller: Biomedicine and Machine Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #93

body.input: for all major diseases known today?

metadata.title: Podcast: Daphne Koller: Biomedicine and Machine Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #93

body.input: And two, do you think we will one day figure out

metadata.title: Podcast: Daphne Koller: Biomedicine and Machine Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #93

body.input: a way to extend the human lifespan,

metadata.title: Podcast: Daphne Koller: Biomedicine and Machine Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #93

body.input: perhaps to the point of immortality?

metadata.title: Podcast: Daphne Koller: Biomedicine and Machine Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #93

body.input: So one day is a very long time,

metadata.title: Podcast: Daphne Koller: Biomedicine and Machine Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #93

body.input: and I don't like to make predictions

metadata.title: Podcast: Daphne Koller: Biomedicine and Machine Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #93

body.input: of the type we will never be able to do X

metadata.title: Podcast: Daphne Koller: Biomedicine and Machine Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #93

body.input: because I think that's a, you know,

metadata.title: Podcast: Daphne Koller: Biomedicine and Machine Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #93

body.input: that's the smacks of hubris.

metadata.title: Podcast: Daphne Koller: Biomedicine and Machine Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #93

body.input: It seems that never in the entire eternity

metadata.title: Podcast: Daphne Koller: Biomedicine and Machine Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #93

body.input: of human existence will we be able to solve a problem.

metadata.title: Podcast: Daphne Koller: Biomedicine and Machine Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #93

body.input: That being said, curing disease is very hard

metadata.title: Podcast: Daphne Koller: Biomedicine and Machine Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #93

body.input: because oftentimes by the time you discover the disease,

metadata.title: Podcast: Daphne Koller: Biomedicine and Machine Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #93

body.input: a lot of damage has already been done.

metadata.title: Podcast: Daphne Koller: Biomedicine and Machine Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #93

body.input: And so to assume that we would be able to cure disease

metadata.title: Podcast: Daphne Koller: Biomedicine and Machine Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #93

body.input: at that stage assumes that we would come up

metadata.title: Podcast: Daphne Koller: Biomedicine and Machine Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #93

body.input: with ways of basically regenerating entire parts

metadata.title: Podcast: Daphne Koller: Biomedicine and Machine Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #93

body.input: of the human body in a way that actually returns it

metadata.title: Podcast: Daphne Koller: Biomedicine and Machine Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #93

body.input: to its original state.

metadata.title: Podcast: Daphne Koller: Biomedicine and Machine Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #93

body.input: And that's a very challenging problem.

metadata.title: Podcast: Daphne Koller: Biomedicine and Machine Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #93

body.input: We have cured very few diseases.

metadata.title: Podcast: Daphne Koller: Biomedicine and Machine Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #93

body.input: We've been able to provide treatment

metadata.title: Podcast: Daphne Koller: Biomedicine and Machine Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #93

body.input: for an increasingly large number,

metadata.title: Podcast: Daphne Koller: Biomedicine and Machine Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #93

body.input: but the number of things that you could actually define

metadata.title: Podcast: Daphne Koller: Biomedicine and Machine Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #93

body.input: to be cures is actually not that large.

metadata.title: Podcast: Daphne Koller: Biomedicine and Machine Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #93

body.input: So I think that there's a lot of work

metadata.title: Podcast: Daphne Koller: Biomedicine and Machine Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #93

body.input: that would need to happen before one could legitimately say

metadata.title: Podcast: Daphne Koller: Biomedicine and Machine Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #93

body.input: that we have cured even a reasonable number

metadata.title: Podcast: Daphne Koller: Biomedicine and Machine Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #93

body.input: of far less all diseases.

metadata.title: Podcast: Daphne Koller: Biomedicine and Machine Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #93

body.input: On the scale of zero to 100,

metadata.title: Podcast: Daphne Koller: Biomedicine and Machine Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #93

body.input: where are we in understanding the fundamental mechanisms

metadata.title: Podcast: Daphne Koller: Biomedicine and Machine Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #93

body.input: of all major diseases?

metadata.title: Podcast: Daphne Koller: Biomedicine and Machine Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #93

body.input: What's your sense?

metadata.title: Podcast: Daphne Koller: Biomedicine and Machine Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #93

body.input: So from the computer science perspective

metadata.title: Podcast: Daphne Koller: Biomedicine and Machine Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #93

body.input: that you've entered the world of health,

metadata.title: Podcast: Daphne Koller: Biomedicine and Machine Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #93

body.input: how far along are we?

metadata.title: Podcast: Daphne Koller: Biomedicine and Machine Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #93

body.input: I think it depends on which disease.

metadata.title: Podcast: Daphne Koller: Biomedicine and Machine Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #93

body.input: I mean, there are ones where I would say

metadata.title: Podcast: Daphne Koller: Biomedicine and Machine Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #93

body.input: we're maybe not quite at 100

metadata.title: Podcast: Daphne Koller: Biomedicine and Machine Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #93

body.input: because biology is really complicated

metadata.title: Podcast: Daphne Koller: Biomedicine and Machine Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #93

body.input: and there's always new things that we uncover

metadata.title: Podcast: Daphne Koller: Biomedicine and Machine Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #93

body.input: that people didn't even realize existed.

metadata.title: Podcast: Daphne Koller: Biomedicine and Machine Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #93

body.input: But I would say there's diseases where we might be

metadata.title: Podcast: Daphne Koller: Biomedicine and Machine Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #93

body.input: in the 70s or 80s, and then there's diseases

metadata.title: Podcast: Daphne Koller: Biomedicine and Machine Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #93

body.input: in which I would say probably the majority

metadata.title: Podcast: Daphne Koller: Biomedicine and Machine Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #93

body.input: where we're really close to zero.

metadata.title: Podcast: Daphne Koller: Biomedicine and Machine Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #93

body.input: Would Alzheimer's and schizophrenia

metadata.title: Podcast: Daphne Koller: Biomedicine and Machine Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #93

body.input: and type 2 diabetes fall closer to zero or to the 80?

metadata.title: Podcast: Daphne Koller: Biomedicine and Machine Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #93

body.input: I think Alzheimer's is probably closer to zero than to 80.

metadata.title: Podcast: Daphne Koller: Biomedicine and Machine Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #93

body.input: There are hypotheses, but I don't think

metadata.title: Podcast: Daphne Koller: Biomedicine and Machine Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #93

body.input: those hypotheses have as of yet been sufficiently validated

metadata.title: Podcast: Daphne Koller: Biomedicine and Machine Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #93

body.input: that we believe them to be true.

metadata.title: Podcast: Daphne Koller: Biomedicine and Machine Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #93

body.input: And there is an increasing number of people

metadata.title: Podcast: Daphne Koller: Biomedicine and Machine Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #93

body.input: who believe that the traditional hypotheses

metadata.title: Podcast: Daphne Koller: Biomedicine and Machine Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #93

body.input: might not really explain what's going on.

metadata.title: Podcast: Daphne Koller: Biomedicine and Machine Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #93

body.input: I would also say that Alzheimer's and schizophrenia

metadata.title: Podcast: Daphne Koller: Biomedicine and Machine Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #93

body.input: and even type 2 diabetes are not really one disease.

metadata.title: Podcast: Daphne Koller: Biomedicine and Machine Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #93

body.input: They're almost certainly a heterogeneous collection

metadata.title: Podcast: Daphne Koller: Biomedicine and Machine Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #93

body.input: of mechanisms that manifest in clinically similar ways.

metadata.title: Podcast: Daphne Koller: Biomedicine and Machine Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #93

body.input: So in the same way that we now understand

metadata.title: Podcast: Daphne Koller: Biomedicine and Machine Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #93

body.input: that breast cancer is really not one disease,

metadata.title: Podcast: Daphne Koller: Biomedicine and Machine Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #93

body.input: it is multitude of cellular mechanisms,

metadata.title: Podcast: Daphne Koller: Biomedicine and Machine Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #93

body.input: all of which ultimately translate

metadata.title: Podcast: Daphne Koller: Biomedicine and Machine Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #93

body.input: to uncontrolled proliferation, but it's not one disease.

metadata.title: Podcast: Daphne Koller: Biomedicine and Machine Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #93

body.input: The same is almost undoubtedly true

metadata.title: Podcast: Daphne Koller: Biomedicine and Machine Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #93

body.input: for those other diseases as well.

metadata.title: Podcast: Daphne Koller: Biomedicine and Machine Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #93

body.input: And that understanding that needs to precede

metadata.title: Podcast: Daphne Koller: Biomedicine and Machine Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #93

body.input: any understanding of the specific mechanisms

metadata.title: Podcast: Daphne Koller: Biomedicine and Machine Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #93

body.input: of any of those other diseases.

metadata.title: Podcast: Daphne Koller: Biomedicine and Machine Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #93

body.input: Now in schizophrenia, I would say

metadata.title: Podcast: Daphne Koller: Biomedicine and Machine Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #93

body.input: we're almost certainly closer to zero

metadata.title: Podcast: Daphne Koller: Biomedicine and Machine Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #93

body.input: than to anything else.

metadata.title: Podcast: Daphne Koller: Biomedicine and Machine Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #93

body.input: Type 2 diabetes is a bit of a mix.

metadata.title: Podcast: Daphne Koller: Biomedicine and Machine Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #93

body.input: There are clear mechanisms that are implicated

metadata.title: Podcast: Daphne Koller: Biomedicine and Machine Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #93

body.input: that I think have been validated

metadata.title: Podcast: Daphne Koller: Biomedicine and Machine Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #93

body.input: that have to do with insulin resistance and such,

metadata.title: Podcast: Daphne Koller: Biomedicine and Machine Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #93

body.input: but there's almost certainly there as well

metadata.title: Podcast: Daphne Koller: Biomedicine and Machine Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #93

body.input: many mechanisms that we have not yet understood.

metadata.title: Podcast: Daphne Koller: Biomedicine and Machine Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #93

body.input: So you've also thought and worked a little bit

metadata.title: Podcast: Daphne Koller: Biomedicine and Machine Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #93

body.input: on the longevity side.

metadata.title: Podcast: Daphne Koller: Biomedicine and Machine Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #93

body.input: Do you see the disease and longevity

metadata.title: Podcast: Daphne Koller: Biomedicine and Machine Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #93

body.input: as overlapping completely, partially, or not at all?

metadata.title: Podcast: Daphne Koller: Biomedicine and Machine Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #93

body.input: As efforts?

metadata.title: Podcast: Daphne Koller: Biomedicine and Machine Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #93

body.input: Those mechanisms are certainly overlapping.

metadata.title: Podcast: Daphne Koller: Biomedicine and Machine Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #93

body.input: There's a well-known phenomenon that says

metadata.title: Podcast: Daphne Koller: Biomedicine and Machine Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #93

body.input: that for most diseases, other than childhood diseases,

metadata.title: Podcast: Daphne Koller: Biomedicine and Machine Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #93

body.input: the risk for contracting that disease

metadata.title: Podcast: Daphne Koller: Biomedicine and Machine Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #93

body.input: increases exponentially year on year,

metadata.title: Podcast: Daphne Koller: Biomedicine and Machine Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #93

body.input: every year from the time you're about 40.

metadata.title: Podcast: Daphne Koller: Biomedicine and Machine Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #93

body.input: So obviously there is a connection

metadata.title: Podcast: Daphne Koller: Biomedicine and Machine Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #93

body.input: between those two things.

metadata.title: Podcast: Daphne Koller: Biomedicine and Machine Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #93

body.input: That's not to say that they're identical.

metadata.title: Podcast: Daphne Koller: Biomedicine and Machine Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #93

body.input: There's clearly aging that happens

metadata.title: Podcast: Daphne Koller: Biomedicine and Machine Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #93

body.input: that is not really associated with any specific disease.

metadata.title: Podcast: Daphne Koller: Biomedicine and Machine Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #93

body.input: And there's also diseases and mechanisms of disease

metadata.title: Podcast: Daphne Koller: Biomedicine and Machine Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #93

body.input: that are not specifically related to aging.

metadata.title: Podcast: Daphne Koller: Biomedicine and Machine Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #93

body.input: So I think overlap is where we're at.

metadata.title: Podcast: Daphne Koller: Biomedicine and Machine Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #93

body.input: Okay.

metadata.title: Podcast: Daphne Koller: Biomedicine and Machine Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #93

body.input: It is a little unfortunate that we get older,

metadata.title: Podcast: Daphne Koller: Biomedicine and Machine Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #93

body.input: and it seems that there's some correlation

metadata.title: Podcast: Daphne Koller: Biomedicine and Machine Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #93

body.input: with the occurrence of diseases,

metadata.title: Podcast: Daphne Koller: Biomedicine and Machine Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #93

body.input: or the fact that we get older.

metadata.title: Podcast: Daphne Koller: Biomedicine and Machine Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #93

body.input: And both are quite sad.

metadata.title: Podcast: Daphne Koller: Biomedicine and Machine Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #93

body.input: Well, I mean, there's processes that happen

metadata.title: Podcast: Daphne Koller: Biomedicine and Machine Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #93

body.input: as cells age that I think are contributing to disease.

metadata.title: Podcast: Daphne Koller: Biomedicine and Machine Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #93

body.input: Some of those have to do with DNA damage

metadata.title: Podcast: Daphne Koller: Biomedicine and Machine Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #93

body.input: that accumulates as cells divide,

metadata.title: Podcast: Daphne Koller: Biomedicine and Machine Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #93

body.input: where the repair mechanisms don't fully correct for those.

metadata.title: Podcast: Daphne Koller: Biomedicine and Machine Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #93

body.input: There are accumulations of proteins that are misfolded

metadata.title: Podcast: Daphne Koller: Biomedicine and Machine Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #93

body.input: and potentially aggregate,

metadata.title: Podcast: Daphne Koller: Biomedicine and Machine Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #93

body.input: and those too contribute to disease

metadata.title: Podcast: Daphne Koller: Biomedicine and Machine Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #93

body.input: and contribute to inflammation.

metadata.title: Podcast: Daphne Koller: Biomedicine and Machine Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #93

body.input: There is a multitude of mechanisms that have been uncovered

metadata.title: Podcast: Daphne Koller: Biomedicine and Machine Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #93

body.input: that are sort of wear and tear at the cellular level

metadata.title: Podcast: Daphne Koller: Biomedicine and Machine Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #93

body.input: that contribute to disease processes.

metadata.title: Podcast: Daphne Koller: Biomedicine and Machine Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #93

body.input: And I'm sure there's many that we don't yet understand.

metadata.title: Podcast: Daphne Koller: Biomedicine and Machine Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #93

body.input: On a small tangent, and perhaps philosophical,

metadata.title: Podcast: Daphne Koller: Biomedicine and Machine Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #93

body.input: does the fact that things get older

metadata.title: Podcast: Daphne Koller: Biomedicine and Machine Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #93

body.input: and the fact that things die

metadata.title: Podcast: Daphne Koller: Biomedicine and Machine Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #93

body.input: is a very powerful feature for the growth of new things.

metadata.title: Podcast: Daphne Koller: Biomedicine and Machine Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #93

body.input: It's a learning mechanism.

metadata.title: Podcast: Daphne Koller: Biomedicine and Machine Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #93

body.input: So it's both tragic and beautiful.

metadata.title: Podcast: Daphne Koller: Biomedicine and Machine Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #93

body.input: In trying to fight disease and trying to fight aging,

metadata.title: Podcast: Daphne Koller: Biomedicine and Machine Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #93

body.input: do you think about the useful fact of our mortality?

metadata.title: Podcast: Daphne Koller: Biomedicine and Machine Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #93

body.input: If you were, could be immortal,

metadata.title: Podcast: Daphne Koller: Biomedicine and Machine Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #93

body.input: would you choose to be immortal?

metadata.title: Podcast: Daphne Koller: Biomedicine and Machine Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #93

body.input: Again, I think immortal is a very long time.

metadata.title: Podcast: Daphne Koller: Biomedicine and Machine Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #93

body.input: And I don't know that that would necessarily be something

metadata.title: Podcast: Daphne Koller: Biomedicine and Machine Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #93

body.input: that I would want to aspire to,

metadata.title: Podcast: Daphne Koller: Biomedicine and Machine Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #93

body.input: but I think all of us aspire to an increased health span,

metadata.title: Podcast: Daphne Koller: Biomedicine and Machine Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #93

body.input: I would say, which is an increased amount of time

metadata.title: Podcast: Daphne Koller: Biomedicine and Machine Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #93

body.input: where you're healthy and active

metadata.title: Podcast: Daphne Koller: Biomedicine and Machine Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #93

body.input: and feel as you did when you were 20.

metadata.title: Podcast: Daphne Koller: Biomedicine and Machine Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #93

body.input: And we're nowhere close to that.

metadata.title: Podcast: Daphne Koller: Biomedicine and Machine Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #93

body.input: People deteriorate physically and mentally over time,

metadata.title: Podcast: Daphne Koller: Biomedicine and Machine Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #93

body.input: and that is a very sad phenomenon.

metadata.title: Podcast: Daphne Koller: Biomedicine and Machine Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #93

body.input: So I think a wonderful aspiration would be

metadata.title: Podcast: Daphne Koller: Biomedicine and Machine Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #93

body.input: if we could all live to the biblical 120,

metadata.title: Podcast: Daphne Koller: Biomedicine and Machine Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #93

body.input: maybe, in perfect health.

metadata.title: Podcast: Daphne Koller: Biomedicine and Machine Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #93

body.input: In high quality of life.

metadata.title: Podcast: Daphne Koller: Biomedicine and Machine Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #93

body.input: High quality of life.

metadata.title: Podcast: Daphne Koller: Biomedicine and Machine Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #93

body.input: I think that would be an amazing goal

metadata.title: Podcast: Daphne Koller: Biomedicine and Machine Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #93

body.input: for us to achieve as a society.

metadata.title: Podcast: Daphne Koller: Biomedicine and Machine Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #93

body.input: Now is the right age, 120,

metadata.title: Podcast: Daphne Koller: Biomedicine and Machine Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #93
Podcast: Daphne Koller: Biomedicine and Machine Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #93

body.input: I think that's up for debate,

metadata.title: Podcast: Daphne Koller: Biomedicine and Machine Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #93

body.input: but I think an increased health span

metadata.title: Podcast: Daphne Koller: Biomedicine and Machine Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #93

body.input: is a really worthy goal.

metadata.title: Podcast: Daphne Koller: Biomedicine and Machine Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #93

body.input: And anyway, in a grand time of the age of the universe,

metadata.title: Podcast: Daphne Koller: Biomedicine and Machine Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #93

body.input: it's all pretty short.

metadata.title: Podcast: Daphne Koller: Biomedicine and Machine Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #93

body.input: Up until now, I don't think it's played

metadata.title: Podcast: Daphne Koller: Biomedicine and Machine Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #93

body.input: very much of a significant role,

metadata.title: Podcast: Daphne Koller: Biomedicine and Machine Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #93

metadata.title: Podcast: Daphne Koller: Biomedicine and Machine Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #93

body.input: There's been dribs and drabs

metadata.title: Podcast: Daphne Koller: Biomedicine and Machine Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #93

body.input: and some interesting machine learning

metadata.title: Podcast: Daphne Koller: Biomedicine and Machine Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #93

body.input: that has been applied.

metadata.title: Podcast: Daphne Koller: Biomedicine and Machine Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #93

body.input: I would say machine learning slash data science,

metadata.title: Podcast: Daphne Koller: Biomedicine and Machine Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #93

body.input: but the last few years are starting to change that.

metadata.title: Podcast: Daphne Koller: Biomedicine and Machine Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #93

body.input: So we now see an increase in some large data sets,

metadata.title: Podcast: Daphne Koller: Biomedicine and Machine Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #93

body.input: but equally importantly,

metadata.title: Podcast: Daphne Koller: Biomedicine and Machine Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #93

metadata.title: Podcast: Daphne Koller: Biomedicine and Machine Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #93

body.input: It's not typically the case

metadata.title: Podcast: Daphne Koller: Biomedicine and Machine Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #93

body.input: that people have deliberately proactively used those tools

metadata.title: Podcast: Daphne Koller: Biomedicine and Machine Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #93

body.input: for the purpose of generating data for machine learning.

metadata.title: Podcast: Daphne Koller: Biomedicine and Machine Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #93

body.input: They, to the extent that those techniques

metadata.title: Podcast: Daphne Koller: Biomedicine and Machine Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #93

body.input: have been used for data production,

metadata.title: Podcast: Daphne Koller: Biomedicine and Machine Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #93

body.input: they've been used for data production

metadata.title: Podcast: Daphne Koller: Biomedicine and Machine Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #93

body.input: to drive scientific discovery.

metadata.title: Podcast: Daphne Koller: Biomedicine and Machine Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #93

body.input: And the machine learning came as a sort of byproduct

metadata.title: Podcast: Daphne Koller: Biomedicine and Machine Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #93

body.input: second stage of, oh, now we have a data set,

metadata.title: Podcast: Daphne Koller: Biomedicine and Machine Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #93

body.input: let's do machine learning on that

metadata.title: Podcast: Daphne Koller: Biomedicine and Machine Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #93

metadata.title: Podcast: Daphne Koller: Biomedicine and Machine Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #93

metadata.title: Podcast: Daphne Koller: Biomedicine and Machine Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #93

metadata.title: Podcast: Daphne Koller: Biomedicine and Machine Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #93

body.input: here's this incredible repertoire of methods

metadata.title: Podcast: Daphne Koller: Biomedicine and Machine Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #93

body.input: that bioengineers, cell biologists have come up with,

metadata.title: Podcast: Daphne Koller: Biomedicine and Machine Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #93

body.input: let's see if we can put them together in brand new ways

metadata.title: Podcast: Daphne Koller: Biomedicine and Machine Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #93

metadata.title: Podcast: Daphne Koller: Biomedicine and Machine Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #93

body.input: that machine learning can really be applied on productively

metadata.title: Podcast: Daphne Koller: Biomedicine and Machine Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #93

body.input: to create powerful predictive models

metadata.title: Podcast: Daphne Koller: Biomedicine and Machine Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #93

body.input: that can help us address fundamental problems

metadata.title: Podcast: Daphne Koller: Biomedicine and Machine Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #93

body.input: in human health.

metadata.title: Podcast: Daphne Koller: Biomedicine and Machine Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #93

body.input: So really focus to get, make data the primary focus

metadata.title: Podcast: Daphne Koller: Biomedicine and Machine Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #93

body.input: and the primary goal

metadata.title: Podcast: Daphne Koller: Biomedicine and Machine Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #93

body.input: and find, use the mechanisms of biology and chemistry

metadata.title: Podcast: Daphne Koller: Biomedicine and Machine Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #93

body.input: to create the kinds of data set

body.input: that could allow machine learning to benefit the most.

metadata.title: Podcast: Daphne Koller: Biomedicine and Machine Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #93

metadata.title: Podcast: Daphne Koller: Biomedicine and Machine Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #93

metadata.title: Podcast: Daphne Koller: Biomedicine and Machine Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #93

body.input: So for us, the end goal is helping address challenges

metadata.title: Podcast: Daphne Koller: Biomedicine and Machine Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #93

body.input: in human health.

metadata.title: Podcast: Daphne Koller: Biomedicine and Machine Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #93

body.input: And the method that we've elected to do that

metadata.title: Podcast: Daphne Koller: Biomedicine and Machine Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #93

body.input: is to apply machine learning to build predictive models.

metadata.title: Podcast: Daphne Koller: Biomedicine and Machine Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #93

body.input: And machine learning, in my opinion,

metadata.title: Podcast: Daphne Koller: Biomedicine and Machine Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #93

body.input: and sufficient quality.

metadata.title: Podcast: Daphne Koller: Biomedicine and Machine Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #93

body.input: so as to drive the ability to generate predictive models

metadata.title: Podcast: Daphne Koller: Biomedicine and Machine Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #93

body.input: which subsequently help improve human health?

body.input: So before we dive into the details of that,

metadata.title: Podcast: Daphne Koller: Biomedicine and Machine Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #93

body.input: let me take a step back and ask,

metadata.title: Podcast: Daphne Koller: Biomedicine and Machine Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #93

body.input: when and where was your interest in human health born?

metadata.title: Podcast: Daphne Koller: Biomedicine and Machine Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #93

body.input: Are there moments, events,

metadata.title: Podcast: Daphne Koller: Biomedicine and Machine Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #93

body.input: perhaps if I may ask, tragedies in your own life

metadata.title: Podcast: Daphne Koller: Biomedicine and Machine Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #93

metadata.title: Podcast: Daphne Koller: Biomedicine and Machine Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #93

body.input: actually dates back to the early 2000s

metadata.title: Podcast: Daphne Koller: Biomedicine and Machine Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #93

metadata.title: Podcast: Daphne Koller: Biomedicine and Machine Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #93

metadata.title: Podcast: Daphne Koller: Biomedicine and Machine Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #93

metadata.title: Podcast: Daphne Koller: Biomedicine and Machine Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #93

metadata.title: Podcast: Daphne Koller: Biomedicine and Machine Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #93

metadata.title: Podcast: Daphne Koller: Biomedicine and Machine Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #93

body.input: and also from an aspirational perspective.

metadata.title: Podcast: Daphne Koller: Biomedicine and Machine Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #93

body.input: but they were better than 20 newsgroups.

metadata.title: Podcast: Daphne Koller: Biomedicine and Machine Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #93

body.input: And so I started out, I think, just by wanting to do something

metadata.title: Podcast: Daphne Koller: Biomedicine and Machine Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #93

body.input: that was more, I don't know,

metadata.title: Podcast: Daphne Koller: Biomedicine and Machine Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #93

body.input: societally useful and technically interesting.

metadata.title: Podcast: Daphne Koller: Biomedicine and Machine Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #93

body.input: And then over time became more and more interested

metadata.title: Podcast: Daphne Koller: Biomedicine and Machine Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #93

metadata.title: Podcast: Daphne Koller: Biomedicine and Machine Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #93

body.input: and began to work even sometimes on papers

metadata.title: Podcast: Daphne Koller: Biomedicine and Machine Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #93

body.input: that were just in biology without having a significant

metadata.title: Podcast: Daphne Koller: Biomedicine and Machine Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #93

body.input: machine learning component.

metadata.title: Podcast: Daphne Koller: Biomedicine and Machine Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #93

body.input: I think my interest in drug discovery is partly due

metadata.title: Podcast: Daphne Koller: Biomedicine and Machine Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #93

body.input: to an incident I had with when my father sadly passed away

metadata.title: Podcast: Daphne Koller: Biomedicine and Machine Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #93

body.input: about 12 years ago, he had an autoimmune disease

metadata.title: Podcast: Daphne Koller: Biomedicine and Machine Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #93

body.input: that settled in his lungs.

metadata.title: Podcast: Daphne Koller: Biomedicine and Machine Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #93

body.input: And the doctor's basic said,

metadata.title: Podcast: Daphne Koller: Biomedicine and Machine Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #93

body.input: well, there's only one thing we can do,

metadata.title: Podcast: Daphne Koller: Biomedicine and Machine Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #93

body.input: which is give him prednisone.

metadata.title: Podcast: Daphne Koller: Biomedicine and Machine Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #93

metadata.title: Podcast: Daphne Koller: Biomedicine and Machine Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #93

metadata.title: Podcast: Daphne Koller: Biomedicine and Machine Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #93

body.input: maybe even more, well, it depends for which autoimmune disease,

metadata.title: Podcast: Daphne Koller: Biomedicine and Machine Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #93

body.input: but there are multiple drugs that can help people

metadata.title: Podcast: Daphne Koller: Biomedicine and Machine Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #93

body.input: with autoimmune disease,

metadata.title: Podcast: Daphne Koller: Biomedicine and Machine Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #93

body.input: many of which didn't exist 12 years ago.

metadata.title: Podcast: Daphne Koller: Biomedicine and Machine Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #93

metadata.title: Podcast: Daphne Koller: Biomedicine and Machine Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #93

metadata.title: Podcast: Daphne Koller: Biomedicine and Machine Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #93

metadata.title: Podcast: Daphne Koller: Biomedicine and Machine Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #93

body.input: than we've ever been able to do before.

metadata.title: Podcast: Daphne Koller: Biomedicine and Machine Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #93

metadata.title: Podcast: Daphne Koller: Biomedicine and Machine Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #93

body.input: Can you maybe speak high level?

metadata.title: Podcast: Daphne Koller: Biomedicine and Machine Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #93

body.input: How can learning systems deal with uncertainty?

metadata.title: Podcast: Daphne Koller: Biomedicine and Machine Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #93

body.input: One of the limitations, I think, of a lot of machine

metadata.title: Podcast: Daphne Koller: Biomedicine and Machine Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #93

body.input: learning models is that they come up with an answer

metadata.title: Podcast: Daphne Koller: Biomedicine and Machine Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #93

body.input: and you don't know how much you can believe that answer.

metadata.title: Podcast: Daphne Koller: Biomedicine and Machine Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #93

body.input: And oftentimes the answer is actually quite poorly

metadata.title: Podcast: Daphne Koller: Biomedicine and Machine Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #93

body.input: calibrated relative to its uncertainties.

metadata.title: Podcast: Daphne Koller: Biomedicine and Machine Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #93

body.input: Even if you look at where the confidence that comes out

metadata.title: Podcast: Daphne Koller: Biomedicine and Machine Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #93

body.input: of the, say, the neural network at the end,

metadata.title: Podcast: Daphne Koller: Biomedicine and Machine Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #93

body.input: and you ask how much more likely is an answer

metadata.title: Podcast: Daphne Koller: Biomedicine and Machine Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #93

metadata.title: Podcast: Daphne Koller: Biomedicine and Machine Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #93

body.input: it's not really in any way calibrated to the actual

metadata.title: Podcast: Daphne Koller: Biomedicine and Machine Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #93

body.input: reliability of that network and how true it is.

metadata.title: Podcast: Daphne Koller: Biomedicine and Machine Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #93

body.input: And the further away you move from the training data,

metadata.title: Podcast: Daphne Koller: Biomedicine and Machine Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #93

body.input: the more, not only the more wrong the network is,

metadata.title: Podcast: Daphne Koller: Biomedicine and Machine Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #93

body.input: often it's more wrong and more confident

metadata.title: Podcast: Daphne Koller: Biomedicine and Machine Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #93

body.input: in its wrong answer.

metadata.title: Podcast: Daphne Koller: Biomedicine and Machine Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #93

body.input: And that is a serious issue in a lot of application areas.

metadata.title: Podcast: Daphne Koller: Biomedicine and Machine Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #93

body.input: So when you think, for instance, about medical diagnosis

metadata.title: Podcast: Daphne Koller: Biomedicine and Machine Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #93

body.input: as being maybe an epitome of how problematic

metadata.title: Podcast: Daphne Koller: Biomedicine and Machine Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #93

metadata.title: Podcast: Daphne Koller: Biomedicine and Machine Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #93

metadata.title: Podcast: Daphne Koller: Biomedicine and Machine Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #93

metadata.title: Podcast: Daphne Koller: Biomedicine and Machine Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #93

metadata.title: Podcast: Daphne Koller: Biomedicine and Machine Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #93

body.input: So I think creating more of an understanding of how do you

metadata.title: Podcast: Daphne Koller: Biomedicine and Machine Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #93

metadata.title: Podcast: Daphne Koller: Biomedicine and Machine Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #93

metadata.title: Podcast: Daphne Koller: Biomedicine and Machine Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #93
