body.input: The following is a conversation with Donald Knuth, his second time on this podcast.

metadata.title: Podcast: Donald Knuth: Programming, Algorithms, Hard Problems & the Game of Life | Lex Fridman Podcast #219

body.input: Don is a legendary computer scientist, Touring Award winner, father of algorithm analysis,

metadata.title: Podcast: Donald Knuth: Programming, Algorithms, Hard Problems & the Game of Life | Lex Fridman Podcast #219

body.input: author of the art of computer programming, creator of tech that led to late tech,

metadata.title: Podcast: Donald Knuth: Programming, Algorithms, Hard Problems & the Game of Life | Lex Fridman Podcast #219

body.input: and one of the kindest and most fascinating human beings I've ever got a chance to talk to.

metadata.title: Podcast: Donald Knuth: Programming, Algorithms, Hard Problems & the Game of Life | Lex Fridman Podcast #219

body.input: I wrote him a letter a long time ago, he responded, and the rest, as they say, is history.

metadata.title: Podcast: Donald Knuth: Programming, Algorithms, Hard Problems & the Game of Life | Lex Fridman Podcast #219

body.input: We've interacted many times since then, and every time it's been joyful and inspiring.

metadata.title: Podcast: Donald Knuth: Programming, Algorithms, Hard Problems & the Game of Life | Lex Fridman Podcast #219

body.input: To support this podcast, please check out our sponsors in the description.

metadata.title: Podcast: Donald Knuth: Programming, Algorithms, Hard Problems & the Game of Life | Lex Fridman Podcast #219

body.input: This is the Lex Friedman Podcast, and here is my conversation with Donald Knuth.

metadata.title: Podcast: Donald Knuth: Programming, Algorithms, Hard Problems & the Game of Life | Lex Fridman Podcast #219

body.input: Donald Knuth, your first large scale program, you wrote it in IBM 650 assembler in the summer of 1957.

metadata.title: Podcast: Donald Knuth: Programming, Algorithms, Hard Problems & the Game of Life | Lex Fridman Podcast #219

body.input: I wrote it in decimal machine language. I didn't know about assembler until a year later.

metadata.title: Podcast: Donald Knuth: Programming, Algorithms, Hard Problems & the Game of Life | Lex Fridman Podcast #219

body.input: But the year 1957, the year and the program was a check.

metadata.title: Podcast: Donald Knuth: Programming, Algorithms, Hard Problems & the Game of Life | Lex Fridman Podcast #219

body.input: Yeah, I might have learned about it. Assembler later that summer. I probably did.

metadata.title: Podcast: Donald Knuth: Programming, Algorithms, Hard Problems & the Game of Life | Lex Fridman Podcast #219

body.input: In 1957, hardly anybody had heard of assemblers. You looked at the user manuals.

metadata.title: Podcast: Donald Knuth: Programming, Algorithms, Hard Problems & the Game of Life | Lex Fridman Podcast #219

body.input: How did you write a program for this machine? It would say, you know, you'd say 69,

metadata.title: Podcast: Donald Knuth: Programming, Algorithms, Hard Problems & the Game of Life | Lex Fridman Podcast #219

body.input: which meant load the distributor, and then you would give the address of the number you wanted

metadata.title: Podcast: Donald Knuth: Programming, Algorithms, Hard Problems & the Game of Life | Lex Fridman Podcast #219

body.input: to load into the distributor. Yesterday, my friend Doug Spicer at the Computer History Museum sent me

metadata.title: Podcast: Donald Knuth: Programming, Algorithms, Hard Problems & the Game of Life | Lex Fridman Podcast #219

body.input: a link to something that just went on YouTube. It was the IBM's progress report from 1956,

metadata.title: Podcast: Donald Knuth: Programming, Algorithms, Hard Problems & the Game of Life | Lex Fridman Podcast #219

body.input: which is, you know, very contemporary with 1957. And in 1956, IBM had donated to Stanford University

metadata.title: Podcast: Donald Knuth: Programming, Algorithms, Hard Problems & the Game of Life | Lex Fridman Podcast #219

body.input: an IBM 650, one of the first ones, when they showed a picture of the assembly line for IBM 650s.

metadata.title: Podcast: Donald Knuth: Programming, Algorithms, Hard Problems & the Game of Life | Lex Fridman Podcast #219

body.input: And they said, you know, this is number 500 or something coming off the assembly line.

metadata.title: Podcast: Donald Knuth: Programming, Algorithms, Hard Problems & the Game of Life | Lex Fridman Podcast #219

body.input: And I had never seen so many IBM 650s, except I did in this movie that was on YouTube now.

metadata.title: Podcast: Donald Knuth: Programming, Algorithms, Hard Problems & the Game of Life | Lex Fridman Podcast #219

body.input: And it showed the picture from Stanford. They said, look, you know, we donated one of these

metadata.title: Podcast: Donald Knuth: Programming, Algorithms, Hard Problems & the Game of Life | Lex Fridman Podcast #219

body.input: to Stanford, one to MIT, and they mentioned one other college. And in December of 56,

metadata.title: Podcast: Donald Knuth: Programming, Algorithms, Hard Problems & the Game of Life | Lex Fridman Podcast #219

body.input: they donated to my university, K-STEC. But anyway, they showed a picture then of a class session

metadata.title: Podcast: Donald Knuth: Programming, Algorithms, Hard Problems & the Game of Life | Lex Fridman Podcast #219

body.input: where a guy was teaching programming, and on the blackboard, it said 69, 8000. I mean,

metadata.title: Podcast: Donald Knuth: Programming, Algorithms, Hard Problems & the Game of Life | Lex Fridman Podcast #219

body.input: he was teaching them how to write code for this IBM 650, which was in decimal numbers.

metadata.title: Podcast: Donald Knuth: Programming, Algorithms, Hard Problems & the Game of Life | Lex Fridman Podcast #219

body.input: So the instructions were 10 decimal digits. You had two digits that said what to do,

metadata.title: Podcast: Donald Knuth: Programming, Algorithms, Hard Problems & the Game of Life | Lex Fridman Podcast #219

body.input: four digits to say what to do it to, and four more digits to say where to get your next instruction.

metadata.title: Podcast: Donald Knuth: Programming, Algorithms, Hard Problems & the Game of Life | Lex Fridman Podcast #219

body.input: And there's a manual that describes what each of the numbers mean.

metadata.title: Podcast: Donald Knuth: Programming, Algorithms, Hard Problems & the Game of Life | Lex Fridman Podcast #219

body.input: And the manual was actually one... If the manual had been well written, I probably never would have

metadata.title: Podcast: Donald Knuth: Programming, Algorithms, Hard Problems & the Game of Life | Lex Fridman Podcast #219

body.input: gone into computer science, but it was so badly written, I figured that I must have a talent for

metadata.title: Podcast: Donald Knuth: Programming, Algorithms, Hard Problems & the Game of Life | Lex Fridman Podcast #219

body.input: it because I'm only a freshman and I could write a better manual. And so I had to write

metadata.title: Podcast: Donald Knuth: Programming, Algorithms, Hard Problems & the Game of Life | Lex Fridman Podcast #219

body.input: a better one. And so I started working at the computer center and wrote some manuals then.

metadata.title: Podcast: Donald Knuth: Programming, Algorithms, Hard Problems & the Game of Life | Lex Fridman Podcast #219

body.input: But this was the way we did it. And my first program then was June of 1957.

metadata.title: Podcast: Donald Knuth: Programming, Algorithms, Hard Problems & the Game of Life | Lex Fridman Podcast #219

body.input: The Tic-Tac-Toe.

metadata.title: Podcast: Donald Knuth: Programming, Algorithms, Hard Problems & the Game of Life | Lex Fridman Podcast #219

body.input: No, that was the second program. The third program. The first program was

metadata.title: Podcast: Donald Knuth: Programming, Algorithms, Hard Problems & the Game of Life | Lex Fridman Podcast #219

body.input: factoring a number. So you dial a number on the switches. I mean, you sat at this big mainframe

metadata.title: Podcast: Donald Knuth: Programming, Algorithms, Hard Problems & the Game of Life | Lex Fridman Podcast #219

body.input: and you turn the dials and set a number. And then it would punch out the factors of that number

metadata.title: Podcast: Donald Knuth: Programming, Algorithms, Hard Problems & the Game of Life | Lex Fridman Podcast #219

body.input: on cards.

metadata.title: Podcast: Donald Knuth: Programming, Algorithms, Hard Problems & the Game of Life | Lex Fridman Podcast #219

body.input: So that's the input is the number?

metadata.title: Podcast: Donald Knuth: Programming, Algorithms, Hard Problems & the Game of Life | Lex Fridman Podcast #219

body.input: The input was... Yeah, the input was a number, a tendinium number. And the output was its factors.

metadata.title: Podcast: Donald Knuth: Programming, Algorithms, Hard Problems & the Game of Life | Lex Fridman Podcast #219

body.input: And I wrote that program. I still have a copy of it somewhere.

metadata.title: Podcast: Donald Knuth: Programming, Algorithms, Hard Problems & the Game of Life | Lex Fridman Podcast #219

body.input: How many lines of code do you remember?

metadata.title: Podcast: Donald Knuth: Programming, Algorithms, Hard Problems & the Game of Life | Lex Fridman Podcast #219

body.input: Well, yeah, it started out as about 20, but then I kept having me debug it. And I discovered

metadata.title: Podcast: Donald Knuth: Programming, Algorithms, Hard Problems & the Game of Life | Lex Fridman Podcast #219

body.input: debugging, of course, when I wrote my first program.

metadata.title: Podcast: Donald Knuth: Programming, Algorithms, Hard Problems & the Game of Life | Lex Fridman Podcast #219

body.input: What does debugging look like on a program with just all numbers?

metadata.title: Podcast: Donald Knuth: Programming, Algorithms, Hard Problems & the Game of Life | Lex Fridman Podcast #219

body.input: Well, you sit there and you... I don't remember how I got it into the machine,

metadata.title: Podcast: Donald Knuth: Programming, Algorithms, Hard Problems & the Game of Life | Lex Fridman Podcast #219

body.input: but I think there was a way to punch it on cards. So each instruction would be one card.

metadata.title: Podcast: Donald Knuth: Programming, Algorithms, Hard Problems & the Game of Life | Lex Fridman Podcast #219

body.input: Maybe I could get seven instructions on a card, eight instructions, I don't know. But anyway,

metadata.title: Podcast: Donald Knuth: Programming, Algorithms, Hard Problems & the Game of Life | Lex Fridman Podcast #219

body.input: so I'm sitting there at the console of the machine. I mean, I'm doing this at night when

metadata.title: Podcast: Donald Knuth: Programming, Algorithms, Hard Problems & the Game of Life | Lex Fridman Podcast #219

body.input: nobody else is around.

metadata.title: Podcast: Donald Knuth: Programming, Algorithms, Hard Problems & the Game of Life | Lex Fridman Podcast #219

body.input: Of course.

metadata.title: Podcast: Donald Knuth: Programming, Algorithms, Hard Problems & the Game of Life | Lex Fridman Podcast #219

body.input: And so you have one set of switches where you dial the number I'm inputting, but there's another

metadata.title: Podcast: Donald Knuth: Programming, Algorithms, Hard Problems & the Game of Life | Lex Fridman Podcast #219

body.input: switch that says, okay, now execute one instruction and show me what you did. Or

metadata.title: Podcast: Donald Knuth: Programming, Algorithms, Hard Problems & the Game of Life | Lex Fridman Podcast #219

body.input: there was another four switches, I'd say, stop if you get to that instruction. So I can say,

metadata.title: Podcast: Donald Knuth: Programming, Algorithms, Hard Problems & the Game of Life | Lex Fridman Podcast #219

body.input: now go until you get there again and watch. So I could watch... It would take that number and

metadata.title: Podcast: Donald Knuth: Programming, Algorithms, Hard Problems & the Game of Life | Lex Fridman Podcast #219

body.input: it would divide it by two. And if there's no remainder, then okay, two is a factor.

metadata.title: Podcast: Donald Knuth: Programming, Algorithms, Hard Problems & the Game of Life | Lex Fridman Podcast #219

body.input: So then I work on... But if not divisible by two, divide by three. Keep trying until you know

metadata.title: Podcast: Donald Knuth: Programming, Algorithms, Hard Problems & the Game of Life | Lex Fridman Podcast #219

body.input: you're at the end.

metadata.title: Podcast: Donald Knuth: Programming, Algorithms, Hard Problems & the Game of Life | Lex Fridman Podcast #219

body.input: And you would find a bug if you were just surprised that something weird happened?

metadata.title: Podcast: Donald Knuth: Programming, Algorithms, Hard Problems & the Game of Life | Lex Fridman Podcast #219

body.input: Well, certainly, I mean, first of all, I might've tried to divide by one instead of two,

metadata.title: Podcast: Donald Knuth: Programming, Algorithms, Hard Problems & the Game of Life | Lex Fridman Podcast #219

body.input: off by one error, people make all the time. But maybe I go to the wrong instruction. Maybe

metadata.title: Podcast: Donald Knuth: Programming, Algorithms, Hard Problems & the Game of Life | Lex Fridman Podcast #219

body.input: I left something in a register that I shouldn't have done. But the first bugs were pretty...

metadata.title: Podcast: Donald Knuth: Programming, Algorithms, Hard Problems & the Game of Life | Lex Fridman Podcast #219

body.input: Probably on the first night, I was able to get the factors of 30 as equal to two, three, and five.

metadata.title: Podcast: Donald Knuth: Programming, Algorithms, Hard Problems & the Game of Life | Lex Fridman Podcast #219

body.input: Okay. So you're... Sorry to interrupt. So you're sitting there late at night.

metadata.title: Podcast: Donald Knuth: Programming, Algorithms, Hard Problems & the Game of Life | Lex Fridman Podcast #219

body.input: So it feels like you spent many years late at night working on a computer.

metadata.title: Podcast: Donald Knuth: Programming, Algorithms, Hard Problems & the Game of Life | Lex Fridman Podcast #219

body.input: Oh, yeah.

metadata.title: Podcast: Donald Knuth: Programming, Algorithms, Hard Problems & the Game of Life | Lex Fridman Podcast #219

body.input: So what's that like? So most of the world is sleeping

metadata.title: Podcast: Donald Knuth: Programming, Algorithms, Hard Problems & the Game of Life | Lex Fridman Podcast #219

body.input: and you have to be there at night because that's when you get access to the computer.

metadata.title: Podcast: Donald Knuth: Programming, Algorithms, Hard Problems & the Game of Life | Lex Fridman Podcast #219

body.input: Between my freshman and sophomore year, I didn't need sleep. I used to do all nighters.

metadata.title: Podcast: Donald Knuth: Programming, Algorithms, Hard Problems & the Game of Life | Lex Fridman Podcast #219

body.input: When I was in high school, I used to do the whole student newspaper every Monday night.

metadata.title: Podcast: Donald Knuth: Programming, Algorithms, Hard Problems & the Game of Life | Lex Fridman Podcast #219

body.input: I'd just stay up all night and it would be done on Tuesday morning.

metadata.title: Podcast: Donald Knuth: Programming, Algorithms, Hard Problems & the Game of Life | Lex Fridman Podcast #219

body.input: That was... I didn't get ulcers and stuff like that until later.

metadata.title: Podcast: Donald Knuth: Programming, Algorithms, Hard Problems & the Game of Life | Lex Fridman Podcast #219

body.input: I don't know if you know Rodney Brooks.

metadata.title: Podcast: Donald Knuth: Programming, Algorithms, Hard Problems & the Game of Life | Lex Fridman Podcast #219

body.input: Rod Brooks, of course.

metadata.title: Podcast: Donald Knuth: Programming, Algorithms, Hard Problems & the Game of Life | Lex Fridman Podcast #219

body.input: Yeah, he told me a story that he really looked up to you. He was actually afraid of you.

metadata.title: Podcast: Donald Knuth: Programming, Algorithms, Hard Problems & the Game of Life | Lex Fridman Podcast #219

body.input: Well, vice versa, I must say.

metadata.title: Podcast: Donald Knuth: Programming, Algorithms, Hard Problems & the Game of Life | Lex Fridman Podcast #219

body.input: But he tells a story when you are working on tech

metadata.title: Podcast: Donald Knuth: Programming, Algorithms, Hard Problems & the Game of Life | Lex Fridman Podcast #219

body.input: that they screwed up something with a machine. I think this might have been MIT. I don't know.

metadata.title: Podcast: Donald Knuth: Programming, Algorithms, Hard Problems & the Game of Life | Lex Fridman Podcast #219

body.input: And you were waiting for them to fix the machine so you can get back to work late at night.

metadata.title: Podcast: Donald Knuth: Programming, Algorithms, Hard Problems & the Game of Life | Lex Fridman Podcast #219

body.input: That happened all the time.

metadata.title: Podcast: Donald Knuth: Programming, Algorithms, Hard Problems & the Game of Life | Lex Fridman Podcast #219

body.input: He was really intimidated. He's like, Dr. Knuth is not happy with this.

metadata.title: Podcast: Donald Knuth: Programming, Algorithms, Hard Problems & the Game of Life | Lex Fridman Podcast #219

body.input: That's interesting. But no, the machine at Stanford AI Lab was down an awful lot because

metadata.title: Podcast: Donald Knuth: Programming, Algorithms, Hard Problems & the Game of Life | Lex Fridman Podcast #219

body.input: they had many talented programmers changing the operating system every day.

metadata.title: Podcast: Donald Knuth: Programming, Algorithms, Hard Problems & the Game of Life | Lex Fridman Podcast #219

body.input: Operating system was getting better every day, but it was also crashing.

metadata.title: Podcast: Donald Knuth: Programming, Algorithms, Hard Problems & the Game of Life | Lex Fridman Podcast #219

body.input: So I wrote almost the entire manual for tech during downtime.

metadata.title: Podcast: Donald Knuth: Programming, Algorithms, Hard Problems & the Game of Life | Lex Fridman Podcast #219

body.input: That's another story.

metadata.title: Podcast: Donald Knuth: Programming, Algorithms, Hard Problems & the Game of Life | Lex Fridman Podcast #219

body.input: Okay. Well, he was saying it's a hardware problem. They tried to fix it.

metadata.title: Podcast: Donald Knuth: Programming, Algorithms, Hard Problems & the Game of Life | Lex Fridman Podcast #219

body.input: They reinserted something and smoke was everywhere.

metadata.title: Podcast: Donald Knuth: Programming, Algorithms, Hard Problems & the Game of Life | Lex Fridman Podcast #219

body.input: That didn't happen as often as the operating system.

metadata.title: Podcast: Donald Knuth: Programming, Algorithms, Hard Problems & the Game of Life | Lex Fridman Podcast #219

body.input: It's a funny story because you're saying there's this tall

metadata.title: Podcast: Donald Knuth: Programming, Algorithms, Hard Problems & the Game of Life | Lex Fridman Podcast #219

body.input: Don Knuth that I look up to and there was pressure to fix the computer.

metadata.title: Podcast: Donald Knuth: Programming, Algorithms, Hard Problems & the Game of Life | Lex Fridman Podcast #219

body.input: It's funny. The kind of things we remember that stick in our memory.

metadata.title: Podcast: Donald Knuth: Programming, Algorithms, Hard Problems & the Game of Life | Lex Fridman Podcast #219

body.input: Well, okay. Yeah. Well, I can tell you a bunch of Rodbroke stories too, but let's go back to the 650.

metadata.title: Podcast: Donald Knuth: Programming, Algorithms, Hard Problems & the Game of Life | Lex Fridman Podcast #219

body.input: So I'm debugging my first program and I had more bugs in it than number of lines of code.

metadata.title: Podcast: Donald Knuth: Programming, Algorithms, Hard Problems & the Game of Life | Lex Fridman Podcast #219

body.input: I mean, the number of lines of code kept growing. And let me explain.

metadata.title: Podcast: Donald Knuth: Programming, Algorithms, Hard Problems & the Game of Life | Lex Fridman Podcast #219

body.input: So I had to punch the answers on cards. All right. So suppose I'm factoring the number 30,

metadata.title: Podcast: Donald Knuth: Programming, Algorithms, Hard Problems & the Game of Life | Lex Fridman Podcast #219

body.input: then I got to put two somewhere on the card. I got to put a three somewhere on the card.

metadata.title: Podcast: Donald Knuth: Programming, Algorithms, Hard Problems & the Game of Life | Lex Fridman Podcast #219

body.input: I got to put a five somewhere on the card. Right. And you know what?

metadata.title: Podcast: Donald Knuth: Programming, Algorithms, Hard Problems & the Game of Life | Lex Fridman Podcast #219

body.input: It was my first program. I probably screwed up and it fell off the edge of the card or something

metadata.title: Podcast: Donald Knuth: Programming, Algorithms, Hard Problems & the Game of Life | Lex Fridman Podcast #219

body.input: like that. But I didn't realize that there are some tend to do numbers that have more than eight

metadata.title: Podcast: Donald Knuth: Programming, Algorithms, Hard Problems & the Game of Life | Lex Fridman Podcast #219

body.input: factors. And the card has only 80 columns. And so I need 10 columns for every factor.
