metadata.title: Podcast: Donald Knuth: Programming, Algorithms, Hard Problems & the Game of Life | Lex Fridman Podcast #219

body.input: Well, I like whether it's consciousness or something else, I like the storytelling part

metadata.title: Podcast: Donald Knuth: Programming, Algorithms, Hard Problems & the Game of Life | Lex Fridman Podcast #219

body.input: that we, it feels like for us humans, it feels like there's a concrete story. It's almost like

metadata.title: Podcast: Donald Knuth: Programming, Algorithms, Hard Problems & the Game of Life | Lex Fridman Podcast #219

body.input: literary programming. I don't know what the programming going on on the inside, but I'm

metadata.title: Podcast: Donald Knuth: Programming, Algorithms, Hard Problems & the Game of Life | Lex Fridman Podcast #219

body.input: getting a nice story here about what happened. And it feels like I'm in control and I'm getting

metadata.title: Podcast: Donald Knuth: Programming, Algorithms, Hard Problems & the Game of Life | Lex Fridman Podcast #219

body.input: a nice clear story. So, but it's also possible there's a computation going on. That's really

metadata.title: Podcast: Donald Knuth: Programming, Algorithms, Hard Problems & the Game of Life | Lex Fridman Podcast #219

body.input: messy. There's a bunch of different competing ideas. And in the end, it just kind of generates

metadata.title: Podcast: Donald Knuth: Programming, Algorithms, Hard Problems & the Game of Life | Lex Fridman Podcast #219

body.input: a story for you to a consistent story for you to believe. And that makes it all nice.

metadata.title: Podcast: Donald Knuth: Programming, Algorithms, Hard Problems & the Game of Life | Lex Fridman Podcast #219

body.input: Yeah. And so I prefer to talk about things that I have some expertise and then things

metadata.title: Podcast: Donald Knuth: Programming, Algorithms, Hard Problems & the Game of Life | Lex Fridman Podcast #219

body.input: for which I, which I'm only a, you know, on the sideline.

metadata.title: Podcast: Donald Knuth: Programming, Algorithms, Hard Problems & the Game of Life | Lex Fridman Podcast #219

body.input: So there's a tricky thing. I don't know if you have any expertise in this.

metadata.title: Podcast: Donald Knuth: Programming, Algorithms, Hard Problems & the Game of Life | Lex Fridman Podcast #219

body.input: You might be a little bit on the sideline. It'd be interesting to ask though.

metadata.title: Podcast: Donald Knuth: Programming, Algorithms, Hard Problems & the Game of Life | Lex Fridman Podcast #219

body.input: What are your thoughts on cellular automata and the game of life?

metadata.title: Podcast: Donald Knuth: Programming, Algorithms, Hard Problems & the Game of Life | Lex Fridman Podcast #219

body.input: Have you ever played with those kinds of little games?

metadata.title: Podcast: Donald Knuth: Programming, Algorithms, Hard Problems & the Game of Life | Lex Fridman Podcast #219

body.input: I think the game of life is wonderful and shows all kind of stuff about how things

metadata.title: Podcast: Donald Knuth: Programming, Algorithms, Hard Problems & the Game of Life | Lex Fridman Podcast #219

body.input: can evolve without the creator understanding anything more than the power of learning in a

metadata.title: Podcast: Donald Knuth: Programming, Algorithms, Hard Problems & the Game of Life | Lex Fridman Podcast #219

body.input: way. But to me, the most important thing about the game of life is how it focused for me

metadata.title: Podcast: Donald Knuth: Programming, Algorithms, Hard Problems & the Game of Life | Lex Fridman Podcast #219

body.input: what it meant to have free will or not. Because the game of life is obviously totally deterministic.

metadata.title: Podcast: Donald Knuth: Programming, Algorithms, Hard Problems & the Game of Life | Lex Fridman Podcast #219

body.input: Yes. And I find it hard to believe that anybody who's ever had children cannot believe in free

metadata.title: Podcast: Donald Knuth: Programming, Algorithms, Hard Problems & the Game of Life | Lex Fridman Podcast #219

body.input: will. On the other hand, this makes it crystal clear. John Conway said,

metadata.title: Podcast: Donald Knuth: Programming, Algorithms, Hard Problems & the Game of Life | Lex Fridman Podcast #219

body.input: he wondered whether it was immoral to shut the computer off after he got into a particularly

metadata.title: Podcast: Donald Knuth: Programming, Algorithms, Hard Problems & the Game of Life | Lex Fridman Podcast #219

body.input: interesting play of the game of life. Wow. Yeah. So there is, to me, the reason I love the game

metadata.title: Podcast: Donald Knuth: Programming, Algorithms, Hard Problems & the Game of Life | Lex Fridman Podcast #219

body.input: of life is exactly as you said, a clear illustration that from simple initial conditions with simple

metadata.title: Podcast: Donald Knuth: Programming, Algorithms, Hard Problems & the Game of Life | Lex Fridman Podcast #219

body.input: rules, you know exactly how the system is operating, it's deterministic. And yet,

metadata.title: Podcast: Donald Knuth: Programming, Algorithms, Hard Problems & the Game of Life | Lex Fridman Podcast #219

body.input: if you allow yourself to lose that knowledge a little bit enough to see the bigger organisms

metadata.title: Podcast: Donald Knuth: Programming, Algorithms, Hard Problems & the Game of Life | Lex Fridman Podcast #219

body.input: that emerge, and then all of a sudden they seem conscious, they seem not conscious, but living.

metadata.title: Podcast: Donald Knuth: Programming, Algorithms, Hard Problems & the Game of Life | Lex Fridman Podcast #219

body.input: If the universe is finite, we're all living in the game of life to slow down. I mean, it's sped up a lot.

metadata.title: Podcast: Donald Knuth: Programming, Algorithms, Hard Problems & the Game of Life | Lex Fridman Podcast #219

body.input: But do you think technically some of the ideas that you used for analysis of algorithms

metadata.title: Podcast: Donald Knuth: Programming, Algorithms, Hard Problems & the Game of Life | Lex Fridman Podcast #219

body.input: can be used to analyze the game of life? Can we make sense of it or is it too weird?

metadata.title: Podcast: Donald Knuth: Programming, Algorithms, Hard Problems & the Game of Life | Lex Fridman Podcast #219

body.input: Yeah. I mean, I've got a dozen exercises in volume for

metadata.title: Podcast: Donald Knuth: Programming, Algorithms, Hard Problems & the Game of Life | Lex Fridman Podcast #219

body.input: Fastical 6 that actually work rather well for that purpose. But Bill Gospers came up with the

metadata.title: Podcast: Donald Knuth: Programming, Algorithms, Hard Problems & the Game of Life | Lex Fridman Podcast #219

body.input: algorithm that allows Golly to run thousands and thousands of times faster.

metadata.title: Podcast: Donald Knuth: Programming, Algorithms, Hard Problems & the Game of Life | Lex Fridman Podcast #219

body.input: You know the website called Golly?

metadata.title: Podcast: Donald Knuth: Programming, Algorithms, Hard Problems & the Game of Life | Lex Fridman Podcast #219

body.input: It simulates the cellular automata, a game of life.

metadata.title: Podcast: Donald Knuth: Programming, Algorithms, Hard Problems & the Game of Life | Lex Fridman Podcast #219

body.input: Yeah, you got to check it out.

metadata.title: Podcast: Donald Knuth: Programming, Algorithms, Hard Problems & the Game of Life | Lex Fridman Podcast #219

body.input: Can I ask you about John Conway?

metadata.title: Podcast: Donald Knuth: Programming, Algorithms, Hard Problems & the Game of Life | Lex Fridman Podcast #219

body.input: Yes. In fact, I'm just reading now the issue of mathematical intelligence that came in last

metadata.title: Podcast: Donald Knuth: Programming, Algorithms, Hard Problems & the Game of Life | Lex Fridman Podcast #219

body.input: week. It's a whole issue devoted to remembrance of him.

metadata.title: Podcast: Donald Knuth: Programming, Algorithms, Hard Problems & the Game of Life | Lex Fridman Podcast #219

body.input: Did you know him?

metadata.title: Podcast: Donald Knuth: Programming, Algorithms, Hard Problems & the Game of Life | Lex Fridman Podcast #219

body.input: I slept overnight in his house several times.

metadata.title: Podcast: Donald Knuth: Programming, Algorithms, Hard Problems & the Game of Life | Lex Fridman Podcast #219

body.input: He recently passed away.

metadata.title: Podcast: Donald Knuth: Programming, Algorithms, Hard Problems & the Game of Life | Lex Fridman Podcast #219

body.input: Yeah, he died a year ago, May, I think it was, of COVID.

metadata.title: Podcast: Donald Knuth: Programming, Algorithms, Hard Problems & the Game of Life | Lex Fridman Podcast #219

body.input: What are some memories of him, of his work that stand out for you?

metadata.title: Podcast: Donald Knuth: Programming, Algorithms, Hard Problems & the Game of Life | Lex Fridman Podcast #219

body.input: On a technical level, did any of his work inspire you? On a personal level, did he himself inspire

metadata.title: Podcast: Donald Knuth: Programming, Algorithms, Hard Problems & the Game of Life | Lex Fridman Podcast #219

body.input: you in some way?

metadata.title: Podcast: Donald Knuth: Programming, Algorithms, Hard Problems & the Game of Life | Lex Fridman Podcast #219

body.input: Absolutely, all of those things. But let's see, when did I first meet him? I guess I first met him

metadata.title: Podcast: Donald Knuth: Programming, Algorithms, Hard Problems & the Game of Life | Lex Fridman Podcast #219

body.input: at Oxford in 1967 when I was-

metadata.title: Podcast: Donald Knuth: Programming, Algorithms, Hard Problems & the Game of Life | Lex Fridman Podcast #219

body.input: Wow. Okay, that's a long time ago.

metadata.title: Podcast: Donald Knuth: Programming, Algorithms, Hard Problems & the Game of Life | Lex Fridman Podcast #219

body.input: Yeah. You were minus 20 years old or something, I don't know, 1967.

metadata.title: Podcast: Donald Knuth: Programming, Algorithms, Hard Problems & the Game of Life | Lex Fridman Podcast #219

body.input: But there was a conference where-

metadata.title: Podcast: Donald Knuth: Programming, Algorithms, Hard Problems & the Game of Life | Lex Fridman Podcast #219

body.input: I was 20 years old.

metadata.title: Podcast: Donald Knuth: Programming, Algorithms, Hard Problems & the Game of Life | Lex Fridman Podcast #219

body.input: I think I was speaking about something that's known as the Knuth Bendix algorithm now, but he

metadata.title: Podcast: Donald Knuth: Programming, Algorithms, Hard Problems & the Game of Life | Lex Fridman Podcast #219

body.input: gave a famous talk about knots. I didn't know at the time, but anyway, that talk had now

metadata.title: Podcast: Donald Knuth: Programming, Algorithms, Hard Problems & the Game of Life | Lex Fridman Podcast #219

body.input: the source of thousands and thousands of papers since then. He was reported on something that he

metadata.title: Podcast: Donald Knuth: Programming, Algorithms, Hard Problems & the Game of Life | Lex Fridman Podcast #219

body.input: had done in high school, almost 10 years earlier before this conference, but he never published it.

metadata.title: Podcast: Donald Knuth: Programming, Algorithms, Hard Problems & the Game of Life | Lex Fridman Podcast #219

body.input: And he climaxed his talk by building some knots. You have these little plastic things that you

metadata.title: Podcast: Donald Knuth: Programming, Algorithms, Hard Problems & the Game of Life | Lex Fridman Podcast #219

body.input: can stick together. It's something like Lego, but easier. And so he made a whole bunch of knots

metadata.title: Podcast: Donald Knuth: Programming, Algorithms, Hard Problems & the Game of Life | Lex Fridman Podcast #219

body.input: in front of the audience and so on, and then disassembled it. So it was a dramatic lecture

metadata.title: Podcast: Donald Knuth: Programming, Algorithms, Hard Problems & the Game of Life | Lex Fridman Podcast #219

body.input: before he had learned how to give even more dramatic lectures later.

metadata.title: Podcast: Donald Knuth: Programming, Algorithms, Hard Problems & the Game of Life | Lex Fridman Podcast #219

body.input: All right. And-

metadata.title: Podcast: Donald Knuth: Programming, Algorithms, Hard Problems & the Game of Life | Lex Fridman Podcast #219

body.input: Were you at that lecture?

metadata.title: Podcast: Donald Knuth: Programming, Algorithms, Hard Problems & the Game of Life | Lex Fridman Podcast #219

body.input: And I was there, yeah, because I was at the same conference.

metadata.title: Podcast: Donald Knuth: Programming, Algorithms, Hard Problems & the Game of Life | Lex Fridman Podcast #219

body.input: And for some reason, I happened to be in Calgary at the same day that he was visiting Calgary.

metadata.title: Podcast: Donald Knuth: Programming, Algorithms, Hard Problems & the Game of Life | Lex Fridman Podcast #219

body.input: And it was the spring of 72, I'm pretty sure. And we had lunch together,

metadata.title: Podcast: Donald Knuth: Programming, Algorithms, Hard Problems & the Game of Life | Lex Fridman Podcast #219

body.input: and he wrote down during the lunch on a napkin all of the facts about what he called numbers.

metadata.title: Podcast: Donald Knuth: Programming, Algorithms, Hard Problems & the Game of Life | Lex Fridman Podcast #219

body.input: And he covered the napkin with the theorems about his idea of numbers. And I thought it was

metadata.title: Podcast: Donald Knuth: Programming, Algorithms, Hard Problems & the Game of Life | Lex Fridman Podcast #219

body.input: incredibly beautiful. And later in 1972, my sabbatical year began and I went to Norway.

metadata.title: Podcast: Donald Knuth: Programming, Algorithms, Hard Problems & the Game of Life | Lex Fridman Podcast #219

body.input: And in December of that year, in the middle of the night, the thought came to me,

metadata.title: Podcast: Donald Knuth: Programming, Algorithms, Hard Problems & the Game of Life | Lex Fridman Podcast #219

body.input: you know, Conway's theory about numbers would be a great thing to teach students how to

metadata.title: Podcast: Donald Knuth: Programming, Algorithms, Hard Problems & the Game of Life | Lex Fridman Podcast #219

body.input: invent research and what the joys are of research. And so I said, and I had also

metadata.title: Podcast: Donald Knuth: Programming, Algorithms, Hard Problems & the Game of Life | Lex Fridman Podcast #219

body.input: read a book in dialogue by Alfred Renier, kind of a Socratic thing where the two characters

metadata.title: Podcast: Donald Knuth: Programming, Algorithms, Hard Problems & the Game of Life | Lex Fridman Podcast #219

body.input: were talking to each other about mathematics. And so at the end in the morning, I woke up my

metadata.title: Podcast: Donald Knuth: Programming, Algorithms, Hard Problems & the Game of Life | Lex Fridman Podcast #219

body.input: wife and said, Jill, I think I want to write a book about Conway's theory. And you know,

metadata.title: Podcast: Donald Knuth: Programming, Algorithms, Hard Problems & the Game of Life | Lex Fridman Podcast #219

body.input: I'm supposed to be writing the auto computer program and doing all this other stuff, but I

metadata.title: Podcast: Donald Knuth: Programming, Algorithms, Hard Problems & the Game of Life | Lex Fridman Podcast #219

body.input: really want to write this other book. And so we made this plan, but I said, I thought I could

metadata.title: Podcast: Donald Knuth: Programming, Algorithms, Hard Problems & the Game of Life | Lex Fridman Podcast #219

body.input: write it in a week. And we made the plan then. So in January, I rented a room in a hotel in

metadata.title: Podcast: Donald Knuth: Programming, Algorithms, Hard Problems & the Game of Life | Lex Fridman Podcast #219

body.input: downtown Oslo. We were in sabbatical in Norway. And I rented the hotel in downtown Oslo and

metadata.title: Podcast: Donald Knuth: Programming, Algorithms, Hard Problems & the Game of Life | Lex Fridman Podcast #219

body.input: did nothing else except write Conway's theory. And I changed the name to surreal numbers.

metadata.title: Podcast: Donald Knuth: Programming, Algorithms, Hard Problems & the Game of Life | Lex Fridman Podcast #219

body.input: And so this book is now published as surreal number. And we figured out, we'd always wondered

metadata.title: Podcast: Donald Knuth: Programming, Algorithms, Hard Problems & the Game of Life | Lex Fridman Podcast #219

body.input: do you like to have an affair in a hotel room? So we figured out that she would visit me twice

metadata.title: Podcast: Donald Knuth: Programming, Algorithms, Hard Problems & the Game of Life | Lex Fridman Podcast #219

body.input: during the week and things like this. We would try to sneak in. This hotel was run by a mission

metadata.title: Podcast: Donald Knuth: Programming, Algorithms, Hard Problems & the Game of Life | Lex Fridman Podcast #219

body.input: organization. These ladies were probably very strict, but anyway. So and-

metadata.title: Podcast: Donald Knuth: Programming, Algorithms, Hard Problems & the Game of Life | Lex Fridman Podcast #219

body.input: It's a wild week in every way.

metadata.title: Podcast: Donald Knuth: Programming, Algorithms, Hard Problems & the Game of Life | Lex Fridman Podcast #219

body.input: But the thing is, I had lost that napkin in which he wrote the theory, but I looked for it,

metadata.title: Podcast: Donald Knuth: Programming, Algorithms, Hard Problems & the Game of Life | Lex Fridman Podcast #219

body.input: but I couldn't find it. So I tried to recreate from memory what he had told me at that lunch in

metadata.title: Podcast: Donald Knuth: Programming, Algorithms, Hard Problems & the Game of Life | Lex Fridman Podcast #219

body.input: Calgary. And as I wrote the book, I was going through exactly what the characters in the book

metadata.title: Podcast: Donald Knuth: Programming, Algorithms, Hard Problems & the Game of Life | Lex Fridman Podcast #219

body.input: were supposed to be doing. So I start with the two axioms that start out the whole thing. And

metadata.title: Podcast: Donald Knuth: Programming, Algorithms, Hard Problems & the Game of Life | Lex Fridman Podcast #219

body.input: everything is defined, flows from that, but you have to discover why. And every mistake that I

metadata.title: Podcast: Donald Knuth: Programming, Algorithms, Hard Problems & the Game of Life | Lex Fridman Podcast #219

body.input: make as I'm trying to discover it, my characters make too. And so it's a long, long story. But I

metadata.title: Podcast: Donald Knuth: Programming, Algorithms, Hard Problems & the Game of Life | Lex Fridman Podcast #219

body.input: worked through this week and it was one of the most intense weeks of my life. And I described it

metadata.title: Podcast: Donald Knuth: Programming, Algorithms, Hard Problems & the Game of Life | Lex Fridman Podcast #219

body.input: in other places. But anyway, after six days, I finished it. And on the seventh day, I rested.

metadata.title: Podcast: Donald Knuth: Programming, Algorithms, Hard Problems & the Game of Life | Lex Fridman Podcast #219

body.input: And I sent to my secretary to type it. It was flowing as I was writing it, faster than I could

metadata.title: Podcast: Donald Knuth: Programming, Algorithms, Hard Problems & the Game of Life | Lex Fridman Podcast #219

body.input: think almost. But after I finished it and tried to write a letter to my secretary telling her how to

metadata.title: Podcast: Donald Knuth: Programming, Algorithms, Hard Problems & the Game of Life | Lex Fridman Podcast #219

body.input: type it, I couldn't write anymore. She gave it everything. The muse had left me completely.

metadata.title: Podcast: Donald Knuth: Programming, Algorithms, Hard Problems & the Game of Life | Lex Fridman Podcast #219

body.input: Can you explain how that week could have happened? That seems like such a magical week of productivity.

metadata.title: Podcast: Donald Knuth: Programming, Algorithms, Hard Problems & the Game of Life | Lex Fridman Podcast #219

body.input: I have no idea, but anyway, it was almost as if I was channeling. So the book was typed,

metadata.title: Podcast: Donald Knuth: Programming, Algorithms, Hard Problems & the Game of Life | Lex Fridman Podcast #219

body.input: I sent it to Conway. And he said, well, Don, you got the one axiom wrong.

metadata.title: Podcast: Donald Knuth: Programming, Algorithms, Hard Problems & the Game of Life | Lex Fridman Podcast #219

body.input: There's a difference between less than or equal and not greater than. The opposite of being greater

metadata.title: Podcast: Donald Knuth: Programming, Algorithms, Hard Problems & the Game of Life | Lex Fridman Podcast #219

body.input: than and less than or equal. But anyway, technically it can make a difference when you're developing

metadata.title: Podcast: Donald Knuth: Programming, Algorithms, Hard Problems & the Game of Life | Lex Fridman Podcast #219

body.input: a logical theory. And the way I had chosen was harder to do than John's original.

metadata.title: Podcast: Donald Knuth: Programming, Algorithms, Hard Problems & the Game of Life | Lex Fridman Podcast #219

body.input: And we visited him at his house in Cambridge in April. We took a boat actually from Norway

metadata.title: Podcast: Donald Knuth: Programming, Algorithms, Hard Problems & the Game of Life | Lex Fridman Podcast #219

body.input: over across the channel and so on and stayed with him for some days. And he talked about all kinds

metadata.title: Podcast: Donald Knuth: Programming, Algorithms, Hard Problems & the Game of Life | Lex Fridman Podcast #219

body.input: of things. He had puzzles that I'd never heard of before. He had a great way to

metadata.title: Podcast: Donald Knuth: Programming, Algorithms, Hard Problems & the Game of Life | Lex Fridman Podcast #219

body.input: to solve the game of solitaire. Many of the common interests that he had never written up.

metadata.title: Podcast: Donald Knuth: Programming, Algorithms, Hard Problems & the Game of Life | Lex Fridman Podcast #219

body.input: But anyway, then in the summertime, I took another week off and went to a place in

metadata.title: Podcast: Donald Knuth: Programming, Algorithms, Hard Problems & the Game of Life | Lex Fridman Podcast #219

body.input: in the mountains of Norway and rewrote the book using the correct axiom.

metadata.title: Podcast: Donald Knuth: Programming, Algorithms, Hard Problems & the Game of Life | Lex Fridman Podcast #219

body.input: So that was the most intensive connection with Conway. After that...

metadata.title: Podcast: Donald Knuth: Programming, Algorithms, Hard Problems & the Game of Life | Lex Fridman Podcast #219

body.input: It started with a napkin.

metadata.title: Podcast: Donald Knuth: Programming, Algorithms, Hard Problems & the Game of Life | Lex Fridman Podcast #219

body.input: It started with a napkin. But we would run into each other.

metadata.title: Podcast: Donald Knuth: Programming, Algorithms, Hard Problems & the Game of Life | Lex Fridman Podcast #219

body.input: The next really... I was giving lectures in Montreal. I was giving a series of

metadata.title: Podcast: Donald Knuth: Programming, Algorithms, Hard Problems & the Game of Life | Lex Fridman Podcast #219

body.input: seven lectures about a topic called stable marriages. And he arrived in Montreal

metadata.title: Podcast: Donald Knuth: Programming, Algorithms, Hard Problems & the Game of Life | Lex Fridman Podcast #219

body.input: between my sixth and seventh lecture. And we met at a party. And I started telling him about the

metadata.title: Podcast: Donald Knuth: Programming, Algorithms, Hard Problems & the Game of Life | Lex Fridman Podcast #219

body.input: topic I was doing. And he sat and thought about it. He came up with a beautiful theory to show that

metadata.title: Podcast: Donald Knuth: Programming, Algorithms, Hard Problems & the Game of Life | Lex Fridman Podcast #219

body.input: the... I mean, in technical terms, it's that the set of all stable marriages forms a lattice.

metadata.title: Podcast: Donald Knuth: Programming, Algorithms, Hard Problems & the Game of Life | Lex Fridman Podcast #219

body.input: It forms a lattice. And there was a simple way to find the greatest lower bound of two stable

metadata.title: Podcast: Donald Knuth: Programming, Algorithms, Hard Problems & the Game of Life | Lex Fridman Podcast #219

body.input: fairings and least upper bound of two stable marrying. And so I could use it in my lecture

metadata.title: Podcast: Donald Knuth: Programming, Algorithms, Hard Problems & the Game of Life | Lex Fridman Podcast #219

body.input: the next day. And he came up with this theorem during the party. It's a distributive last.

metadata.title: Podcast: Donald Knuth: Programming, Algorithms, Hard Problems & the Game of Life | Lex Fridman Podcast #219

body.input: And I mean, it added greatly to the theory of stable matching.

metadata.title: Podcast: Donald Knuth: Programming, Algorithms, Hard Problems & the Game of Life | Lex Fridman Podcast #219

body.input: So you mentioned your wife, Jill. You mentioned stable marriage.

metadata.title: Podcast: Donald Knuth: Programming, Algorithms, Hard Problems & the Game of Life | Lex Fridman Podcast #219

body.input: Can you tell the story of how you two met?

metadata.title: Podcast: Donald Knuth: Programming, Algorithms, Hard Problems & the Game of Life | Lex Fridman Podcast #219

body.input: So we celebrated 60 years of Wedded Bliss last month. And we met because I was dating her roommate.

metadata.title: Podcast: Donald Knuth: Programming, Algorithms, Hard Problems & the Game of Life | Lex Fridman Podcast #219

body.input: This was my sophomore year, her freshman year. I was dating her roommate and I wanted her advice on

metadata.title: Podcast: Donald Knuth: Programming, Algorithms, Hard Problems & the Game of Life | Lex Fridman Podcast #219

body.input: strategy or something like this. And anyway, I found I enjoyed her advice better than her.

metadata.title: Podcast: Donald Knuth: Programming, Algorithms, Hard Problems & the Game of Life | Lex Fridman Podcast #219

body.input: I enjoyed her roommate.

metadata.title: Podcast: Donald Knuth: Programming, Algorithms, Hard Problems & the Game of Life | Lex Fridman Podcast #219

body.input: You guys were majoring the same thing?

metadata.title: Podcast: Donald Knuth: Programming, Algorithms, Hard Problems & the Game of Life | Lex Fridman Podcast #219

body.input: No, no, no.

metadata.title: Podcast: Donald Knuth: Programming, Algorithms, Hard Problems & the Game of Life | Lex Fridman Podcast #219

body.input: Because I read something about working on a computer in grad school on a difficult computer

metadata.title: Podcast: Donald Knuth: Programming, Algorithms, Hard Problems & the Game of Life | Lex Fridman Podcast #219

body.input: science topic.

metadata.title: Podcast: Donald Knuth: Programming, Algorithms, Hard Problems & the Game of Life | Lex Fridman Podcast #219

body.input: So she's an artist and I'm a geek.

metadata.title: Podcast: Donald Knuth: Programming, Algorithms, Hard Problems & the Game of Life | Lex Fridman Podcast #219

body.input: And what was she doing with a computer science book? Or I read the, was it the manual that she

metadata.title: Podcast: Donald Knuth: Programming, Algorithms, Hard Problems & the Game of Life | Lex Fridman Podcast #219

body.input: was reading? What was she reading?

metadata.title: Podcast: Donald Knuth: Programming, Algorithms, Hard Problems & the Game of Life | Lex Fridman Podcast #219

body.input: I wrote the manual that she had to take a class in computer science.

metadata.title: Podcast: Donald Knuth: Programming, Algorithms, Hard Problems & the Game of Life | Lex Fridman Podcast #219

body.input: Okay.

metadata.title: Podcast: Donald Knuth: Programming, Algorithms, Hard Problems & the Game of Life | Lex Fridman Podcast #219

body.input: So you're the tutor?

metadata.title: Podcast: Donald Knuth: Programming, Algorithms, Hard Problems & the Game of Life | Lex Fridman Podcast #219

body.input: No, no. Yeah. No, we, there were terrible times trying to learn certain concepts, but I learned

metadata.title: Podcast: Donald Knuth: Programming, Algorithms, Hard Problems & the Game of Life | Lex Fridman Podcast #219

body.input: art from her. And so we worked together occasionally in design projects, but every year

metadata.title: Podcast: Donald Knuth: Programming, Algorithms, Hard Problems & the Game of Life | Lex Fridman Podcast #219

body.input: we write a Christmas card and we each have to compromise our own notions of beauty.

metadata.title: Podcast: Donald Knuth: Programming, Algorithms, Hard Problems & the Game of Life | Lex Fridman Podcast #219

body.input: When did you fall in love with her?

metadata.title: Podcast: Donald Knuth: Programming, Algorithms, Hard Problems & the Game of Life | Lex Fridman Podcast #219

body.input: That day that I asked her about her roommate.

metadata.title: Podcast: Donald Knuth: Programming, Algorithms, Hard Problems & the Game of Life | Lex Fridman Podcast #219

body.input: Okay. Okay. So you're, I don't mind telling these things, depending on how far you go, but

metadata.title: Podcast: Donald Knuth: Programming, Algorithms, Hard Problems & the Game of Life | Lex Fridman Podcast #219

body.input: let me tell you this, that I never really enjoyed kissing until I found how she did it.

metadata.title: Podcast: Donald Knuth: Programming, Algorithms, Hard Problems & the Game of Life | Lex Fridman Podcast #219

body.input: Wow. And 60 years. Is there a secret you can say in terms of stable marriages of how you

metadata.title: Podcast: Donald Knuth: Programming, Algorithms, Hard Problems & the Game of Life | Lex Fridman Podcast #219

body.input: stayed together so long?

metadata.title: Podcast: Donald Knuth: Programming, Algorithms, Hard Problems & the Game of Life | Lex Fridman Podcast #219

body.input: The topic stable marriage, by the way, is not, is a technical term.

metadata.title: Podcast: Donald Knuth: Programming, Algorithms, Hard Problems & the Game of Life | Lex Fridman Podcast #219

body.input: It's a joke, Don.

metadata.title: Podcast: Donald Knuth: Programming, Algorithms, Hard Problems & the Game of Life | Lex Fridman Podcast #219

body.input: But two different people will have to learn how to compromise and work together and

metadata.title: Podcast: Donald Knuth: Programming, Algorithms, Hard Problems & the Game of Life | Lex Fridman Podcast #219

body.input: you're going to have ups and downs and crises and so on. And so as long as you don't

metadata.title: Podcast: Donald Knuth: Programming, Algorithms, Hard Problems & the Game of Life | Lex Fridman Podcast #219

body.input: set your expectation on having 24 hours of bliss, then there's a lot of hope for stability. But if

metadata.title: Podcast: Donald Knuth: Programming, Algorithms, Hard Problems & the Game of Life | Lex Fridman Podcast #219

body.input: you decide that there's going to be no frustration, then.

metadata.title: Podcast: Donald Knuth: Programming, Algorithms, Hard Problems & the Game of Life | Lex Fridman Podcast #219

body.input: So you're going to have to compromise on your notions of beauty when you write Christmas cards.

metadata.title: Podcast: Donald Knuth: Programming, Algorithms, Hard Problems & the Game of Life | Lex Fridman Podcast #219

body.input: That's it.

metadata.title: Podcast: Donald Knuth: Programming, Algorithms, Hard Problems & the Game of Life | Lex Fridman Podcast #219

body.input: You mentioned that Richard Feynman was someone you looked up to.

metadata.title: Podcast: Donald Knuth: Programming, Algorithms, Hard Problems & the Game of Life | Lex Fridman Podcast #219

body.input: Yeah.

metadata.title: Podcast: Donald Knuth: Programming, Algorithms, Hard Problems & the Game of Life | Lex Fridman Podcast #219

body.input: Probably you've met him in Caltech.

metadata.title: Podcast: Donald Knuth: Programming, Algorithms, Hard Problems & the Game of Life | Lex Fridman Podcast #219

body.input: Well, we knew each other. Yeah, at Caltech for sure.

metadata.title: Podcast: Donald Knuth: Programming, Algorithms, Hard Problems & the Game of Life | Lex Fridman Podcast #219

body.input: You are one of the seminal personalities of computer science. He's one for physics.

metadata.title: Podcast: Donald Knuth: Programming, Algorithms, Hard Problems & the Game of Life | Lex Fridman Podcast #219

body.input: Is there specific things you picked up from him by way of inspiration or?

metadata.title: Podcast: Donald Knuth: Programming, Algorithms, Hard Problems & the Game of Life | Lex Fridman Podcast #219

body.input: So we used to go to each other's lectures.

metadata.title: Podcast: Donald Knuth: Programming, Algorithms, Hard Problems & the Game of Life | Lex Fridman Podcast #219

body.input: And but if I saw him sitting in the front row, it would throw me for a loop, actually. And I

metadata.title: Podcast: Donald Knuth: Programming, Algorithms, Hard Problems & the Game of Life | Lex Fridman Podcast #219

body.input: would miss a few sentences. What unique story do I have? I mean, I often refer to his time in Brazil

metadata.title: Podcast: Donald Knuth: Programming, Algorithms, Hard Problems & the Game of Life | Lex Fridman Podcast #219

body.input: where he essentially said they were teaching all the physics students the wrong way. They were

metadata.title: Podcast: Donald Knuth: Programming, Algorithms, Hard Problems & the Game of Life | Lex Fridman Podcast #219

body.input: just learning how to pass exams and not learning any physics. And he said, if you want me to prove

metadata.title: Podcast: Donald Knuth: Programming, Algorithms, Hard Problems & the Game of Life | Lex Fridman Podcast #219

body.input: it, here I'll turn to any page of this textbook and I'll tell you what's wrong with this page.

metadata.title: Podcast: Donald Knuth: Programming, Algorithms, Hard Problems & the Game of Life | Lex Fridman Podcast #219

body.input: And he did so. And the textbook had been written by his host. And it was a big embarrassing

metadata.title: Podcast: Donald Knuth: Programming, Algorithms, Hard Problems & the Game of Life | Lex Fridman Podcast #219

body.input: incident, but he had previously asked his host if he was supposed to tell the truth.

metadata.title: Podcast: Donald Knuth: Programming, Algorithms, Hard Problems & the Game of Life | Lex Fridman Podcast #219

body.input: But anyway, it epitomizes the way education goes wrong in all kinds of fields and has to periodically

metadata.title: Podcast: Donald Knuth: Programming, Algorithms, Hard Problems & the Game of Life | Lex Fridman Podcast #219

body.input: be brought back from a process of giving credentials to a process of giving knowledge.

metadata.title: Podcast: Donald Knuth: Programming, Algorithms, Hard Problems & the Game of Life | Lex Fridman Podcast #219

body.input: And that's probably a story that continues to this day in a bunch of places where it's too easy for

metadata.title: Podcast: Donald Knuth: Programming, Algorithms, Hard Problems & the Game of Life | Lex Fridman Podcast #219

body.input: educational institutions to fall into credentialism versus inspirationalism.

metadata.title: Podcast: Donald Knuth: Programming, Algorithms, Hard Problems & the Game of Life | Lex Fridman Podcast #219

body.input: I don't know if those are words, but sort of understanding versus just giving a little

metadata.title: Podcast: Donald Knuth: Programming, Algorithms, Hard Problems & the Game of Life | Lex Fridman Podcast #219

body.input: plaque. And it's pretty much like what we were talking about if you want the computer to,

metadata.title: Podcast: Donald Knuth: Programming, Algorithms, Hard Problems & the Game of Life | Lex Fridman Podcast #219

body.input: if you want to be able to believe the answer, a computer is doing that. One of the things

metadata.title: Podcast: Donald Knuth: Programming, Algorithms, Hard Problems & the Game of Life | Lex Fridman Podcast #219

body.input: Bob Floyd showed me in the 60s, he loved this cartoon. There were two guys standing in front of,

metadata.title: Podcast: Donald Knuth: Programming, Algorithms, Hard Problems & the Game of Life | Lex Fridman Podcast #219

body.input: in those days, a computer was a big thing. And the first guy says to the other guy, he said,

metadata.title: Podcast: Donald Knuth: Programming, Algorithms, Hard Problems & the Game of Life | Lex Fridman Podcast #219

body.input: this machine can do in one second what it would take a million people to do in a hundred years.

metadata.title: Podcast: Donald Knuth: Programming, Algorithms, Hard Problems & the Game of Life | Lex Fridman Podcast #219

body.input: And the other guy says, oh, so how do you know it's right?

metadata.title: Podcast: Donald Knuth: Programming, Algorithms, Hard Problems & the Game of Life | Lex Fridman Podcast #219

body.input: That's a good line. Is there some interesting distinction between physics and math to you?

metadata.title: Podcast: Donald Knuth: Programming, Algorithms, Hard Problems & the Game of Life | Lex Fridman Podcast #219

body.input: Have you looked at physics much to like speaking of Richard Feynman? So the difference between

metadata.title: Podcast: Donald Knuth: Programming, Algorithms, Hard Problems & the Game of Life | Lex Fridman Podcast #219

body.input: the physics community, the physics way of thinking, the physics intuition versus the computer science,

metadata.title: Podcast: Donald Knuth: Programming, Algorithms, Hard Problems & the Game of Life | Lex Fridman Podcast #219

body.input: the theoretical computer science, the mathematical sciences, do you see that as a gap? Are they

metadata.title: Podcast: Donald Knuth: Programming, Algorithms, Hard Problems & the Game of Life | Lex Fridman Podcast #219

body.input: strongly overlapping? It's quite different in my opinion. I started as a physics major and I

metadata.title: Podcast: Donald Knuth: Programming, Algorithms, Hard Problems & the Game of Life | Lex Fridman Podcast #219

body.input: switched into math. And probably the reason was that I could get A plus on the physics exam, but

metadata.title: Podcast: Donald Knuth: Programming, Algorithms, Hard Problems & the Game of Life | Lex Fridman Podcast #219

body.input: I never had any idea why I would have been able to come up with the problems that were on those

metadata.title: Podcast: Donald Knuth: Programming, Algorithms, Hard Problems & the Game of Life | Lex Fridman Podcast #219

body.input: exams. But in math, I knew why the teacher set those problems and I thought of other problems

metadata.title: Podcast: Donald Knuth: Programming, Algorithms, Hard Problems & the Game of Life | Lex Fridman Podcast #219

body.input: that I could set too. And I believe it's quite a different mentality.

metadata.title: Podcast: Donald Knuth: Programming, Algorithms, Hard Problems & the Game of Life | Lex Fridman Podcast #219

body.input: It has to do with your philosophy of geekdom?

metadata.title: Podcast: Donald Knuth: Programming, Algorithms, Hard Problems & the Game of Life | Lex Fridman Podcast #219

body.input: Some of my computer scientists friends are really good at physics and others are not.

metadata.title: Podcast: Donald Knuth: Programming, Algorithms, Hard Problems & the Game of Life | Lex Fridman Podcast #219

body.input: And I'm really good at algebra, but not at geometry. Talk about different parts of mathematics.

metadata.title: Podcast: Donald Knuth: Programming, Algorithms, Hard Problems & the Game of Life | Lex Fridman Podcast #219

body.input: So they're different kinds of physics, but physicists think of things in terms of waves.

metadata.title: Podcast: Donald Knuth: Programming, Algorithms, Hard Problems & the Game of Life | Lex Fridman Podcast #219

body.input: And I can think of things in terms of waves, but it's like a dog walking on hind legs if I'm thinking about it.

metadata.title: Podcast: Donald Knuth: Programming, Algorithms, Hard Problems & the Game of Life | Lex Fridman Podcast #219

body.input: So you basically like to see the world in discrete ways and then physics is more continuous?

metadata.title: Podcast: Donald Knuth: Programming, Algorithms, Hard Problems & the Game of Life | Lex Fridman Podcast #219

body.input: Yeah, I'm not sure if Turing would have been a great physicist.

metadata.title: Podcast: Donald Knuth: Programming, Algorithms, Hard Problems & the Game of Life | Lex Fridman Podcast #219

body.input: I think it was a pretty good chemist, but I don't know. But anyway, I see things.

metadata.title: Podcast: Donald Knuth: Programming, Algorithms, Hard Problems & the Game of Life | Lex Fridman Podcast #219

body.input: I believe that computer science is largely driven by people who have brains who are good at

metadata.title: Podcast: Donald Knuth: Programming, Algorithms, Hard Problems & the Game of Life | Lex Fridman Podcast #219

body.input: resonating with certain kind of concepts. And quantum computers takes a different kind of brain.

metadata.title: Podcast: Donald Knuth: Programming, Algorithms, Hard Problems & the Game of Life | Lex Fridman Podcast #219

body.input: Yeah, that's interesting. Yeah. Well, quantum computers is almost like at the intersection

metadata.title: Podcast: Donald Knuth: Programming, Algorithms, Hard Problems & the Game of Life | Lex Fridman Podcast #219

body.input: in terms of brain between computer science and physics because it involves both at least at this time.

metadata.title: Podcast: Donald Knuth: Programming, Algorithms, Hard Problems & the Game of Life | Lex Fridman Podcast #219

body.input: But there is like the physicists I've known, they have incredibly powerful intuition.

metadata.title: Podcast: Donald Knuth: Programming, Algorithms, Hard Problems & the Game of Life | Lex Fridman Podcast #219

body.input: And I mean, statistical mechanics. So I study statistical mechanics.

metadata.title: Podcast: Donald Knuth: Programming, Algorithms, Hard Problems & the Game of Life | Lex Fridman Podcast #219

body.input: I mean, random processes are related to algorithms in a lot of ways.

metadata.title: Podcast: Donald Knuth: Programming, Algorithms, Hard Problems & the Game of Life | Lex Fridman Podcast #219

body.input: But there are lots of different flavors of physics as there are different flavors of mathematics as well.

metadata.title: Podcast: Donald Knuth: Programming, Algorithms, Hard Problems & the Game of Life | Lex Fridman Podcast #219

body.input: But the thing is that I don't see, well, actually when they talk to physicists,

metadata.title: Podcast: Donald Knuth: Programming, Algorithms, Hard Problems & the Game of Life | Lex Fridman Podcast #219

body.input: use a completely different language than when they're talking to, when they're writing expository papers.

metadata.title: Podcast: Donald Knuth: Programming, Algorithms, Hard Problems & the Game of Life | Lex Fridman Podcast #219

body.input: And so I didn't understand quantum mechanics at all from reading about it in Scientific American.

metadata.title: Podcast: Donald Knuth: Programming, Algorithms, Hard Problems & the Game of Life | Lex Fridman Podcast #219

body.input: But when I read how they describe it to each other talking about eigenvalues and various things,

metadata.title: Podcast: Donald Knuth: Programming, Algorithms, Hard Problems & the Game of Life | Lex Fridman Podcast #219

body.input: and various mathematical terms that made sense, then it made sense to me.

metadata.title: Podcast: Donald Knuth: Programming, Algorithms, Hard Problems & the Game of Life | Lex Fridman Podcast #219

body.input: But Hawking said that every formula you put in a book, you lose half of your readers.

metadata.title: Podcast: Donald Knuth: Programming, Algorithms, Hard Problems & the Game of Life | Lex Fridman Podcast #219

body.input: And so he didn't put any formulas in the book. So I couldn't understand his book at all.

metadata.title: Podcast: Donald Knuth: Programming, Algorithms, Hard Problems & the Game of Life | Lex Fridman Podcast #219

body.input: You could say you understood it, but I really didn't.

metadata.title: Podcast: Donald Knuth: Programming, Algorithms, Hard Problems & the Game of Life | Lex Fridman Podcast #219

body.input: Well, Feynman also spoke in this way. So Feynman, I think, prided himself on really strong intuition.

metadata.title: Podcast: Donald Knuth: Programming, Algorithms, Hard Problems & the Game of Life | Lex Fridman Podcast #219

body.input: But at the same time, he was hiding all the really good, the deep computation he was doing.

metadata.title: Podcast: Donald Knuth: Programming, Algorithms, Hard Problems & the Game of Life | Lex Fridman Podcast #219

body.input: So there was one thing that I was never able to, I wish I had had more time to work out with him,

metadata.title: Podcast: Donald Knuth: Programming, Algorithms, Hard Problems & the Game of Life | Lex Fridman Podcast #219

body.input: but I guess I could describe it for you. There's something that got my name attached to it called

metadata.title: Podcast: Donald Knuth: Programming, Algorithms, Hard Problems & the Game of Life | Lex Fridman Podcast #219

body.input: Knuth-Arrow notation. But it's a notation for very large numbers. And so I find out that somebody

metadata.title: Podcast: Donald Knuth: Programming, Algorithms, Hard Problems & the Game of Life | Lex Fridman Podcast #219

body.input: invented it in the 1830s. It's fairly easy to understand anyway. So you start with x plus x

metadata.title: Podcast: Donald Knuth: Programming, Algorithms, Hard Problems & the Game of Life | Lex Fridman Podcast #219

body.input: plus x plus x n times, and you can call that xn. So xn is multiplication. Then you take x times x

metadata.title: Podcast: Donald Knuth: Programming, Algorithms, Hard Problems & the Game of Life | Lex Fridman Podcast #219

body.input: times x times xn times, that gives you exponentiation, x to the nth power.

metadata.title: Podcast: Donald Knuth: Programming, Algorithms, Hard Problems & the Game of Life | Lex Fridman Podcast #219

body.input: So that's one arrow. So xn with no arrows is multiplication. X arrow n is x to the nth power.

metadata.title: Podcast: Donald Knuth: Programming, Algorithms, Hard Problems & the Game of Life | Lex Fridman Podcast #219

body.input: Yeah, so just to clarify for the... So x times x times xn times is obviously xn.

metadata.title: Podcast: Donald Knuth: Programming, Algorithms, Hard Problems & the Game of Life | Lex Fridman Podcast #219

body.input: X plus x plus xn times.

metadata.title: Podcast: Donald Knuth: Programming, Algorithms, Hard Problems & the Game of Life | Lex Fridman Podcast #219

body.input: Yeah, okay. And then...

metadata.title: Podcast: Donald Knuth: Programming, Algorithms, Hard Problems & the Game of Life | Lex Fridman Podcast #219

body.input: Xn, no arrow.

metadata.title: Podcast: Donald Knuth: Programming, Algorithms, Hard Problems & the Game of Life | Lex Fridman Podcast #219

body.input: And then multiplication is x to the n. And then here the arrow is when you're

metadata.title: Podcast: Donald Knuth: Programming, Algorithms, Hard Problems & the Game of Life | Lex Fridman Podcast #219

body.input: doing the same kind of repetitive operation for the exponential.

metadata.title: Podcast: Donald Knuth: Programming, Algorithms, Hard Problems & the Game of Life | Lex Fridman Podcast #219

body.input: So I put in one arrow and I get x to the nth power. Now I put in two arrows,

metadata.title: Podcast: Donald Knuth: Programming, Algorithms, Hard Problems & the Game of Life | Lex Fridman Podcast #219

body.input: and that takes x to the x to the x to the x to the xn times power. So in other words,

metadata.title: Podcast: Donald Knuth: Programming, Algorithms, Hard Problems & the Game of Life | Lex Fridman Podcast #219

body.input: if it's two double arrow, three, that would be two to the two to the two.

metadata.title: Podcast: Donald Knuth: Programming, Algorithms, Hard Problems & the Game of Life | Lex Fridman Podcast #219

body.input: So that would be two to the fourth power. That'd be 16, okay.

metadata.title: Podcast: Donald Knuth: Programming, Algorithms, Hard Problems & the Game of Life | Lex Fridman Podcast #219

body.input: Okay. So that's the double arrow. And now you can do with triple arrow, of course, and so on.

metadata.title: Podcast: Donald Knuth: Programming, Algorithms, Hard Problems & the Game of Life | Lex Fridman Podcast #219

body.input: And I had this paper called, well, essentially big numbers. You try to impress your friend,

metadata.title: Podcast: Donald Knuth: Programming, Algorithms, Hard Problems & the Game of Life | Lex Fridman Podcast #219

body.input: but by saying a number they've never thought of before. And I gave a special name

metadata.title: Podcast: Donald Knuth: Programming, Algorithms, Hard Problems & the Game of Life | Lex Fridman Podcast #219

body.input: for it and designed a font for it that has script k and so on. But it really is 10,

metadata.title: Podcast: Donald Knuth: Programming, Algorithms, Hard Problems & the Game of Life | Lex Fridman Podcast #219

body.input: I think like 10 quadruple arrow three, or something like that. And I claimed that that number

metadata.title: Podcast: Donald Knuth: Programming, Algorithms, Hard Problems & the Game of Life | Lex Fridman Podcast #219

body.input: is so mind boggling that you can't comprehend how large it is. But anyway, Feynman,

metadata.title: Podcast: Donald Knuth: Programming, Algorithms, Hard Problems & the Game of Life | Lex Fridman Podcast #219

body.input: I talked to Feynman about this and he said, oh, let's just use double arrow. But instead

metadata.title: Podcast: Donald Knuth: Programming, Algorithms, Hard Problems & the Game of Life | Lex Fridman Podcast #219

body.input: of taking integers, let's consider complex numbers. I mean, okay, x arrow arrow two,

metadata.title: Podcast: Donald Knuth: Programming, Algorithms, Hard Problems & the Game of Life | Lex Fridman Podcast #219

body.input: that means x to the x. But what about x double arrow 2.5? Well, that's not too hard to figure out.

metadata.title: Podcast: Donald Knuth: Programming, Algorithms, Hard Problems & the Game of Life | Lex Fridman Podcast #219

body.input: That's interpolate between those. But what about x double arrow i or one plus i or some complex number?

metadata.title: Podcast: Donald Knuth: Programming, Algorithms, Hard Problems & the Game of Life | Lex Fridman Podcast #219

body.input: So he claimed that there was no analytic function that would do the job.

metadata.title: Podcast: Donald Knuth: Programming, Algorithms, Hard Problems & the Game of Life | Lex Fridman Podcast #219

body.input: But I didn't know how he could claim that that wasn't true.

metadata.title: Podcast: Donald Knuth: Programming, Algorithms, Hard Problems & the Game of Life | Lex Fridman Podcast #219

body.input: And his next question was, did it then have a complex number of arrows?

metadata.title: Podcast: Donald Knuth: Programming, Algorithms, Hard Problems & the Game of Life | Lex Fridman Podcast #219

body.input: Wow. Okay.

metadata.title: Podcast: Donald Knuth: Programming, Algorithms, Hard Problems & the Game of Life | Lex Fridman Podcast #219

body.input: Okay. So that's Feynman.

metadata.title: Podcast: Donald Knuth: Programming, Algorithms, Hard Problems & the Game of Life | Lex Fridman Podcast #219

body.input: Can you describe what the Knuth-Morris-Pratt algorithm does? And how did you come to develop

metadata.title: Podcast: Donald Knuth: Programming, Algorithms, Hard Problems & the Game of Life | Lex Fridman Podcast #219

body.input: it? One of the many things that you're known for and has your name attached to it?

metadata.title: Podcast: Donald Knuth: Programming, Algorithms, Hard Problems & the Game of Life | Lex Fridman Podcast #219

body.input: Yeah. All right. So it should be actually Morris-Pratt-Knuth.

metadata.title: Podcast: Donald Knuth: Programming, Algorithms, Hard Problems & the Game of Life | Lex Fridman Podcast #219

body.input: But we decided to use alphabetical order when we published the paper.

metadata.title: Podcast: Donald Knuth: Programming, Algorithms, Hard Problems & the Game of Life | Lex Fridman Podcast #219

body.input: The problem is something that everybody knows now if they're using a search engine.

metadata.title: Podcast: Donald Knuth: Programming, Algorithms, Hard Problems & the Game of Life | Lex Fridman Podcast #219

body.input: You have a large collection of text and you want to know if the word Knuth appears anywhere in the

metadata.title: Podcast: Donald Knuth: Programming, Algorithms, Hard Problems & the Game of Life | Lex Fridman Podcast #219

body.input: text, or some other word that's less interesting than Knuth.

metadata.title: Podcast: Donald Knuth: Programming, Algorithms, Hard Problems & the Game of Life | Lex Fridman Podcast #219

body.input: That's the most interesting word.

metadata.title: Podcast: Donald Knuth: Programming, Algorithms, Hard Problems & the Game of Life | Lex Fridman Podcast #219

body.input: Like Morris or something.

metadata.title: Podcast: Donald Knuth: Programming, Algorithms, Hard Problems & the Game of Life | Lex Fridman Podcast #219

body.input: Like Morris, right.

metadata.title: Podcast: Donald Knuth: Programming, Algorithms, Hard Problems & the Game of Life | Lex Fridman Podcast #219

body.input: So we have a large piece of text and it's all one long one-dimensional thing. First letter,

metadata.title: Podcast: Donald Knuth: Programming, Algorithms, Hard Problems & the Game of Life | Lex Fridman Podcast #219

body.input: second letter, etc. And so we'd like to be able to do this quickly. And the obvious way is,

metadata.title: Podcast: Donald Knuth: Programming, Algorithms, Hard Problems & the Game of Life | Lex Fridman Podcast #219

body.input: let's say we're looking for Morris. So we would go through and wait till we get to letter M.

metadata.title: Podcast: Donald Knuth: Programming, Algorithms, Hard Problems & the Game of Life | Lex Fridman Podcast #219

body.input: Then we look at the next word and sure enough it's an O and then an R. But then, too bad,

metadata.title: Podcast: Donald Knuth: Programming, Algorithms, Hard Problems & the Game of Life | Lex Fridman Podcast #219

body.input: the next letter is E. So we missed out on Morris. And so we go back and start looking for another.

metadata.title: Podcast: Donald Knuth: Programming, Algorithms, Hard Problems & the Game of Life | Lex Fridman Podcast #219

body.input: All over again.

metadata.title: Podcast: Donald Knuth: Programming, Algorithms, Hard Problems & the Game of Life | Lex Fridman Podcast #219

body.input: So that's the obvious way to do it. And Jim Morris noticed there was a more clever way

metadata.title: Podcast: Donald Knuth: Programming, Algorithms, Hard Problems & the Game of Life | Lex Fridman Podcast #219

body.input: to do it. The obvious way would have started, let's say we found that letter M at character

metadata.title: Podcast: Donald Knuth: Programming, Algorithms, Hard Problems & the Game of Life | Lex Fridman Podcast #219

body.input: position 1000. Started next at character position 1001. But he said, no, look, we already read the

metadata.title: Podcast: Donald Knuth: Programming, Algorithms, Hard Problems & the Game of Life | Lex Fridman Podcast #219

body.input: O and the R and we know that they aren't M's. So we can start, we don't have to read those

metadata.title: Podcast: Donald Knuth: Programming, Algorithms, Hard Problems & the Game of Life | Lex Fridman Podcast #219

body.input: over again. And this gets pretty tricky when the word isn't Morris, but it's more like

metadata.title: Podcast: Donald Knuth: Programming, Algorithms, Hard Problems & the Game of Life | Lex Fridman Podcast #219

body.input: abracadabra where you have patterns that are occurring.

metadata.title: Podcast: Donald Knuth: Programming, Algorithms, Hard Problems & the Game of Life | Lex Fridman Podcast #219

body.input: Like repeating patterns. At the beginning, at the middle.

metadata.title: Podcast: Donald Knuth: Programming, Algorithms, Hard Problems & the Game of Life | Lex Fridman Podcast #219

body.input: Right. So he worked it out and he put it into the system software at Berkeley, I think it was,

metadata.title: Podcast: Donald Knuth: Programming, Algorithms, Hard Problems & the Game of Life | Lex Fridman Podcast #219

body.input: where he was writing some Berkeley Unix, I think it was some routine that was supposed to find

metadata.title: Podcast: Donald Knuth: Programming, Algorithms, Hard Problems & the Game of Life | Lex Fridman Podcast #219

body.input: occurrences of patterns in text. And we didn't explain it. And so he found out that several

metadata.title: Podcast: Donald Knuth: Programming, Algorithms, Hard Problems & the Game of Life | Lex Fridman Podcast #219

body.input: months later, somebody had looked at it, didn't look right. And so they ripped it out.

metadata.title: Podcast: Donald Knuth: Programming, Algorithms, Hard Problems & the Game of Life | Lex Fridman Podcast #219

body.input: So he had this algorithm, but it didn't make it through because it wasn't understood.

metadata.title: Podcast: Donald Knuth: Programming, Algorithms, Hard Problems & the Game of Life | Lex Fridman Podcast #219

body.input: Nobody knew about this particularly. Von Pratt also had independently discovered it a year or two later.

metadata.title: Podcast: Donald Knuth: Programming, Algorithms, Hard Problems & the Game of Life | Lex Fridman Podcast #219

body.input: I forget why. I think Von was studying some technical problem

metadata.title: Podcast: Donald Knuth: Programming, Algorithms, Hard Problems & the Game of Life | Lex Fridman Podcast #219

body.input: about palindromes or something like that. He wasn't really, Von wasn't working on

metadata.title: Podcast: Donald Knuth: Programming, Algorithms, Hard Problems & the Game of Life | Lex Fridman Podcast #219

body.input: text searching, but he was working on an abstract problem that was related.

metadata.title: Podcast: Donald Knuth: Programming, Algorithms, Hard Problems & the Game of Life | Lex Fridman Podcast #219

body.input: Well, at that time, Steve Cook was a professor at Berkeley. And it was the greatest mistake that

metadata.title: Podcast: Donald Knuth: Programming, Algorithms, Hard Problems & the Game of Life | Lex Fridman Podcast #219

body.input: Berkeley CS department made was not to give him tenure. So Steve went to Toronto.

metadata.title: Podcast: Donald Knuth: Programming, Algorithms, Hard Problems & the Game of Life | Lex Fridman Podcast #219

body.input: But I knew Steve while he was at Berkeley, and he had come up with a very peculiar theorem

metadata.title: Podcast: Donald Knuth: Programming, Algorithms, Hard Problems & the Game of Life | Lex Fridman Podcast #219

body.input: about a technical concept called a stack automaton. And a stack automaton is a machine that

metadata.title: Podcast: Donald Knuth: Programming, Algorithms, Hard Problems & the Game of Life | Lex Fridman Podcast #219

body.input: can't do everything a Turing machine can do, but it can only look at something at the top of a stack

metadata.title: Podcast: Donald Knuth: Programming, Algorithms, Hard Problems & the Game of Life | Lex Fridman Podcast #219

body.input: or it can put more things on the stack or it can take things off the stack. It can't remember

metadata.title: Podcast: Donald Knuth: Programming, Algorithms, Hard Problems & the Game of Life | Lex Fridman Podcast #219

body.input: a long string of symbols, but it can remember them in reverse order. So if you tell a stack automaton
